Position: Finance Assistant (Consultant) – Nepal Emergency Response

Location: Nepal

Project HOPE is an international NGO with more than 1,000 engaged employees and volunteers who work around the globe, responding to the world’s most pressing global health challenges. Throughout our 60-year legacy, Project HOPE has treated millions of patients, provided more than $3 billion worth of medicines to local health care organizations around the world helped build hundreds of health programs from the ground up, and responded to humanitarian crises worldwide.

Code of Conduct

It is our shared responsibility and obligation to treat each other with respect, take affirmative steps to prevent matters involving Sexual Exploitation & Abuse and Trafficking in Persons, and to disclose all potential and actual violations of our Code of Conduct, which may include Conflicts of Interest, Fraud, Corruption, Discrimination or Harassment. Together we can reinforce a culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and transparency.

Summary:

Project HOPE is seeking a Finance Assistant Consultant to provide administrative and financial support to its emergency response activities in Nepal. The consultant will support financial operations, including financial documentation, payment processing, petty cash tracking, transaction recording, reconciliations, and financial reporting while ensuring compliance with Project HOPE procedures, donor requirements, and applicable Nepal statutory requirements in a humanitarian operating environment.

In carrying out the scope of work, the consultant will coordinate, as needed, with the Finance Officer, relevant Project HOPE teams, vendors, and other stakeholders.

Purpose:

The purpose of this consultancy is to provide additional finance capacity to support Project HOPE’s Nepal emergency response and facilitate timely, accurate, and well-documented financial operations during the consultant assignment period.

Scope of Consultancy

The consultant will provide services in the following areas:

Financial Operations

  • Support recording and maintenance of financial transactions in the accounting system.
  • Review financial documentation for completeness, accuracy, and appropriate approvals.
  • Support payment processing, including vendor and consultant payments, advances, and other approved payments.
  • Prepare payment requests, advance clearances, and related supporting documentation.
  • Support month-end financial close activities and account reconciliations.

Cash and Financial Records

  • Support petty cash administration, documentation, tracking, and reconciliation.
  • Maintain payment, advance, contract, and other finance tracking records.
  • Ensure financial documents are properly organized, scanned, filed and archived.
  • Support preparation of weekly cash reports and monthly cash requests.

Compliance and Reporting

  • Review supporting documentation for procurement, travel, advances, and expenses to ensure compliance with Project HOPE and donor requirements.
  • Support preparation and processing of personnel-related payments, as applicable and as directed by the Finance Officer.
  • Assist with internal and donor financial reporting.
  • Support finance documentation and processes required under applicable Nepal laws and requirements, as directed.

Coordination

  • Coordinate with the Finance Officer, Nepal program and operations teams, vendors, implementing partners, and Project HOPE HQ Finance as appropriate.
  • Provide regular updates on finance activities, outstanding items, and issues requiring follow-up.

EXPECTED OUTPUTS

During the consultancy period, the consultant is expected to contribute to:

  • Timely and accurate recording of financial transactions.
  • Complete and properly maintained financial documentation and records.
  • Timely processing and tracking of payments, advances, and other approved financial obligations.
  • Accurate petty cash and cash management records and reconciliations.
  • Timely completion of monthly financial close activities and related reporting support.
  • Regular coordination and follow-up with Nepal and HQ Finance teams.
  • Detailed deliverables, timelines, and expectations will be outlined in the consultancy Statement of Work.

Duration of Assignment: Approximately 3-6 months

MINIMUM QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Diploma or Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, Business Administration, or related field.
  • Minimum 1–3 years of relevant experience in finance or administrative support, preferably in NGO, INGO, or humanitarian settings in Nepal.
  • Basic understanding of accounting, financial documentation, payment processing, and petty cash management.
  • Familiarity with applicable Nepal finance, tax, and statutory documentation requirements is preferred.
  • Experience supporting procurement documentation, vendor payments, cash advances, and reconciliations is desirable.
  • Strong attention to detail and demonstrated ability to maintain accurate financial documentation and records.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities, and meet deadlines in an emergency response environment.
  • Strong communication and coordination skills, including the ability to work effectively with field teams, vendors, financial institutions, and implementing partners.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Excel and Word and familiarity with electronic financial or accounting systems; NetSuite experience is desirable.
  • Fluency in Nepali and working proficiency in English are required.
  • The consultancy fee will be determined based on the scope of services, qualifications, and experience of the selected consultant.

Notice to applicants: Project HOPE does not conduct direct solicitation/recruitment via email. Project HOPE never asks consultant applicants for payment or financial information at any stage of the recruitment process. Project HOPE will never send you a third-party check and ask you to cash it. If you have been recruited via email, please contact Compliance@projecthope.org

Due to the substantial number of inquiries we receive, only those who meet the required qualifications and experience for this consultancy will be contacted. No phone calls please. However, since we are active around the world in the field of public health, we may wish to retain your CV in our database for other/future opportunities, unless you direct us otherwise.

Thank you very much for your interest in Project HOPE.

Employee Contract Type: Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

World Vision International Nepal (WVI Nepal) has launched a Category II Emergency Response in the districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot, Bagmati Province, following devastating flash floods along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors that caused casualties, displacement and extensive damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The 12-month Nepal Flash Flood Response (NFFR) 2026 plan which is funded by several donors targets 25,000 people, including 10,000 children, from around 5,000 affected households across seven sectors, moving from relief into early recovery. This position will also support health and nutrition activities in the other emergency response project funded by the US government (RISE project) focuses on moderate acute malnutrition in districts of Madhesh Province (Mahottari, Sarlahi and Rautahat).

This position has responsibility to lead the health and nutrition activities in the Nepal Flash Flood Response project and RISE project to respond to emergency needs and to functionalize health, nutrition and hygiene (WASH) interventions. The activities will take place in the emergency response locations (Rasuwa and Nuwakot) and in WVI Nepal’s development program areas (such as in Mahottari, Sarlahi and Rautahat districts). The role ensures technically sound programming of World Vision and partner NGOs in the areas of health, nutrition and the hygiene component of WASH. The role will also ensure the technical aspects are compliant with WVI Nepal’s standards, government policies, and humanitarian norms. Key Responsibilities include:

Monitoring partner NGOs’ health, nutrition and hygiene program quality and project delivery.
Providing technical and functional support for quality health, nutrition and hygiene programming.
Leading on emergency nutrition actions including IYCF-E, screening, management of MAM and referral of SAM cases, community mobilization, and integrated health and WASH interventions.
Coordinating with government authorities, UN agencies, INGOs, and cluster coordination mechanisms
Developing annual technical support plans and rolling out tools, benchmarks, and guidance for emergency contexts and in development contexts, where relevant.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Technical support in project implementation

  • Support the project and PNGO managers to implement health, nutrition and hygiene (related to WASH programming) planning, budgeting, implementation, monitoring, and support reporting to ensure achievement of agreed emergency response and DHR funded RISE project objectives, targets, and quality standards.
  • Provide overall technical leadership to the World Vision team and partner NGOs implementing nutrition interventions, including Positive Deviance (PD) Hearth,
  • Management of Moderate Acute Malnutrition (MAM) and referral support for severe acute malnutrition, maternal health and nutrition, and integrated WASH activities.
  • Ensure timely and quality implementation of emergency nutrition interventions, including community screening, identification and referral of SAM and MAM cases, growth monitoring, child vaccination support, and hygiene interventions.
  • Conduct community awareness sessions on personal, household, and environmental hygiene. Educate community members on proper handwashing with soap at critical times, including before eating and after using the toilet.
  • Promote safe water handling, treatment, storage, and consumption practices to prevent waterborne diseases.
  • Capacity development of health operations and management committees to functionalize health systems at local health facility level.
  • Conduct regular program reviews with partners to assess progress, address bottlenecks, and strengthen implementation quality.
  • Lead project start-up, transition, close-out, and sustainability planning processes together with partners.
  • Facilitate integration of Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) principles throughout project planning, implementation, monitoring, and evaluation.

Emergency Preparedness and Response

  • Provide technical leadership and coordination for emergency health and nutrition responses, including floods, earthquakes, disease outbreaks, and other humanitarian emergencies.
  • Lead rapid needs assessments for health and nutrition and support emergency response planning, implementation, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Ensure implementation of emergency nutrition interventions, including IYCF-E, acute malnutrition screening and referral, micronutrient support, and hygiene activities.
  • Support emergency health response activities, including disease surveillance, rapid health assessments, referral of vulnerable cases, and coordination with health facilities to ensure timely access to essential health services.
  • Conduct community outreach and health awareness sessions on disease prevention, hygiene promotion, safe water practices, outbreak preparedness, and emergency health measures during disasters and public health emergencies.
  • Coordinate with government and humanitarian partners on emergency health, nutrition, vaccination, WASH, and health and nutrition related risk communication and community engagement activities.
  • Monitor public health and nutrition risks and support preparedness and response measures during emergencies.
  • Ensure integration of nutrition, health, WASH, with other sectors such as protection, and integrate psychosocial considerations within emergency responses.

Information Management and Learning

  • Ensure accurate, timely, and real-time collection, analysis, and reporting of nutrition-related data, including SAM/MAM caseloads, maternal nutrition indicators, and maternal, newborn, child health and nutrition service coverage.
  • Health and hygiene information management – timely information sharing on possible disease outbreaks and prepared mitigation measures as per the context.
  • Support the design and implementation of digital and paper-based monitoring systems that improve data quality and decision-making.
  • Collaborate closely with the MEAL team to roll out emergency information management systems such as SORMAS, 5Ws reporting, and other donor-required reporting mechanisms.
  • Conduct routine data verification, validation, and quality assurance exercises to ensure accuracy and reliability of program information.
  • Generate periodic analytical reports highlighting program achievements, gaps, trends, and recommendations for management decision-making.
  • Document and disseminate case studies, success stories, lessons learned, and best practices from both non-emergency health, nutrition and hygiene programming and emergency flood response interventions
  • Support the project managers to maintain proper program documentation and information management systems in compliance with organizational policies.

Capacity Strengthening and Technical Support

  • Assess technical and operational capacity gaps related to health, nutrition and hygiene related to WASH among partner staff and develop capacity-strengthening plans.
  • Provide technical guidance, coaching, mentoring, and supportive supervision to WVI Nepal staff, partners staff and government staff to improve program quality and effectiveness.
  • Strengthen partner capacity on key nutrition interventions, including:
  • Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) and IYCF in Emergencies (IYCF-E) practices (e.g. Exclusive breastfeeding promotion and support, complementary feeding for children aged 6-23 months).
  • Community-based management and referral of acute malnutrition.
  • Maternal nutrition interventions.
  • Super Cereal distribution and monitoring.
  • Support establishment and quality functioning of IYCF corners in shelters, temporary settlements, health facilities, and communities.
  • Strengthening community mobilization, behaviour change communication, and nutrition awareness initiatives in communities and schools.
  • Strengthening partner capacity on key health and hygiene interventions, including:
  • Community-based disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness and response.
  • Hygiene promotion, handwashing practices, and risk communication and community engagement.
  • Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) measures in community and health facility settings.
  • Maternal, newborn, and child health (MNCH) awareness and referral mechanisms.
  • Promote integration of GESI, disability inclusion, safeguarding, protection, and environmental sustainability across partner program.

Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning

  • Conduct regular field monitoring visits to assess programme quality, effectiveness, compliance, and beneficiary satisfaction.
  • Monitor project performance against approved indicators, benchmarks, work plans, and donor commitments.
  • Verify program data through spot checks, field observations, and review of partner reporting systems.
  • Work closely with the MEAL team to strengthen community feedback and accountability mechanisms and ensure appropriate response to beneficiary concerns.
  • Monitor coverage and quality of nutrition, health, and WASH services at community and facility levels.
  • Support evaluations, assessments, operational research, surveys, and learning reviews to enhance programme effectiveness.
  • Promote utilization of monitoring and learning findings for adaptive program management.

Risk Management & Compliance

  • Identify, assess, and monitor program risks related to public health emergencies, disease outbreaks, operational challenges, supply chains, and service delivery.
  • Develop and implement risk mitigation and contingency plans related to health, nutrition and hygiene programming in collaboration with partner NGOs, local authorities, and relevant stakeholders.
  • Ensure compliance with World Vision International policies, donor regulations, government guidelines, and humanitarian principles through engagement with partner NGOs and project visits.
  • Support partners in maintaining adequate documentation and evidence required for audits, donor reviews, and compliance assessments.
  • Strengthen accountability, transparency, safeguarding, and ethical practices throughout program implementation.

External Engagement and Coordination

  • Build and maintain productive relationships with provincial and local governments, UN agencies, INGOs, NGOs, and other stakeholders.
  • Represent World Vision International Nepal in nutrition, health, WASH, and emergency coordination forums at local and provincial levels.
  • Participate in relevant technical working groups, clusters, task forces, and coordination mechanisms.
  • Advocate for improved access to quality nutrition and health services for vulnerable populations.
  • Strengthening collaboration, information sharing, and joint planning among partners to enhance program effectiveness and avoid duplication.
  • Contributes to increased visibility, communication efforts and donor engagement by showcasing program achievements, impact, and learning.

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

  • A 2-3 years proven record of health and nutrition experience working both in emergency and in development program

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health, Nutrition, Nursing, or in the fields suitable for development.

Essential Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Knowledge of development and humanitarian industry.
  • Writing quality reports.
  • Data management.
  • Demonstrate collaboration & team building skills.
  • Effective relationship management skills; ability to influence without having authority.
  • Strong oral and written English and Nepali communication skills.
  • Ability to structure and manage one’s own work.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Cross-functional management experience in an I/NGO, UN/ bilateral organizational environment
  • Knowledge and experience of humanitarian response action in Nepal
  • Perform other organizational and business processes that are required to contribute to WVIN’s strategic objectives and to maintain a healthy organizational life
  • Demonstrate understanding of and commitment to World Vision’s Core Values in the approach to work and relationships

Job Title: Education Specialist – Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL)
Department: Programme
Reports To: Senior Programme Manager
Location: Kathmandu with frequent travel to UWS Nepal programme districts

About UWS Nepal

United World Schools (UWS) Nepal is committed to ensuring that every child has access to quality education and acquires foundational skills required for lifelong learning. UWS Nepal collaborates closely with schools, communities, local governments and education stakeholders to improve educational quality, equity and learning outcomes through Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (FLN), Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL), teacher professional development, instructional leadership, school improvement and education system strengthening initiatives.

Purpose of the Position

The Education Specialist – TaRL will serve as the lead technical resource for the design, implementation, quality assurance and continuous improvement of UWS Nepal’s TaRL approach. The position will support programmes that assess children’s current learning levels, group learners according to ability rather than grade, deliver targeted literacy and numeracy instruction, and use regular assessment data to improve learning outcomes.
The post holder will bring specialist expertise in foundational learning, TaRL methodology, remedial instruction, simple learning assessment, teacher coaching, mentoring, instructional leadership, programme quality improvement and Nepal’s education system.

Key Responsibilities

1. Technical Leadership in TaRL (30%)

  •  Lead the design, contextualisation, implementation and continuous improvement of UWS Nepal’s TaRL approach for foundational literacy and numeracy.
  • Provide technical leadership and guidance to programme teams to ensure TaRL implementation is simple, evidence-informed, child-centred and focused on measurable learning gains.
  •  Develop and refine TaRL tools, routines and teaching-learning activities that strengthen children’s basic reading, comprehension, number sense, arithmetic and problem solving skills.
  •  Ensure TaRL interventions are aligned with national priorities, local government plans, global evidence and UWS education quality frameworks.
  •  Contribute to organisational TaRL strategies, foundational learning frameworks, technical standards and scale-up plans.

 TaRL Pedagogy, Grouping and Learning Improvement (20%)

  •  Provide technical expertise on TaRL pedagogy, level-based grouping, targeted instruction, competency-based learning, and effective classroom practice.
  •  Promote inclusive, child-centred and developmentally appropriate TaRL activities that respond to learners’ current skill levels.
  • Support learning camps, remedial cycles, differentiated instruction and level-wise progression so that children move from basic to more advanced learning groups.
  •  Strengthen classroom practices that use simple activities, peer learning, practice opportunities, and frequent checks for understanding to improve learning outcomes.

 Teacher Professional Development and Instructional Leadership (20%)

  • Design and facilitate TaRL-oriented professional development programmes for teachers, head teachers, education coordinators, mentors, and local education stakeholders.
  • Develop training packages, facilitator guides, practice-based coaching tools, simple assessment protocols and teaching-learning resources for TaRL delivery.
  •  Strengthen systems for TaRL-focused coaching, mentoring, classroom observation, feedback and continuous professional development.
  •  Support instructional leadership initiatives that enable head teachers and education officials to sustain TaRL practices and improve learning outcomes.

TaRL Assessment, Learning Data and Programme Quality (15%)

  • Lead the development and use of simple TaRL assessment tools to identify children’s current learning levels in reading and arithmetic.
  •  Support teachers and programme teams to group children by learning level, track progress regularly and adapt instruction based on assessment results.
  • Analyse TaRL assessment data to identify learning gaps, monitorlearner progression, and inform targeted programme improvements.
  •  Collaborate with programme and MEAL teams to integrate TaRL indicators, monitoring tools and quality assurance processes into programme systems.

Stakeholder Engagement, Knowledge Management and Representation (15%)

  • Serve as UWS Nepal’s technical focal point for TaRL and foundational learning.
  •  Build and maintain effective relationships with government stakeholders, municipalities, schools, development partners, and TaRL technical networks.
  •  Represent UWS Nepal in education forums, technical working groups and sector consultations related to TaRL, FLN and learning recovery.
  •  Document lessons learned, good practices and evidence from TaRL implementation to support programme learning, adaptation and scale-up.

Required Qualifications

Education

  • Master’s degree in Education, Curriculum Studies, Teacher Education, Educational Leadership, Educational Planning, Assessment and Evaluation, Child Development, Literacy, Mathematics Education or related field.
  •  Additional specialization or training in Teaching at the Right Level, FLN, remedial education, teacher professional development, learning assessment or instructional leadership is desirable.

Experience

  •  Minimum 5 years of progressively responsible experience in education programmes, with substantial experience in foundational learning or learning improvement initiatives.
  •  Significant experience in demonstrating foundational learning, TaRL, remedial education or similar level-based learning improvement programmes.
  •  Experience designing and facilitating teacher professional development programmes focused on TaRL, FLN, remedial pedagogy or classroom-based learning improvement.
  •  Experience in learner assessment, level-based grouping, targeted instruction, instructional coaching, and use of data for programme improvement.
  •  Experience working with government education systems, municipalities, schools, NGOs and development partners to implement, monitor or scale learning improvement programmes.

Essential Technical Competencies

TaRL and Foundational Learning

  •  Deep understanding of TaRL principles, foundational literacy and numeracy, and accelerated learning for children who are below grade-level expectations.
  • Level-based grouping, targeted instruction and child-centred TaRL classroom activities.
  •  Basic reading, comprehension, expression, number sense, arithmetic, reasoning and problem-solving.
  •  Simple assessment, learner grouping, progress tracking, and use of assessment data for instruction and course correction.
  • Learning camps, remedial cycles, and practical strategies for helping children progress quickly from their current learning level.

Child Learning, Inclusion and Education Quality

  •  Child development and learning theories.
  •  Early grade and primary education.
  •  Inclusive and child-centered education approaches.
  •  Foundational learning improvement through TaRL, remedial learning, and targeted instruction.
  •  Gender Equality, Disability, and Social Inclusion (GEDSI).

Knowledge of Nepal’s Education Sector, including

  •  School Education Sector Plan (SESP).
  • National Curriculum Framework and Basic Education Curriculum.
  • National Strategy for Foundational Learning and relevant TaRL, FLN and learning recovery initiatives.
  •  Teacher Professional Development Framework.
  •  Federal, provincial and local education governance structures.
  •  Functions of CEHRD, CDC, ERO, and local governments.

Teacher Professional Development and Instructional Leadership

  •  Adult learning principles.
  •  Teacher coaching and mentoring for TaRL classroom practice, learner grouping, and use of assessment data.
  • Classroom observation and feedback focused on TaRL routines, learner participation, and progress against learning levels.
  •  School improvement and instructional leadership.

Core Competencies

  •  Strategic Thinking
  •  Technical Leadership
  • Stakeholder Engagement and Influencing
  •  Results Orientation
  •  Planning and Organising
  • Commitment to Equity, Diversity and Inclusion

Safeguarding and Child Protection

The post holder will adhere to UWS Nepal’s Child Protection and Safeguarding Policies and ensure that all programme activities promote child safety, wellbeing, inclusion, dignity and rights. Compliance with safeguarding requirements is mandatory and will be assessed throughout the recruitment process.

Internship – Department of Health Determinants, Promotion and Prevention – (2603774)

Grade: No grade

Contractual Arrangement: Intern

Contract Duration (Years, Months, Days): 6 months

Closing Date : Sep 28, 2026,

Primary Location : Switzerland-Geneva

Organization : HQ/HPR Health Promotion HEP

Schedule : Full-time

IMPORTANT NOTICE: Please note that the deadline for receipt of applications indicated above reflects your personal device’s system settings.

OBJECTIVES OF THE PROGRAMME

The WHO Report on the Global Tobacco Epidemic (GTCR) is published every two years and for the last 18 years has successfully tracked the progress in tobacco control across all Member States. The next report, the eleventh in the series, will be published in 2027. The GTCR is one of WHO’s flagship publications and is supported by Bloomberg Philanthropies.

DESCRIPTION OF DUTIES

Under the supervision of a technical expert in the respective area, the intern is assigned the agreed terms of reference:

  • proofread and cross-check drafts and revisions
  • conduct an independent data validation on all analyses reported in the report
  • undertake web research and data collection on specific subject areas
  • organize and validate data and documents
  • assist in organizing the launch of the report
  • participate in on-going departmental projects

Learning objectives
The purpose of the WHO Internship Programme is to provide an enriching learning experience for students and recent graduates. The Learning Objectives outlined within each internship vacancy are a key component of the programme.

Within this internship, the intern will:

  • Understand the objectives of the programme/area of work
  • Communicate clearly about the programme/area of work
  • Understand the global status of tobacco control policies
  • Understand the role of monitoring policy progress in global health
  • Communicate clearly about the programme/area of work
  • Know how to assemble data and prepare a comprehensive analysis
  • Communicate clearly and effectively between stakeholders to ensure the production of a high-quality global report
  • Understand the difference of work between headquarters, regional offices and country offices

DURATION OF INTERNSHIP 

1 February 2027- 16 July 2027

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

Education

Have completed the equivalent of three years of full-time studies in a health or data-science related subject at a university or equivalent institution prior to commencing the assignment; AND be enrolled in a course of study at a university or equivalent institution leading to a formal qualification (applicants who have already graduated may also qualify for consideration provided that they apply to the internship within eighteen months after completion of their formal qualification).

Skills

Core competencies

  • Team work
  • Respecting and promoting individual and cultural differences
  • Communication

All interns should be able to demonstrate the following skills in line with the WHO core competencies:

  • Communicating effectively orally and in writing
  • Showing willingness to learn from mistakes
  • Producing and delivering quality results
  • Working collaboratively with team members

In addition, interns need to be familiar with commonly used computer programmes, such as Word, Excel, PowerPoint. Knowledge of specialized computer programmes, for example, statistical software may be an advantage.

Experience

  • Experience in research and/or in drafting reports
  • Experience in the subject area through academic work or research
  • Experience with data analysis, statistical packages and interest in the design of graphical display and analysis of health information in an international comparative perspective, such as for health system performance assessment
  • More specific experience such as specialized computer programmes

Languages

Essential: Expert knowledge of English.
Desirable: Intermediate knowledge of other UN language.

FINANCIAL SUPPORT

Interns do not receive a salary. They do however receive a living allowance. The amount of living allowance is different in each duty station. The amount also depends on any other external financial support received by the intern (grant, scholarships, etc.) and whether their permanent residence is in the duty station of the internship. In Geneva, for interns with permanent residence in the duty station, the maximum amount of the allowance provided by WHO is 739 CHF per month. For interns whose permanent residence is outside of the duty station, the maximum amount is 1680 CHF per month. The exact amount of the living allowance will be calculated for each intern, after selection, based on a legal financial disclosure form that the individual will complete. In addition, all interns in Geneva will receive  daily lunch vouchers for meal expenses (20 CHF per working day). WHO also provides all interns with accident and medical insurance coverage.


ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

  • Please note that internships at WHO are very competitive and only a small number of applicants will be accepted every year. Only candidates under serious consideration will be contacted.
  • Living abroad is expensive and finding accommodation can be challenging. All intern candidates should be aware of these factors before they consider applying for a WHO Internship.
  • If selected for a WHO Internship, candidates will be required to provide certified copies of proof of enrolment in an eligible course of studies, a completed WHO medical certificate of fitness for work, and the contact details for reference checks.
  • WHO only considers higher educational qualifications obtained from an institution accredited/recognized in the World Higher Education Database (WHED), a list updated by the International Association of Universities (IAU)/United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization (UNESCO). The list can be accessed through the link: http://www.whed.net. Some professional certificates may not appear in the WHED and will require individual review.
  • WHO prides itself on a workforce that adheres to the highest ethical and professional standards and that is committed to put the WHO Values Charter into practice.
  • WHO has zero tolerance towards sexual exploitation and abuse (SEA), sexual harassment and other types of abusive conduct (i.e., discrimination, abuse of authority and harassment). All members of the WHO workforce have a role to play in promoting a safe and respectful workplace and should report to WHO any actual or suspected cases of SEA, sexual harassment and other types of abusive conduct. To ensure that individuals with a substantiated history of SEA, sexual harassment or other types of abusive conduct are not hired by the Organization, WHO will conduct a background verification of final candidates.
  • The WHO is committed to creating a diverse and inclusive environment of mutual respect. The WHO recruits and employs staff regardless of disability status, sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, language, race, marital status, religious, cultural, ethnic and socio-economic backgrounds, or any other personal characteristics.
  • The WHO is committed to achieving gender parity and geographical diversity in its workforce. Women, persons with disabilities, and nationals of unrepresented and underrepresented Member States (https://www.who.int/careers/diversity-equity-and-inclusion) are strongly encouraged to apply.
  • Persons with disabilities can request reasonable accommodations to enable participation in the recruitment process. Requests for reasonable accommodation should be sent through an email to reasonableaccommodation@who.int
  • WHO has a smoke-free environment and does not recruit smokers or users of any form of tobacco.
  • Please note that WHO’s contracts are conditional on members of the workforce confirming that they are vaccinated as required by WHO before undertaking a WHO assignment, except where a medical condition does not allow such vaccination, as certified by the WHO Department of Staff Health and Wellbeing (SHW). The successful candidate will be asked to provide relevant evidence related to this condition. A copy of the updated vaccination card must be shared with WHO medical service in the medical clearance process. Please note that certain countries require proof of specific vaccinations for entry or exit. For example, official proof /certification of yellow fever vaccination is required to enter many countries. Country-specific vaccine recommendations can be found on the WHO international travel and Staff Health and Wellbeing website. For vaccination-related queries please contact SHW directly at shws@who.int.

The project focuses on addressing immediate humanitarian needs through emergency relief, early recovery support, and the restoration of essential services while ensuring accountability, compliance, and efficient use of resources.

Key Summary of Functions

The Procurement and Logistics Manager will provide leadership, coordination and technical oversight of procurement, logistics and supply chain functions across PIN Nepal, ensuring the timely, efficient and compliant procurement, movement, storage and delivery of goods, services, equipment and relief materials. During the initial six months, the position will have a particular focus on the Rasuwa Flood Response, providing hands-on coordination and technical support to emergency procurement, supply chain, transportation, warehousing, customs clearance and field logistics. The position will also contribute to strengthening country-level procurement and logistics systems, staff capacity and supply chain visibility. The role requires a good understanding of the Nepal humanitarian and operational context, including local markets, suppliers, geographical and access constraints, transportation, government processes and emergency operating environments.

Minimum 3-4 years in senior level.
  • Experience with procurement, warehousing, transportation, fleet and/or customs clearance, with an understanding of their integration with financial management.
  • Experience supervising, coaching or supporting teams across different locations.

Introduction

People in Need (PIN) is a non-governmental, non-profit, international organisation founded in the Czech 1992. PIN arrived in Nepal as part of a humanitarian response to the April 25, 2015 earthquake. Since its inception in Nepal, PIN has had a strong role in designing and facilitating systemic solutions, advocating for and addressing the needs of vulnerable populations affected by disasters, including people who live in geographically remote areas of the country, historically marginalised ethnic groups, and those marginalised because of their age and/or gender identity. PIN is strongly committed to the safeguarding of children and vulnerable adults, including persons with disabilities, in line with its safeguarding framework and child protection policy.

Scope of Work

Under the direct supervision of the Project Manager, the Provincial Coordinator will support the project team in the effective implementation of the related activities under the ACCESS project and represent PIN at Provincial and local/district levels. This includes supporting the program, M&E department, and partners’ staff and district chapters in the implementation of project deliverables in the field. S/he will be responsible for the management of activity trackers and information sharing across the organisation, partners and other relevant stakeholders. Additionally, PC will work together with the GIEN lead and GIEN officers.

All PIN staff agree to:

  • Comply with all relevant PIN policies, Country Program Policies, and guidelines related to their position.
  • Show a strong commitment to the inclusion of all groups within Nepal and dedication to PIN Nepal’s Inclusion Guidelines.
  • Perform and accurately complete administrative tasks related to their position.
  • Strive for quality in all aspects of their work and ensure the highest quality performance of the Country Program.
  • Maintain a positive attitude and promote a professional & productive working environment across all staff, departments, and among all of PIN’s partners.

About the Project

ACCESS – Accelerating Civil Society’s Role in Securing Education for All in Madhesh, Karnali and Sudurpaschim Provinces _ ACCESS programme

People in Need (PIN), the National Campaign for Education (NCE), the Nepal Disabled Women Association (NDWA), and Accountability Lab Nepal (ALN) have collaborated to develop a comprehensive, locally-driven initiative in the Madhesh, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim provinces. This initiative aims to strengthen the role of civil society in ensuring education for all by empowering CSOs and networks to lead the implementation of the School Education Sector Plan (SESP). The consortium will partner with member CSOs of NCE and NDWA to (i) enhance their organisational and technical capacities in implementing inclusive education methodologies, and (ii) provide local CSOs with the skills to promote transparency and accountability in education plans through the mobilisation of Girls and Inclusive Education Networks (GIEN) and the CivActs model. The EU-funded ACCESS project is scheduled to begin implementation on April 1, 2024. It is expected that this program will directly benefit community members, Community-Based Organisations (CBOs), Civil Society Organisations (CSOs), and government tiers across the three provinces, including community schools, by strengthening civil society’s role and improving participation in advancing equitable access to education. The priority provinces for this initiative are Madhesh, Karnali, and Sudurpaschim.

It saves lives and protects people on the move, drives solutions to displacement, and facilitates pathways for regular migration, while providing services and advice to governments and migrants.

IOM is committed to fostering a respectful, inclusive and supportive workplace where all employees can thrive professionally and feel valued. By creating such an environment, IOM aims to better harness the full potential of migration and strengthen its support to people on the move.

IOM invites candidates from diverse backgrounds to apply and provides reasonable accommodation throughout the recruitment process when required. Learn more about IOM’s workplace culture at IOM workplace culture | International Organization for Migration

Organizational Context and Scope

On 26 August 2026, a sudden and destructive flood and debris flow affected communities along the river systems in central Nepal, causing extensive loss of life, displacement and damage to homes and critical infrastructure. The disaster severely affected settlements in Rasuwa, Nuwakot, Dhading and other downstream districts, while damage to roads and communications continues to constrain access to some affected areas. As of 4 September 2026, the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority (NDRRMA) reports that 1,294 bodies have been recovered, 5,053 people remain missing, and 301 people have been injured. A total of 13,095 people have been rescued. An estimated 352,000 people, across 17 municipalities in six districts, have been affected by the flood.

Given the mixed displacement patterns observed at the collective sites, host family arrangements, and in-place sheltering near damaged homes, IOM will also support a phased approach that moves from immediate life-saving emergency shelter support toward household-level recovery assistance. The initiative is designed to address initial emergency response and shelter recovery ensuring affected households are not left without adequate shelter during the transitional period while national damage assessments and recovery frameworks are finalized.

Under the overall supervision of the International Organization for Migration (IOM)’s Chief of Mission and the direct supervision of the Head of MECR department, the successful candidate will support the implementation of activities of Shelter and Settlements.

5. Coordinate with relevant government authorities, Shelter and CCCM Cluster partners and other stakeholders to ensure technical quality, complementarity and adherence to agreed standards.

6. Support technical reporting, assessments, project planning and resource mobilization, as required.

7. Provide shelter/settlement related training/orientation to all relevant parties including field engineers, masons and contractors.

8. Donor engagement.

9. Facilitate joint monitoring with government and donors.

10. Liaise with IOM regional and headquarters, as needed.

11. Perform duties as assigned by Supervisor.

Vacancy No.: S18627
Category of Contract: National

Country: NEPAL

Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans.

The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal.

On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins.

Due to the evolving operational requirements of the Rasuwa Flash Flood 2026 response operation, this role profile provides an overview of the principal responsibilities and functions associated with this position within a Federation-coordinated operation.

Job Purpose

Senior Officer, Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene (WASH) is a member who supports the IFRC’s programmatic vision for WASH and its translation into programmatic interventions, in close collaboration and coordination with NSs, by providing technical advice, support and coordination to the Federation’s programmes in the area of WASH throughout the resilience continuum (in emergency, recovery and development contexts).

The person will be the principal representative in executing the WASH activities at field level and report to Operations Manager. The main objective of the Sr. WASH Officer is to establish strong coordination among stakeholders and linkages with NRCS technical leads in the field to ensure that program activities are implemented successfully.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

Enable RCRC to be a global leading player in the WASH sector

  • Contribute to and support the coordination of the work of RCRC at relevant regional, ensuring interventions are in line with global and regional strategic directions and advocacy themes.
  • Contribute to the development of global policies, strategies, guidelines and tools as well as the integration of these standards into the work of RCRC to ensure sound and sustainable WASH programmes and effective public health outcomes.
  • Work closely with other members of the WASH team and relevant colleagues at the IFRC CCSTs/COs, contributing to ensuring appropriate visibility, resource mobilization and public awareness of the work of IFRC/RCRC.

Support NSs to improve its emergency WASH performance

  • Support the mapping of regional WASH programming, progress and best practices and priority needs of NSs especially in the context of emergency WASH and contribute to the development of project and programme proposals in line with best practice.
  • Work closely with NSs and provide technical guidance to the planning process of emergency WASH activities.
  • Contribute to providing specific technical support to ensure NSs are able to effectively incorporate WASH components/elements within each stage of the emergency cycle and along the resilience continuum: strengthening of WASH as part of prevention; WASH disaster preparedness; water quality monitoring as part of community disease detection and early warning; emergency WASH response including full spectrum of public health related WASH capacities and WASH during recovery aimed at ‘building back better’.
  • Contribute to the four cross organizational WASH related work streams: WASH for development through expansion of GWSI; WASH in disasters; WASH during public health emergencies and WASH in Urban Settings.

Contribute to and backstop coordination of WASH during emergencies

  • Provide technical input to emergency plans of action and engage with implementing NSs to support operations as appropriate including supporting the selection and deployment of surge personnel.
  • When required and in line with other work priorities be available for direct deployment to support emergency response for up to 1 month.

Contribute to delivering quality emergency WASH programming

  • Take an active role in the preparation and facilitation of related trainings organised by IFRC CCSTs/COs and NSs. Training preparation could include working on training modules/content, aligned with global policies, strategies, guidelines and tools, and strategies/priorities of the NSs.
  • Contribute to the development of tools and guidelines in accordance with applicable international standards to enhance the quality of operations, and eventual dissemination to NSs and IFRC CCSTs/COs.
  • Working in close collaboration with NSs and IFRC CCSTs/COs to put in place, where relevant and appropriate, a systematic approach to data collection and analysis, contributing to quality reporting.

Contribute to accountable emergency WASH programming

  • Contribute to the preparation of terms of reference for monitoring and evaluation exercises and development of research questions and work to ensure implementation of recommendations for improvement.
  • When appropriate and in line with other work priorities be available to participate as an evaluation team member.

Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)

Contribute to an effective, high-quality IFRC team:

  • Be accountable to the Regional WASH Coordinator by providing regular progress reports on results against objectives.
  • Be a proactive team member fostering a customer service-oriented culture that values proactivity, continuous improvement, innovation, high performance and cost effectiveness.
  • Foster a co-creative environment with colleagues in the Region and with NSs including actors in the relevant external environment.
  • Be responsible for the project management of sections of the regional project portfolio as required.

Education

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent higher education degree.
  • Technical training courses linked to the post.

Experience

  • 6-7 years’ experience in an adequate field
  • Experience in the humanitarian or development sector, with a focus on WASH
  • Demonstrated professional credibility in the sector and experience working in an international or cross-cultural environment.
  • Experience working in a Red Cross or Red Crescent National Society and/or IFRC or ICRC

Knowledge, Skills and Languages

  • Knowledge of WASH and public health and experience in practically applying this knowledge into policy, programmes and positioning
  • Proactive, innovative, willing, and committed to stay and travel in the remote areas to work with poor and vulnerable communities.
  • Programme and project management
  • Results-oriented and demand-driven individual, entrepreneurial, ability to lead in unprecedented and/or ambiguous situations.
  • Demonstrated track record in innovating, contributing to a learning culture, sharing knowledge and new approaches to engaging partners.
  • Professional credibility, able to work effectively at all levels across the organisation
  • Proven good judgment and ability to work with complete integrity and confidentiality
  • Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problem solving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants.
  • Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values.

Competencies, Values and Comments

Values: Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability

Core competencies: Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust.

The National Federation of Women Living with HIV and AIDS (NFWLHA), was officially registered in 2007 with a vision to create a just and equitable society for women and children infected and affected with HIV, so that they can live a productive, empowered and dignified life, free from stigma and discrimination. Underpinned by guiding principles of gender equity and human rights, evidence-based planning, programming, and policy advocacy, NFWLHA has broadened its strategic intervention areas over the last nine years, focusing mainly on strengthening and capacity development of the network, knowledge management for evidence-based policy advocacy and community system strengthening.

Currently, NFWLHA is implementing the Treatment, Care and Support Program in 25 districts across Koshi, Madhesh, and Bagmati Provinces with support from the Global Fund through UNDP. To support the effective implementation of this program, NFWLHA invites applications from qualified and motivated candidates for the following position:

Position: Finance Assistant-1 (Treatment Care and Support Program)

Duty Station: NFWLHA Central Office, Kathmandu (Frequent travel to program district)

Purpose of the Position:

The Finance Assistant will provide support to the finance department in managing the financial operations of NFWLHA. This will include assisting with accounting tasks, processing payments, maintaining financial records, and ensuring compliance with financial policies and procedures.

Accounting Support:

Administrative Support:

Reporting and recording

Meeting and communications

Organizational Development

Education and Qualification

  • Strong knowledge of basic accounting principles and procedures.

FAO seeks gender, geographical and linguistic diversity in order to best serve FAO Members in all regions.

FAO is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, background and culture
Qualified female applicants, qualified nationals of non-and under-represented Members and person with disabilities are encouraged to apply

Organizational Setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level.

The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources.

Specifically, FAO Country Offices:

  • advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate;
  •  provide technical assistance and deliver core services;
  •  assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation;
  • Position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation;
  • ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management.

Despite being continuously dependent on agriculture, with 67 percent of the population living in agricultural households, Nepal’s agriculture sector still struggles with low productivity, limited competitiveness, and weak commercialization. These challenges have severely limited income-generation opportunities and broader rural transformation efforts, further contributing to the persistent outmigration of youth and the deterioration of the long-term vitality of farming communities. Women, in this context, carry multiple responsibilities and obligations while lacking access to productive resources, services, technologies and decision-making spaces. Meanwhile, Nepal’s agrifood systems are becoming increasingly vulnerable to growing climate-related shocks and stresses. The resilience of smallholder farmers and local food systems is becoming increasingly fragile under these compounding pressures. Adding to these challenges are food and nutrition insecurity, limited access to clean and safe drinking water, and the absence of sustainable long-term operation and maintenance systems, highlighting the need for integrated and locally grounded intervention.

As a result of these challenges, FAO Nepal has been requested by the Government of Nepal, represented by the Ministry of Agriculture, Forest and Environment, to provide technical assistance for the project “Strengthening Agrifood System in Nepal” under the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund supported through CIDCA. The project is designed as a 24-month initiative with a total budget of USD 2,488,810. The implementation will focus on Nepal’s hill and mountain regions, with Mandandeupur Municipality and Panchkhal Municipality in Kavre and Rong Rural Municipality and Suryodaya Municipality in Ilam serving as demonstration sites for piloting and operationalizing the interventions.The projects aim to strengthen the foundation for long-term agrifood systems transformation in Nepal through comprehensive interventions that emphasize governance capacity, scaling up climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive technologies, improving market access and inclusion, expanding water security solutions, and promoting environmental sustainability and agrobiodiversity conservation. Institutional strengthening, alongside field-level investments and community-based actions, will also be prioritized to secure stronger support from local governments, farmer organizations, and partner institutions.

To support effective project delivery and ensure quality implementation, FAO Nepal seeks to engage two Field Facilitation Supports, one based in Kavrepalanchok District, and one based in Ilam District, to provide day-to-day field facilitation support and technical support for project implementation. The Field Facilitation Support in Kavrepalanchok will support activities in Mandandeupur Municipality and Panchkhal Municipality, while the Field Facilitation Support in Ilam will support activities in the designated municipalities under the guidance and supervision of FAO personnel. Their responsibilities will include supporting field implementation, beneficiary registration, data collection, monitoring, documentation, reporting, and logistical arrangements for project activities, in accordance with approved workplans and FAO procedures.

Reporting Lines

The Field Facilitation Support will work under the overall supervision of the Assistant FAO Representative (Programme) in Nepal, Programme Manager and the direct supervision of the Project Coordinator for the project “Strengthening Agrifood Systems in Nepal” (GCP/NEP/094/CPR).

Technical Focus

The Field Facilitation Support will provide technical and operational support to project implementation, monitoring, data collection, documentation and reporting activities at the municipal level under the direct supervision of FAO technical personnel. The Field Facilitation Support will support field-level activities related to climate-smart and nutrition-sensitive agriculture, agrifood systems development, beneficiary engagement, capacity-development events, monitoring activities and project documentation.

Tasks and responsibilities

  • Assist the FAO Supervisor in preparing municipality-level implementation schedules and activity plans based on approved project workplans.
  • Support transparent beneficiary identification, verification and mobilization, ensuring inclusion targets and disaggregated records are maintained.
  •  Support baseline surveys, field assessments, value chain assessments, data collection exercises and compilation of project-related information as directed by the FAO Supervisor.
  •  Assist in organizing trainings, demonstrations, farmer field activities, nutrition field activities, awareness campaigns, consultations and exchange visits, including logistical and administrative arrangements.
  • Support the dissemination of technical information and training materials related to climate-smart agriculture, nutrition-sensitive agriculture, agroecological practices, soil fertility management, integrated pest management, water-use efficiency and food safety under the guidance of FAO technical personnel.
  •  Support producer groups, cooperatives and enterprises participating in project activities by maintaining records and facilitating their participation in project interventions.
  • Assist in site verification, distribution tracking, installation support, user orientation and monitoring of project-supported inputs, equipment, irrigation systems, storage facilities and other assets.
  • Support the collection and maintenance of records related to project-supported infrastructure, equipment and community-level interventions.
  •  Maintain municipality-level project documentation, including attendance records, participant profiles, photographs, geotagged information, field visit notes, evaluation forms, distribution records and beneficiary feedback.
  • Collect, compile and submit progress information, supporting documentation and evidence related to project outputs and indicators.
  •  Assist in documenting field observations, achievements, challenges, lessons learned, success stories and beneficiary experiences for reporting purposes.
  •  Support monitoring visits undertaken by FAO personnel and promptly report observations and issues to the FAO Supervisor for follow-up.
  •  Assist FAO personnel in organizing meetings, workshops, field visits, assessments and review events at municipal level.
  • Provide logistical and administrative support for field missions, monitoring visits, assessments and project-related events.
  •  Assist in the preparation of reports, presentations, briefing materials and other project documentation by compiling relevant data and supporting information.
  • Apply gender equality, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, climate resilience, safeguarding, informed consent, confidentiality, responsible data management and do-no-harm principles while carrying out assigned duties.

CANDIDATES WILL BE ASSESSED AGAINST THE FOLLOWING

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor’s degree in Agriculture, Agricultural Economics, Rural Development, Natural Resource Management, Development Studies or a related field.
  • At least five years of relevant experience in agriculture, rural development, food security, climate resilience or community-based projects.
  •  Working knowledge of English and Nepali.
  • National of Federal Democratic Republic of Nepal or resident of the country with a valid work permit.

FAO Core Competencies

  • Results Focus
  •  Teamwork
  • Communication
  • Building Effective Relationships
  • Knowledge Sharing and Continuous Improvement

Technical/Functional Skills

  •  Experience working with local governments, farmer groups, cooperatives, women’s groups and community organizations.
  • Proven experience in field-level project implementation, training, beneficiary mobilization, monitoring, reporting and stakeholder coordination.
  •  Good understanding of agrifood systems, value chains, climate-smart agriculture, nutrition-sensitive agriculture and rural livelihoods.
  •  Experience in data collection, documentation, monitoring and evaluation, and report preparation.
  • Strong communication, facilitation, coordination and problem-solving skills.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office and digital data-collection and reporting tools.
  • Ability to work effectively in multicultural environments and undertake frequent field travel.

Selection Criteria

  •  Extent and relevance of experience in municipality-level agricultural or rural-development project implementation.
  •  Extent and relevance of experience in training, demonstrations, community engagement and stakeholder coordination.
  • Knowledge of local government systems, Agriculture Knowledge Centres and community institutions.
  •  Experience with development partners, NGOs, United Nations agencies or government programmes.
  •  Understanding of gender equality, social inclusion, environmental sustainability and safeguarding principles.
  •  Working knowledge of Chinese is an asset for coordination with Chinese experts and institutions under the CIDCA-supported project.

Please note that all candidates should adhere to FAO Values of Commitment to FAO, Respect for All and Integrity and Transparency.

FAO’s commitment to environmental sustainability is integral to our strategic objectives and operations.

The District Coordinator will lead and coordinate the implementation of the Nepal flash flood response project at Rasuwa district and municipal levels. Additionally, this position will represent WVI Nepal in the district as required and oversee the local partner NGO’s performance, compliances (security, safeguarding, financial, procurement), assurance quality, and participate in partner NGO’s meeting (including Board meeting) to provide and get updates as well.

The incumbent should be a team player, agile and strategic leader, issue and problem solving and emphatic. The role expects to maintain a good rapport and coordination with peer organizations, key stakeholders including the government line agencies.

This position is expected to have a comprehensive understanding and operational skill to expedite the momentum of the programme delivery. This includes creating an enabling and conducive environment in the given working areas of the district.

Organizational Setting

FAO is a specialized agency of the UN that leads international efforts to defeat hunger. FAO’s goal is to achieve food security for all and ensure that people have regular access to enough high-quality food to lead active, healthy lives. With 195 Members (194 countries and the European Union), FAO works in over 130 countries worldwide.

FAO Country Offices, working under overall corporate guidance and in line with the Strategic Framework, offer policy advice and support to countries in the mandated areas of FAO, facilitated through partnerships, resources and an active country programme to provide technical assistance, develop capacities and deliver core services while fully observing international standards of accountability to establish leadership and strengthen impact at the country level.

The offices deliver on the programmatic priorities of each country as agreed in their respective Country Programming Frameworks (CPFs) aligned to the UN Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework (UNSDCF) and ensure effective and efficient operations with adequate human and financial resources.

Specifically, FAO Country Offices:

(i) advocate, inform and support policies and investments in the areas of FAO’s mandate;
(ii) provide technical assistance and deliver core services;
(iii) assist and catalyse partnership and resource mobilization activities to support agrifood systems transformation;
(iv) Position FAO as the specialized/authoritative technical agency in food and agriculture and agrifood systems transformation;
(v) ensure risk-smart and accountable operations and management.

Nepal’s agrifood systems continue to face significant challenges, including low agricultural productivity, weak commercialization, climate vulnerability, food and nutrition insecurity, limited access to safe drinking water, and inadequate operation and maintenance systems. These constraints disproportionately affect smallholder farmers, women, and rural communities, limiting livelihood opportunities and contributing to youth outmigration.

To address these challenges, FAO Nepal, at the request of the Government of Nepal, is implementing the project “Strengthening Agrifood Systems in Nepal” (GCP/NEP/094/CPR) under the Global Development and South-South Cooperation Fund supported by the China International Development Cooperation Agency (CIDCA). The 24-month project, with a budget of USD 2.49 million, supports agrifood systems transformation in Kavre and Ilam districts through interventions on governance, production, nutrition, enterprise development, water systems, social inclusion, and environmental sustainability.

In parallel, FAO Nepal is implementing the UN Joint Programme “Innovative Financial Solutions for Local Food Systems Transformation in Nepal” (UNJP/NEP/091/UNJ), funded by the Joint SDG Fund and jointly implemented with UNDP, WFP, and UNCDF. Under this programme, FAO leads the development of innovative financing solutions, including blended finance, public-private partnerships (PPPs), investment pipeline development, and support to women-led agribusinesses and cooperatives in Panchkhal Municipality.

Given the strong complementarities between the CIDCA-supported project and the Joint SDG Fund programme, particularly in Panchkhal Municipality, coordinated implementation is essential to maximize synergies, strengthen stakeholder engagement, avoid duplication, and enhance the sustainability and impact of project investments.

To support effective implementation, FAO Nepal seeks a National Project Coordinator.

The National Project Coordinator will be under the overall supervision of the Assistant FAOR (Programme), and the direct supervision of the Programme Manager and relevant FAO technical officers.

The National Project Coordinator will provide overall technical, programmatic, and operational leadership for the implementation of the projects “Strengthening Agrifood Systems in Nepal” (GCP/NEP/094/CPR) and “Innovative Financial Solutions for Local Food Systems Transformation in Nepal” (UNJP/NEP/091/UNJ), with a focus on project planning, coordination, implementation, monitoring, reporting, stakeholder engagement, partnership development, innovative financing mechanisms, agrifood systems transformation, and results-based management, while promoting gender equality, social inclusion, climate resilience, environmental sustainability, and effective collaboration with government institutions, UN agencies, financial institutions, private-sector partners, cooperatives, and community organizations.
