Posiiton: Administrative Assistant
Vacancy No.: S18628
Category of Contract: National
Position Type: National
Application Deadline: 25/09/2026
Job Posted On: 18/09/2026
Duty Station: Kathmandu
Country: NEPAL
Grade: National Staff
Duty Station Status: N/A
Accompanied Status: N/A
Duration: 12 months

Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability. IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpur); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe. The IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles. The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans. The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal. On 26 August 2026, a major ice-rock avalanche occurred in the upper Bhote Koshi watershed near the China–Nepal border, resulting in an historically powerful flash flood that advanced from the border down the entire length of Nepal along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli River basins. Due to the evolving operational requirements of the Rasuwa Flash Flood 2026 response operation, this role profile provides an overview of the principal responsibilities and functions associated with this position within a Federation-coordinated operation.

Job Purpose: This position caters to the daily administrative operations of the Country Delegation Nepal of IFRC, especially to the office and administrative needs of the PNSs which are under operation.

Job Duties and Responsibilities

  •  Support the efficient implementation of office administrative procedures and workflows.
  • Coordinate administrative support services for staff, delegates, visitors, and partner National Societies as required.
  •  Maintain and update filing systems, databases, contact lists, inventories, contracts, agreements, and administrative records in both electronic and hard-copy formats.
  •  Assist in preparing correspondence, reports, meeting minutes, presentations, and other administrative documents.
  • Coordinate domestic travel arrangements, including air ticket bookings, hotel reservations, and maintenance of travel-related records. Liaise with the fleet team to arrange and track airport pick-up and drop-off services for visitors as required.
  •  Assist in arranging residential accommodation for delegates, including sourcing suitable housing options, coordinating property viewings, preparing inventory documentation, liaising with landlords, and facilitating administrative processes related to lease agreements and utility services.
  • Provide administrative support for domestic meetings, workshops, trainings, conferences, field visits, and official events across Nepal, including venue arrangements, accommodation, transportation, participant coordination, and other event-related requirements.
  •  Support procurement processes in accordance with IFRC policies and procedures, including obtaining quotations, preparing procurement documentation, following up on deliveries, maintaining procurement records, and processing administrative invoices and supporting documentation.
  • Track and process telecommunication, internet, utility, and other administrative service bills, ensuring timely payments and compliance with IFRC policies and procedures.

Job Duties and Responsibilities (continued)

  •  Maintain updated inventory and asset registers and support periodic physical verification of office assets.
  •  Monitor office supplies and stationery stocks and arrange timely replenishment.
  • Liaise with vendors, landlords, service providers, and maintenance contractors to ensure timely and quality service delivery.
  • Support management of office facilities, utilities, office equipment, and maintenance requirements.
  •  Monitor administrative service agreements and contracts and coordinate timely renewals when required.
  • Ensure proper documentation, filing, and archiving of administrative records and correspondence.
  •  Maintain confidentiality of sensitive organizational information and records.
  • Support compliance with administrative policies, procedures, and operational standards.
  • Be proactive and liaise with different department to ensure the smooth functioning of Administration Unit and delivery of services in an efficient and effective manner.

Education: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent higher education degree.

Experience

Required: 2-3 years’ experience in a relevant field Proactive, innovative, willing, and committed to staying and traveling in remote areas to work with vulnerable communities. Preferred: Experience in working in an international environment, preferably with the United Nations or a similar organization Experience within the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement

Knowledge, Skills and Languages

Excellent professional communication skills, both verbal and written in both English and Nepali A high degree of competence in teamwork, commitment to the International Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement and its work, integrity and personal conduct, flexibility and adaptability Sound knowledge of Microsoft Office applications Demonstrated core proficiency in (a) digital communication & collaboration, (b) basic digital content creation, (c) digital safety & security, (d) data literacy, and (e) problem solving with technology (including responsible use of AI assistants. Understanding of and commitment to IFRC’s mission and values.

Competencies, Values and Comments

Values: Respect for diversity; Integrity; Professionalism; Accountability Core competencies: Communication; Collaboration and teamwork; Judgement and decision making; National society and customer relations; Creativity and innovation; Building trust

We are looking for a responsible and organized Librarian to oversee the day-to-day operations of the school library. The role involves maintaining library resources and records, managing the issue and return of books, supporting students and teachers with library activities, ensuring the library remains clean and organized, and maintaining a peaceful and productive learning environment.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

  •  Ensure all library items are maintained in proper and functional condition.
  •  Prepare and implement library rules and regulations in consultation with the Vice Principal and Principal.
  • Issue library books and other materials according to established library procedures.
  • Ensure that issued books and materials are returned on time.
  •  Provide reading record forms to students along with issued books and maintain proper records.
  •  Compile reading record forms class-wise and submit them to the Vice Principal on the first day of each month for the previous month.
  •  Maintain a neat, clean, organized, and peaceful library environment.
  •  Conduct library classes for students as per the school timetable.
  •  Enter and maintain records of all library books and resources in the system.
  •  Maintain proper documentation and records related to library activities.
  •  Perform other library-related duties and responsibilities as assigned by the Principal.

KEY REQUIREMENTS

1. Qualification

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent qualification in Education, Library Science, or a relevant field.
  • Additional training or certification in library management will be an advantage.

2. Experience

  • Previous experience working as a Librarian, preferably in a school or educational institution.
  •  Experience in library management, record keeping, and electronic database systems will be an advantage.

3. Knowledge, Skills and Competencies

  •  Strong organizational and record-management skills.
  • Effective communication and interpersonal skills.
  •  Ability to multitask and manage library activities efficiently.
  • Proficiency in MS Office and basic computer applications.
  •  Experience working with electronic databases or library management systems.
  •  Strong time-management and coordination skills.
  •  Creativity and problem-solving skills.
  •  Ability to maintain a clean, organized, and peaceful library environment.
  •  Responsible, disciplined, and proactive approach to work.

Posiiton: WASH & Shelter Coordinator
Location: Kathmandu

End Date: September 27, 2026

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

Local – Fixed Term Employee (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

World Vision International Nepal (WVI Nepal) has launched a Category II Emergency Response in the priority districts of Rasuwa and Nuwakot, Bagmati Province, following devastating flash floods along the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli river corridors that caused casualties, displacement and extensive damage across Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. The 12-month Nepal Flash Flood Response (NFFR) 2026 plan targets 25,000 people, including 10,000 children, from around 5,000 affected households across seven sectors, moving from relief into early recovery.

The WASH & Shelter Coordinator will provide overall planning, technical leadership and oversight for the WASH and Shelter interventions under the Nepal Flash Flood Response 2026 related projects in Rasuwa and Nuwakot district. WASH coordinator’s main responsibility will be planning, assessment, design, development estimate costing, providing overall quality oversight of the physical infrastructure construction/rehabilitation of WASH facilities, Shelter etc. including facilitation of the soft components – awareness, social mobilization and ensuring the standards of the WASH and Shelter technical parts of projects planned in the projects as well. This position will have regular coordination among internal teams for the required technical input, with Partner NGOs and all relevant stakeholders.

This position will lead technical input, field implementation, coordination with partner non-government organizations & government stakeholders, participation in the cluster meeting at local/district level, reporting and support required technical documents as per the government standard and norms.

This role envisions a good team player, managing issues and problem solving, innovative and agile leadership. Overall purpose of this role is to ensure the planned activities are timely delivered to the targeted populace, and key learnings are captured for future interventions.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Project implementation and technical support engagement

  • Identify and implement the appropriate technologies used in WASH and Shelter programs which are culturally appropriate, user friendly and safe for environment
  • Coordinate and mobilize communities and local partners on WASH and Infrastructure activity planning, designing and implementation.
  • Facilitate needs assessment, problem identification, stakeholder and situation analysis along with project team in Partner NGO.
  • Provide technical lead regarding design, construction, structural assessment and recommendation for the infrastructure (WASH facilities and Shelter) rehabilitation/construction as per the different phases of responses.
  • Ensure the intervened structures are earthquake resilient, gender and disability friendly.
  • Provide technical backstopping in preparing construction material specifications, monitoring construction quality, and estimating quantities and costs of materials, equipment, and labor for effective project planning and implementation
  • Coordinate with supply chain management team for required sourcing of the infrastructure facilities and engage in technical evaluation process. Coordinate and contribute for water quality and hygiene maintenance in shelters, and in communities along with health and nutrition team.
  • Train local partners on SPHERE standards and project monitoring for the Infrastructure & WASH interventions.
  • Prepare day-to-day monitoring report.
  • Work closely with Operation Manager for budget preparation and implementation, forecast, support Partner NGOs for the WASH and Shelter related interventions
  • Verify program data through spot checks, field observations, and review of partner reporting systems.
  • Any immediate changes or contextual alteration should be identified and planned ensuring all the given processes

Meet quality of infrastructure activities and ensure timely implementation

  • Conduct regular monitoring, onsite coaching & mentoring and evaluation of all infrastructure construction works within project areas.
  • Ensure timely response and resolutions to the feedback/issues.
  • Coordination with related line agencies/stakeholders at the project locations for smooth operation of construction works.
  • Ensure project on-time delivery, operation & maintenance plans, project quality, and adherence to safety protocols and ensure works are carried out to the appropriate National or International Building Standards.
  • Ensure that construction expenses are made by the phased budget, project budget and compliance with World Vision financial procedure
  • Ensure effective and efficient utilization of program resources through monitoring and tracking expenditures against project plan. Lead budget revision if needed.
  • Maintain a tracker for all infrastructure interventions and proactively plan and implement measures to address and minimize project delays.
  • Construction expenses are in line with budget and World Vision financial procedure.
  • Prepare/Review running bills/completion reports and recommendation for the payment process.
  • Monitor project performance against approved indicators, benchmarks, work plans, and donor requirements.
  • Work closely with the MEAL team to strengthen community feedback and accountability mechanisms and ensure appropriate response to beneficiary concerns.
  • Promote utilization of monitoring and learning findings for adaptive program management.

Networking and Advocacy

  • Represent World Vision in WASH, Shelter cluster and technical working group at district and provincial level.
  • Coordinate with line agencies to plan and implement the Infrastructure & WASH interventions as per the cluster guidance and to address the contextual need.
  • Strengthen relationships with project stakeholders such as Community groups, Children, parents, the Government of Nepal Offices, NGOs, like minded organization and private sectors such as vendors, and contractors to collaboration and avoid the duplication through partnership and cooperation. The Stakeholders assisted with different programs according to the project design.

Timely and quality documentation and reporting

  • Regular update sharing with project teams for the Infrastructure and WASH interventions deliverables.
  • Preparation of certificate of completion for the completed scheme.
  • Prepare operations and maintenance (O & M) manuals for the implemented construction scheme.
  • Document relevant data and evidence to showcase the outcomes of the project
  • Gather photographs and videos of project deliverables, locations, institutions, communities, children, and community members along with stories to share with the wider audience.
  • Support partners in maintaining adequate documentation and evidence required for audits, donor reviews, and compliance assessments
  • Strengthen accountability, transparency, safeguarding, and ethical practices throughout program implementation.
  • Develop quality reports & submit them on time. The reports are expected to showcase impacts to the beneficiaries.
  • Prepare or present progress and completion reports.
  • Support to line manager to prepare monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual report in accordance with project compliance.
  • All reports and records are properly documented

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering with 5 years of experience in WASH, building construction, and disaster-resilient infrastructures.
  • Oral and written communication skills in English and Nepali.
  • Ability to work in a team and be a great team player.
  • Technical knowledge to do construction activities, field surveys, design, drawing & estimation.
  • Technical knowledge to do and check vulnerability assessments of structures.
  • Through understanding of construction works through a community/contractor approach, handling of multiple contractors/UC in NGOs/INGOs.
  • Ability to ensure specification of construction materials/works & ensure the quality of construction works.

Required Education, training, license, registration, and certification

  • Bachelor’s degree in civil engineering or equivalent from the recognized university.
  • Technical knowledge of civil engineering, building construction, and construction contract management in remote locations.
  • Ability to train non-technical users in the use of technical systems in a cross-cultural setting.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Experience in WASH in an emergency context
  • Cross-cultural sensitivity, flexible worldview, emotional maturity, and physical stamina
  • Ability to exhibit an exemplary lifestyle as interpreted in a specific local culture context
  • Team building, collaboration, facilitation and leadership skills
  • Demonstrated networking, partnership and coordination ability
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and detail orientation
  • Able to work under pressure
  • Demonstrate understanding of and commitment to World Vision’s Core Values in the approach to work and relationships
  • Willingness to work outside office hours especially when traveling and working with partners and communities.
  • Skilled in MS Office applications and AUTO CAD

Work Base: Nuwakot District
Duration: One year

Travel and/or Work Environment

Extensive travel to Rasuwa and Nuwakot of up to 60% of working time. Field travel may involve difficult road conditions, disrupted access, remote locations, and basic accommodation.

Physical Requirements

Willingness and physical ability to travel to Rasuwa and Nuwakot, including remote and disaster-affected locations, for up to 60% of working time.

Language Requirements

Excellent written and spoken English and Nepali, with a demonstrated ability to write reports for donors and external stakeholders.

Minimum 7 years of experience in humanitarian response, disaster management, emergency relief, or early recovery, including at least 3 years in senior project management roles. Experience managing projects, human resources, finance, administration, and partners. Experience working with government agencies in post-disaster contexts.

  • Strong motivator, a team player, and a coach

  • Capacitate finance team of the project and assist in the capacity building of and leading partner companies in developing their capacity in accounting and financial management.

2.4 Administrative and Human Resources management

  •  Liaison with the project staff to ensure that they are aware of all of the administrative systems and procedures;
  •  Lead international and local procurement (where tenders/quotations are required) as a procurement focal person for the project in accordance with HELVETAS Nepal procurement procedures of goods and services;

  •  Ensure efficient vehicle and logistics management and support;
  •  Preparation of contractors’, consultants’ agreements, and contracts, in accordance with programme rules and regulations and available budget;

  • Effective and efficient inventory management;
  • Act as a HR focal person of the project
  •  Coordinate and facilitate for the recruitment process of the project as necessary;
  • Ensure proper induction to new employees on orgainisational policies and guidelines;
  • Contribute for a fair, inclusive, and equitable working environment within the project;
  •  Plan and implement capacity building activities for project and partner staff members;
  •  Ensure proper documentation and confidential of personal records and other HR documents of project staff;
  •  Manage the Human Resource Information System of the project.

2.5 Others

  • Other tasks as and when necessary and as requested by the Project Manager.

3. Job Requirements

3.1 Minimum Education and Professional Experience:

  • Master’s degree in Business Administration, Management, or Commerce with Finance/Accounting as a major subject, or a professional accountancy degree. Minimum 5 years of work experience managing overall finance and accounting of the project, preferably in an international organization.

3.2 Required competencies:

  • Strong ability in supervision of overall financial systems with inclusive frameworks and procedures
  •  Good understanding of national rules and regulations
  •  Understanding of development programme budgeting and financial monitoring
  •  Good understanding of VAT/ Tax rules and regulations
  •  Good time management and task prioritization skills
  •  Commitment towards gender equality, social inclusion, and poverty reduction
  •  Result-oriented maintaining deadlines
  •  Excellent interpersonal, intercultural competencies and team player
  •  Ability to work independently with a minimum level of supervision
  •  Showing initiative in making processes more effective and cost efficient

Position: Team Lead – Emergency Project
Level / Grade: Coordinator, Band III
Number of positions: One
Duty station: Nuwakot
Project / Department: Nuwakot Response and Recovery Project (RRP-Nuwakot)
Reports to: Team Lead, Public Health and DRR
Application deadline: September 26, 2026
Duration of contract: One (1) year with the possibility of extension
Gross salary: NPR 16,10,997 per annum (approx.) plus annual health package and insurance benefits

1. Background

Good Neighbors International is an international, non-profit humanitarian and development organization established in 1991 and headquartered in the Republic of Korea working in 51 countries across Asia, Africa and Latin America in the areas of education, health, water, sanitation and hygiene, income generation, child protection, disaster risk reduction, advocacy and network building. Good Neighbors International Nepal has been working in Nepal since 2002 with the objective of improving the lives of poor and marginalised people, especially children, through integrated community development programmes. Currently, Good Neighbors International Nepal serves marginalized, vulnerable, and poor children, families, and communities in 20 districts across Nepal.

The recent Bhote Koshi flood significantly affected communities in Nuwakot, disrupting homes, essential services, livelihoods, education, and community wellbeing. Vulnerable households, children, and displaced families face increased needs related to shelter, WASH, health, psychosocial wellbeing, education, and child protection.

Good Neighbors International Nepal is thus implementing Nuwakot Response and Recovery Project (RRP-Nuwakot) to support affected communities to transition from immediate relief to safe, dignified, and sustainable recovery through integrated assistance in basic services, child protection, education, and livelihood restoration, including skills development, enterprise support, asset recovery, and market linkages.

The Team Lead – Emergency Project will provide overall strategic, technical, operational, and field-level leadership for the Nuwakot Response and Recovery Project, ensuring effective implementation, coordination, monitoring, quality assurance, and adaptive management of integrated interventions for flood-affected children, families, schools, and communities. The position will coordinate staff, partners, government authorities, and other stakeholders while ensuring compliance with Good Neighbors International Nepal policies, donor requirements, Government of Nepal regulations, safeguarding standards, and relevant humanitarian standards.

Key Responsibilities

Planning and Implementation (30%)

  • Lead overall project planning, implementation, and management, ensuring alignment with the approved project document, work plans, budget, results framework, donor requirements, and organizational policies.
  • Provide strategic and operational leadership to project staff, implementing partners, and technical teams, ensuring integrated interventions covering child protection, CFS/Safe Spaces, PSS, education, health, WASH, livelihoods, and community recovery and resilience.
  • Ensure inclusive, child-centered, and needs-based programming, incorporating gender, disability, conflict sensitivity, community participation, and local ownership throughout project planning and implementation.
  • Develop and monitor annual, quarterly, monthly, and activity-level plans, ensuring timely, quality, and results-oriented implementation across all target areas.
  • Lead the transition from emergency response to early recovery and resilience, including rehabilitation, livelihood restoration, and longer-term community recovery interventions.
  • Monitor implementation progress, identify gaps and emerging needs, and lead timely corrective action, replanning, or reprogramming, in coordination with Good Neighbors
  • International Nepal management, technical departments, partners, government authorities, and donors, while ensuring achievement of approved outputs, outcomes, and indicators.

Coordination and Collaboration (20%)

  • Serve as the primary field-level coordination focal person with DDMC, DAO, local governments, ward offices, government line agencies, schools, health facilities, and other relevant stakeholders, ensuring alignment with government response and recovery priorities.
  • Establish and maintain strategic partnerships with local governments, NGOs, INGOs, UN agencies, development partners, civil society, community organizations, schools, health institutions, and other relevant actors.
  • Facilitate regular coordination and consultation mechanisms, including coordination/review meetings, technical discussions, joint monitoring visits, stakeholder consultations, and effective information sharing.
  • Coordinate sector-specific interventions with relevant education, health, WASH, livelihood, cooperative, market, and technical stakeholders to ensure quality, continuity, referral, recovery, and sustainability of project interventions.
  • Represent Good Neighbors International Nepal in relevant coordination forums, humanitarian platforms, clusters/sectors, technical meetings, and stakeholder events, as delegated, and maintain effective engagement with external partners.
  • Ensure strong internal and external collaboration by coordinating with Good Neighbors International Nepal’s MEAL, Finance, HR, Procurement, Logistics, Communications/PD, and technical teams, as well as project staff and implementing partners, for smooth and effective project delivery.
  • Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) (20%)
  • Ensure effective implementation of the MEAL framework and results-based management, tracking indicators, targets, work plans, budgets, timelines, and quality through regular monitoring and field visits.
  • Conduct regular field monitoring of project sites, schools, CFS/Safe Spaces, health and WASH facilities, livelihood activities, and partner sites, identifying gaps, delays, risks, and emerging needs and ensuring corrective action.
  • Work closely with the MEAL team to ensure quality data collection, validation, analysis, and use, including baseline, needs assessment, PDM, outcome monitoring, evaluation, review, and end-line activities.
  • Ensure accountability to affected communities through effective feedback and complaints mechanisms and appropriate follow-up of concerns.
  • Ensure timely reporting and documentation of project progress, achievements, challenges, lessons learned, good practices, case studies, and success stories, including donor and periodic reports.
  • Lead project reviews, learning, and evidence-based replanning, using monitoring findings and community feedback to support adaptive management, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Capacity Development (5%)

  • Develop and implement capacity-building plans and provide coaching, mentoring, technical guidance, and supportive supervision to project staff, partners, government counterparts, teachers, health workers, and other stakeholders.
  • Lead trainings, orientations, workshops, and technical learning on child protection, safeguarding, PSS, education, health, WASH, livelihoods, DRR, and community resilience, while strengthening partner and local government capacity.
  • Promote community capacity, meaningful participation, knowledge sharing, innovation, and cross-learning, ensuring engagement of children, adolescents, women, caregivers, teachers, and community leaders.

General Administrative, Financial and Resource Management (15%)

  • Ensure compliance with Good Neighbors International Nepal policies, donor requirements, Government regulations, project agreements, safeguarding, and humanitarian standards.
  • Oversee project budgets and financial performance, including expenditure, forecasting, revisions, settlements, and resource allocation, ensuring timely and efficient use of funds.
  • Coordinate with Finance, Procurement, Logistics, and Administration for procurement planning, logistics, partner contracts, and timely implementation of project activities.
  • Promote transparency, accountability, value for money, and proper documentation, ensuring complete and accurate project records and financial supporting documents.
  • Support audits, donor/government monitoring, organizational reviews, and compliance assessments, ensuring timely follow-up and corrective actions, and perform other duties assigned by the supervisor and EMT.

Risk Management, Safeguarding and Emergency Action (5%)

  • Identify and manage programmatic, operational, financial, security, safeguarding, reputational, and compliance risks, including contingency and alternative implementation arrangements, in coordination with relevant teams and partners.
  • Monitor the changing humanitarian and recovery context and emerging needs, ensuring timely action within delegated authority, with critical issues escalated to Good Neighbors International Nepal management as required.
  • Ensure strict adherence to safeguarding, child protection, PSEA, anti-fraud, accountability, and “Do No Harm” principles, including appropriate identification, referral, and follow-up of
  • vulnerable individuals and prevention of unnecessary risks to children, communities, staff, and partners.

Visibility, Branding and Communication (5%)

  • Ensure compliance with Good Neighbors International NAL Nepal and donor visibility requirements, including appropriate branding across project sites, materials, CFS/Safe Spaces, education, WASH, training, distributions, and livelihood activities.
  • Coordinate with the Communications/PD team to document and develop project stories, photographs, videos, case studies, and success stories while ensuring the dignity, privacy, safety, and best interests of children and affected communities.
  • Represent and communicate GOOD NEIGHBORS INTERNATIONAL Nepal’s contribution and partnership with government, communities, media, donors, and development partners, as authorized, at relevant local, district, provincial, national, and international levels.

General Administrative, Financial and Resource Management (15%)

  • Ensure compliance with Good Neighbors International Nepal policies, donor requirements, Government regulations, project agreements, safeguarding, and humanitarian standards.
  • Oversee project budgets and financial performance, including expenditure, forecasting, revisions, settlements, and resource allocation, ensuring timely and efficient use of funds.
  • Coordinate with Finance, Procurement, Logistics, and Administration for procurement planning, logistics, partner contracts, and timely implementation of project activities.
  • Promote transparency, accountability, value for money, and proper documentation, ensuring complete and accurate project records and financial supporting documents.
  • Support audits, donor/government monitoring, organizational reviews, and compliance assessments, ensuring timely follow-up and corrective actions, and perform other duties assigned by the supervisor and EMT.

Risk Management, Safeguarding and Emergency Action (5%)

  • Identify and manage programmatic, operational, financial, security, safeguarding, reputational, and compliance risks, including contingency and alternative implementation arrangements, in coordination with relevant teams and partners.
  • Monitor the changing humanitarian and recovery context and emerging needs, ensuring timely action within delegated authority, with critical issues escalated to Good Neighbors International Nepal management as required.
  • Ensure strict adherence to safeguarding, child protection, PSEA, anti-fraud, accountability, and “Do No Harm” principles, including appropriate identification, referral, and follow-up of vulnerable individuals and prevention of unnecessary risks to children, communities, staff, and partners.

Visibility, Branding and Communication (5%)

  • Ensure compliance with Good Neighbors International NAL Nepal and donor visibility requirements, including appropriate branding across project sites, materials, CFS/Safe Spaces, education, WASH, training, distributions, and livelihood activities.
  • Coordinate with the Communications/PD team to document and develop project stories, photographs, videos, case studies, and success stories while ensuring the dignity, privacy, safety, and best interests of children and affected communities.
  • Represent and communicate GOOD NEIGHBORS INTERNATIONAL Nepal’s contribution and partnership with government, communities, media, donors, and development partners, as authorized, at relevant local, district, provincial, national, and international levels.

Job Requirements

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • ≥90% of planned project activities implemented on time and in accordance with approved work plans.
  • ≥90% of annual project targets achieved, subject to approved contextual modifications.
  • 100% of required donor, government, and organizational reports submitted within agreed timelines.
  • ≥90% of approved project budget utilized effectively and in compliance with approved plans and procedures.
  • 100% of project locations and implementing partners receive planned monitoring, supportive supervision, and technical backstopping.
  • 100% compliance with project implementation, monitoring, reporting, safeguarding, and visibility/branding requirements.
  • Effective coordination maintained with key government, humanitarian, development, and community stakeholders, as evidenced by planned coordination and review meetings.
  • Monitoring and corrective actions: planned field monitoring visits completed, with ≥90% of identified implementation gaps addressed within agreed timelines.
  • Learning and documentation: planned case studies, success stories, good practices, lessons learned, and knowledge products produced.
  • Zero major safeguarding, fraud, compliance, or audit findings attributable to inadequate project management or oversight.
  • Effective transition from emergency response to recovery, including livelihood restoration and community resilience-building, demonstrated through documented progress and outcomes.

Required Qualification

  • Master’s degree in Development Studies, Disaster Risk Management, Social Sciences, Public Health, Education, Management, Agriculture, Social Work, or a related field.
  • Minimum 5 years of relevant experience in humanitarian response, disaster recovery, development, or multi-sectoral programme management.
  • Proven experience in programme planning, implementation, monitoring, adaptive management, and project coordination.
  • Experience in one or more relevant sectors, including child protection, PSS, education, health, WASH, livelihoods, DRR, or community resilience.
  • Demonstrated experience in government and stakeholder coordination, partner management, emergency response/recovery, and donor-funded projects, including compliance and reporting.

Competencies

  • Strong technical knowledge of humanitarian response, disaster recovery, child protection, safeguarding, and multi-sectoral programming.
  • Strong leadership and management skills, with demonstrated ability to lead teams, manage multiple priorities, manage partners, and deliver results under pressure.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, decision-making, and adaptive-management skills, with the ability to work effectively in emergencies and changing contexts.
  • Excellent communication, reporting, facilitation, and representation skills, with commitment to safeguarding, inclusion, accountability, integrity, and the Do No Harm principle.

Working Conditions

  • Frequent field travel to project areas, communities, schools, health facilities, government offices.
  • Regular coordination with government, humanitarian, development, partner, and community stakeholders.
  • Ability to work in challenging and emergency environments, manage multiple priorities, meet deadlines, and work extended hours when required.

Behavioral Expectations

About the job

Admin & Communications Officer ABOUT HEALING TOGETHER

Healing Together Nepal builds the power of everyday people to disrupt generational cycles of trauma and violence. Our mental health and trauma-informed care workshops and support groups democratize access to community-centered, peer-led healing resources so communities impacted by trauma can reclaim their inherent strength, wisdom, resilience, and power to heal themselves and others.
To date, we have facilitated trainings with 3,000+ community leaders from various districts of Nepal, who support over 300,000 trauma survivors in their communities.
We are seeking a passionate, highly self-motivated, and multi-talented professional who can support administration, communications, and training activities as Healing Together Nepal continues to grow its impact and co-create a movement for mental health and healing justice in a thoughtful, equitable, adaptable, and sustainable way.
Our ideal candidate has a proven track record of taking responsibility and completing projects from start to finish, finding practical solutions to challenges, and working with humility, care, creativity, and accountability while remaining aligned with Healing Together’s Guiding Principles.
We encourage applications from women, people from historically marginalized communities, and members of the LGBTQ+ community. title.rendered: Fesslowship Opportunity for Bachelor and Master Studdents

content.rendered:
The Centre for Genomic Regulation (CRG) aims to provide highly motivated undergraduate and master students the opportunity to conduct research at the CRG. The goal is to encourage students (from all nationalities) in the pursuit of a scientific career giving them the prospect to get experience in an international laboratory while improving their skills.

The CRG is a center of excellence with international teams representing a broad range of disciplines, with first class core technologies to support the research projects, a wide range of seminars given by high-profile invited speakers, and courses on complementary and transferable skills integrated with the training programme.

We accept applications throughout the year for any type of internship with a learning agreement with your university. Have a look at our labs and research programmes and contact the Group Leader of your choice directly with the following documents attached:

  • Motivation letter
  • CV
  • Reference letter
  • University transcripts

Acceptance will depend on the capacity of the research group and the ongoing projects.

We host online events and workshops to inform you about various opportunities available at the CRG and guide you on how to search for PhD positions. If you are keen to learn more, please check HERE.

Fellowships available for the academic year 2026/2027:

We are pleased to offer 10 fellowship opportunities across different research projects at the CRG. Each project will remain open until the right candidate is found, giving motivated students the chance to join our vibrant research community and contribute to cutting-edge science.

Please remember that the candidate must be enrolled in an official undergraduate or MSc programme at a university, as an agreement will have to be signed between the candidate’s University and the CRG.

Publication date of these fellowships: August 6th, 2026

Fellowships conditions

  • Stipend: 700€/month/gross – up to 4 months
  • Travel support: Return ticket (up to 1000€/non European flights / up to 400€ for European flights)
  • Eligibility: The fellowship can only be given to new recruits, not students already at the CRG
  • Timing: The fellowship needs to be given within the 2026/2027 academic year

Application Procedure: 

Read carefully the projects below and, if interested, contact the project supervisor and group leader. Please include the following documents in your application:

  • Motivation letter
  • Curriculum Vitae (CV)
  • Reference letter
  • University transcripts

Proteomics – Sabido Core technologies

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – Development of robust LC-MS/MS workflows for proteoform characterization in liquid biopsies

Proteomics | LC-MS/MS | Mass spectrometry | Method development | Sample preparation | Liquid biological samples | Analytical workflow | Protein analysis

Mass spectrometry-based proteomics has become an indispensable tool for the comprehensive characterization of proteins in biological systems, providing valuable insights into cellular processes, disease mechanisms, and biomarker discovery. However, obtaining high-quality and reproducible proteomic data from liquid biological samples remains technically challenging due to sample complexity and variability. Robust sample preparation and optimized analytical workflows are therefore essential to maximize proteome coverage, reproducibility, and quantitative performance.
The aim of this project is to develop and optimize LC-MS/MS-based workflows for the proteomic analysis of liquid biopsies. The student will evaluate key steps in the experimental workflow, including sample preparation, protein digestion, peptide clean-up, and analytical performance, with the objective of establishing a robust and reproducible protocol suitable to perform proteoform characterization in liquid biopsies. Workflow performance will be assessed using quality metrics such as protein and peptide identification rates, reproducibility, and quantitative consistency.
Throughout the project, the student will gain practical experience in modern proteomics methodologies, including sample preparation, liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (LC-MS/MS), experimental design, quality control, and data analysis. The optimized workflow developed during this project will contribute to improving proteomic analyses performed within the CRG Proteomics Unit and will provide a valuable methodological framework for future biomedical research projects.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

The project is suitable for a Master’s student with a background in Biochemistry, Biotechnology, Molecular Biology, Biomedical Sciences, or a related field. Basic laboratory experience in molecular biology or biochemistry is desirable, while prior experience in proteomics or mass spectrometry is not required. The student should be motivated to learn new experimental techniques, have good organizational and analytical skills, and be interested in applying proteomics technologies to biomedical research.

HOW TO APPLY

Send applications documents to the PI and Hiba Salim – HERE

Regulatory genomics and diabetes – Ferrer Lab 

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screening platform in human pancreatic beta cells

Type 1 Diabetes | CRISPR interference screening | CROP-seq | Islet cell therapy | Functional genomics

Type 1 diabetes (T1D) is an autoimmune disease characterised by the progressive destruction of insulin-producing pancreatic beta cells, leading to a lifelong dependence on exogenous insulin. Transplantation of cadaveric islets can restore glycaemic control, but the scarce supply has limited the widespread use of this therapy. Recent studies have enabled the efficient differentiation of human pluripotent stem cells into insulin-producing islet-like clusters (SC-islets), offering a scalable alternative source of cells for cell therapy, as reflected in ongoing clinical trials. Despite this progress, current SC-islets still show metabolic limitations and require immunosuppression, highlighting the need to further optimise beta-cell function. Machine learning approaches can be used to improve SC-islets. It is possible to build a virtual beta cell platform, able to predict how defined perturbations affect beta cell function, guiding the rational optimisation of SC-islets for T1D cell therapies.
To enable robust virtual cell models, it is critically important to generate genetic perturbation data in relevant cell types, which can be used to train the model. This project aims to establish the feasibility of a pooled CRISPR interference (CRISPRi) screening platform in human pancreatic beta cells. The screen will target genes central to beta cell identity, function, and stress resilience, including regulatory network hubs, transcription factors, genetic effectors of T1D and T2D risk, as well as genes that form part of pathways relevant to T1D pathophysiology and graft failure. The screening will be integrated with single-cell RNA sequencing using the CROP-seq approach, which allows simultaneous detection of transcriptional state and the corresponding genetic perturbation at the single-cell level. This strategy will set the basis for a virtual cell model capable of predicting beta-cell transcriptional responses to perturbations.
During this four-month project, the student will be trained in and will perform the key experimental steps required to generate the screening dataset: cloning of guide RNA constructs into CRISPRi backbone, production and titration of lentiviral vectors, transduction of human pancreatic beta cells, and generation of single-cell sequencing libraries. The resulting single-cell data will be analysed by a bioinformatics postdoctoral researcher in the laboratory, and the student will follow this analytical process to gain an understanding of the computational pipeline.
This project will provide training in functional genomics and single-cell technologies, while generating proof-of-concept data to establish the feasibility of the CROP-seq screening that will ultimately feed into the virtual beta cell model for optimising SC-islet-based T1D therapies.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

The ideal candidate for this project is an undergraduate student with a background in biotechnology, molecular biology, genetics, or a related life sciences discipline. A basic understanding of molecular cloning, cell culture, and general genetics principles is desirable, though not strictly required, as full training will be provided. More important are genuine curiosity and motivation to learn hands-on wet lab techniques, including molecular cloning, lentiviral production, and cell culture, alongside a willingness to engage with the basics of dry lab work, such as understanding how single-cell sequencing data is processed and analysed. Strong attention to detail, reliability in following experimental protocols, and good communication skills are also valuable, given the collaborative nature of the project.

HOW TO APPLY

Send applications documents to the PI and Chiara Simoni – HERE

Single cell genomics and evolution – Sebé-Pedrós Lab

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – Comparing large-scale integration approaches for genome-wide expression in developmental trajectories

Single cell transcriptomics | Gene regulation | Genomics | Development | Computational biology | Systems biology

Single cell technologies have transformed our understanding of core developmental processes. Classic questions involving the nature of cell differentiation, and the extent of its conservation across animal lineages, can now be revisited with unprecedented cellular resolution by performing time-series single cell transcriptomics throughout development. To properly quantify and assess the conservation of cellular trajectories, we need to integrate (stitch) temporal atlases to relate cellular identities from consecutive stages in a rigorous way. To date, multiple approaches have been tested, but they have not been compared systematically. Here we propose a bioinformatics project to implement and compare three stitching approaches (graph-based methods using k-nearest-neighbour co-embedding, tree-based methods, and modality-specific modelling of cell-to-cell transitions) throughout animal development (one or more chordate species, like amphioxus, zebrafish, or mouse). The candidate will gain access to state-of-the-art methods and resources for analysing high-throughput single cell transcriptomics data, and their contributions will pave the way for a standardised method in large-scale comparative studies.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

We are looking for a Life Sciences BSc/MSc with an interest in gene regulation and computational biology. Ideally, the student should have a background in development, genomics, bioinformatics, and computational biology. They will require basic skills in the command line (Bash/Linux) and R, as well as basic knowledge of Python. Prior experience with R programming and/or working in a high-performance cluster (HPC) will be highly valued. Organisation skills will also be valued.

HOW TO APPLY

Send applications documents to the PI and Alberto Pérez Posada – HERE

Systems and Synthetic Biology – Latorre Lab

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – Evolutionary CpG Spatial Organisation and Mammalian Longevity 

Comparative genomics | CpG depletion | DNA methylation | Aging evolution | Bioinformatics

DNA methylation leaves a long-term evolutionary footprint on the genome sequence. Methylated cytosines at CpG dinucleotides are especially prone to mutation, contributing to CpG depletion over evolutionary time, while many regulatory regions remain comparatively CpG-rich. Previous comparative studies have linked CpG density in selected genomic regions to species lifespan and age at maturity. However, it remains unclear whether the spatial arrangement of CpGs contains information about longevity beyond their overall abundance.
This four-month project will develop a reproducible comparative-genomics workflow to measure distances between adjacent CpG sites across approximately 30-50 mammalian genomes. The student will construct empirical inter-CpG gap distributions and multiscale survival curves, then extract robust spatial descriptors and compare them with established measures. These genomic features will be integrated with publicly available lifespan, body-mass and maturity data. Phylogenetically controlled statistical models will test whether CpG spatial organisation explains variation in maximum lifespan or body-mass-adjusted longevity after accounting for shared ancestry and major technical covariates.
Mammals are used as the primary proof-of-concept because they combine broad lifespan variation with relatively comparable methylation biology, high-quality genome assemblies and well-curated life history information. If time permits, the pipeline will be tested on a small panel of non-mammalian vertebrates. The project will generate a documented analysis workflow, a quality-controlled comparative dataset and interpretable results, including the scientifically informative possibility that spatial descriptors do not outperform simpler composition metrics.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

We are looking for a BSc or MSc student interested in bioinformatics and computational biology, with an enthusiasm for genomics, evolution, or ageing research. This is a computational (bioinformatics) project involving the analysis of large-scale genomic datasets. Suitable backgrounds include bioinformatics, biology, biotechnology, genetics, computer science, or another quantitative discipline.
Basic programming experience in Python or R is desirable. Familiarity with Linux, command-line tools, Git, statistics, or genomic file formats would be an advantage, but is not essential. More important are curiosity, careful data handling, a willingness to learn, clear documentation habits, and the ability to work independently while seeking guidance when needed.
The project is well suited to either a life-science student who wants to strengthen computational and bioinformatics skills or a quantitative student who wants to gain experience in biological data analysis. Prior knowledge of DNA methylation or phylogenetic comparative methods is welcome but not required; the relevant biological concepts, bioinformatics tools, and analytical methods will be introduced during the project.

HOW TO APPLY

Send applications documents to the PI and Eric Macwan – HERE

Cell fate decoding and engineering – Lin Lab

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – Understanding neuronal diversity

Cell fate engineering | Transcription factors | Molecular cloning | Lentiviral vectors | Mammalian cell culture

Cell fate engineering holds enormous potential for both basic research and translational applications, yet current in vitro models capture only a small fraction of the neuronal diversity present in the human brain. While thousands of neuronal subtypes arise in vivo through the coordinated action of regional patterning cues and dynamic transcriptional programs, many existing engineering approaches rely on the overexpression of a limited set of transcription factors from pluripotency to directly generate specific neuronal identities. How combinations of transcription factors interact with distinct progenitor states to generate neuronal diversity is currently underexplored.
This project aims to address these limitations through a systematic transcription factor perturbation framework guided by gene regulatory network inference from human brain atlases. Candidate transcription factors will be assembled into optimized delivery vectors and introduced into regionally specified progenitor cells to investigate how developmental context shapes transcription factor-driven fate conversion. We will explore combinatorial transcription factor perturbations and seek to uncover multiple neuronal identities simultaneously and define how progenitor state and transcription factor interactions cooperate to generate cellular diversity.
Overall, this work aims to establish a scalable framework for understanding and engineering neuronal diversity, providing new insights into the developmental principles that govern cell fate specification and contributing to the generation of more physiologically relevant human neural models.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

The project is suitable for students from a range of backgrounds, as we will provide training from the ground up. More important than prior experience is motivation, curiosity, and a willingness to learn and actively integrate into the group. Previous experience in molecular cloning would be an advantage, but it is not required.

HOW TO APPLY

Probabilistic machine learning and genomics – Dias & Frazer Lab

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – Folding versus function: disentangling the molecular mechanisms of missense variants in gene-trait associations

Protein language models | Missense variants | Protein stability | Protein folding | Human genetics | UK Biobank | Variant effect prediction | Computational biology | Machine learning | Protein biophysics

Genome sequencing has grown exponentially, but determining the phenotypic consequences of missense variants remains a key challenge in human genetics. Deep-learning unsupervised methods, such as protein language models (pLM), that learn the distribution of sequence variation across organisms have emerged as promising tools for scoring variant effects. In gene-trait association studies, regression tests using pLMs find ∼50% more associations than burden tests (Jang et al., Cell Genomics 2026) and can be run directly from precomputed summary statistics (Dinh et al., Nature Methods 2026). However, pLM are trained on evolutionary data and therefore often fall short of attributing effects to specific biophysical mechanisms.We propose to integrate protein language models with folding energetics to disentangle effects on stability and on functions beyond folding, such as allostery, ligand/partner binding and downstream interactions. We will quantify and separate mutational effects on the energetics of protein folding versus natural selection by computing protein “dark energy”, defined as the difference between physical folding free energies and evolutionary free energies derived from a pLM (Galpern et al., PNAS 2026).  We will apply this biophysical decomposition to study the genotype-phenotype summary statistics from the UK Biobank as provided by Genebass (Karczewski et al., Cell Genomics 2022), focusing specifically on genes associated with blood biochemistry biomarkers. We will relate the predicted folding-stability and dark energy changes for each missense variant to the effect sizes and contrast those regressions against the gene’s putative loss-of-function (pLoF) effect. We will disentangle variants destabilizing the encoded protein from others that preserve protein stability but affect specific chemical activities. Together, this work will pave the way to a scalable framework to move beyond statistical gene–trait associations toward a residue-level, mechanistic understanding of how missense variation perturbs protein biology in human genetics.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

We are looking for a motivated master student with a background in bioinformatics, computational biology, computer science, physics, mathematics, or a related quantitative discipline. Previous programming experience in Python is expected. Familiarity with molecular biology, genetics, statistics, or machine learning is desirable but not required. The student should be curious and interested in applying computational methods to biological questions.

HOW TO APPLY

Send applications documents to the PI and Ezequiel Galpern – HERE

Systems & Synthetic Biology – MARTIN Lab

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – Understanding the effect of environmental changes on a genotype-phenotype map

Evolution | Genotype-phenotype maps | Fitness seascapes

Models of evolution using genotype-phenotype maps and the resulting fitness landscapes allow for the accurate treatment of genetic sequences and the high-dimensional structure of mutations. Improvements in both computational resources and experimental methods make it possible to study increasingly large landscapes, but there are still many unanswered questions about what structures can and do exist in real genotype spaces, and how an individual’s changing environment influences both its phenotype and fitness. This project will use computational tools to understand the effect of a changing environment on a genotype-phenotype map, and on the subsequent effect that a changing genotype-phenotype map has on evolutionary simulations.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

As an interdisciplinary field, this project will be most interesting to a student either:
– With a physics/computer science background and an interest in learning more about biology and genetics, or
– With a biology/bioinformatics background with an interest in learning more about programming and statistics.
A strong motivation to learn about new topics is essential.

HOW TO APPLY

Send applications documents to the PI and Kye Hunter – HERE

Computational Biology and Health Genomics – Bernardo Rodríguez Martín Lab

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – Mapping regulatory sequence motifs in repetitive structural variants to interpret their impact on gene regulation 

Structural variants | Long-read sequencing | Gene regulation | Mobile elements | Tandem repeats | Transcription factors | RNA binding proteins

Understanding how disease-associated variants impact gene function, and pinpointing the underlying causal variant, remains challenging despite decades of association studies like GWAS and expression QTLs. Often overlooked as the potential mechanism driving these associations are structural variants (SVs). Although SVs represent the largest source of genetic variation between human genomes by megabase pairs (Collins and Talkowski 2025), and are more likely than single nucleotide variants to be causal (Chiang et al. 2017; Bai et al. 2026), their repetitive nature makes them difficult to detect and interpret, leaving them largely understudied.
Excitingly, long-read sequencing technologies are helping bridge the gap. We recently produced the largest map of human SVs to date by analyzing 1019 long-read human genomes, detecting ~two-fold more SVs detected per genome compared to short reads and fully resolving their sequences (Schloissnig et al. 2025). Crucially, by studying the previously inaccessible internal sequence we can gain insights into their functional effects. For example, CpGs in tandem repeats, a type of SV with variable lengths across individuals, can lead to hypermethylation resulting in abnormal gene silencing in disease (Hannan 2018). Similarly, mobile element insertions often contain splice and transcription factor binding sites, leading to aberrant isoforms and ectopic oncogene expression (Payer and Burns 2019; Diaz-Portal et al. 2026).
In this project, we propose to analyze their internal sequence as a source of evidence for interpreting SVs in disease-associated loci. We have recently annotated the sequences of SVs derived from 1019 long-read human genomes from diverse populations, and found extensive variability both between repeat copies (Schloissnig et al. 2025). The student will help us make sense of these layers of variation by mapping transcription factor and RNA-binding protein binding sites within these sequences (Grant et al. 2011), and explore predictive approaches, such as AlphaGenome (Avsec et al. 2026), to link the presence of motifs with gene expression variation.
Overall, the annotations will serve as a basis to interpret the functional effects of some of the most difficult-to-study variants in the genome. These results will identify SVs likely impacting the regulation of nearby genes, and allow us to propose an underlying molecular mechanism of disease-associated loci.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

Skills: Python, Bash/command line
Knowledge: molecular biology, statistics, genomics
Background: bioinformatics, biotechnology, genomic sciences, or similar.

HOW TO APPLY

Send applications documents to the PI and Jesus Emiliano Sotelo – HERE

Evolutionary Processes Modeling – Weghorn Lab

PROJECT DESCRIPTION – How do genetic and evolutionary factors shape the immunogenic potential of cancer-associated mutations

Evolution | Neoantigen | Immunogenicity

Cancer develops through the accumulation of somatic mutations, some of which generate neoantigens that can be presented by human leukocyte antigen (HLA) molecules and recognized by T cells. These interactions may influence which mutations persist during tumour evolution, but the extent and determinants of immune-mediated selection remain unclear. Progress has been limited by the difficulty of modelling mutation probabilities, antigen presentation, and T-cell recognition with sufficient accuracy. This project will investigate how genetic and evolutionary factors shape the immunogenic potential of cancer-associated mutations. Using comparative sequence analysis, evolutionary simulations, and context-aware computational models, we will examine how variation in coding sequences affects the likelihood that somatic mutations generate peptides with the potential for immune recognition. The work will provide a broader understanding of the relationship between genome evolution, somatic mutation, and tumour immunogenicity, and may help clarify the factors that influence immune selection during cancer development.

WHO ARE WE LOOKING FOR?

A student with:
– An interest in computational biology, evolution, or cancer genomics.
– Experience in Python (or similar) and handling large datasets.
– Some familiarity with bioinformatics pipelines (preferred but not required).

Organizational Context

The International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC) is the world’s largest humanitarian network, with 191 member National Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies. IFRC uses the Triple R – response, resilience and respect – to deliver on Strategy 2030. IFRC responds to disasters and crises, ensuring timely, coordinated and locally led humanitarian action. IFRC supports its members in building community resilience in the areas of climate and environment, health and wellbeing, and migration and displacement. IFRC promotes respect for our fundamental principles of humanity, impartiality, neutrality, independence, voluntary service, unity, and universality, including in our work on values, power and inclusion. The IFRC focuses throughout on our core mandate – our raison d’être – of strategic and operational coordination, humanitarian diplomacy, National Society development, and accountability.

IFRC is led by its Secretary General and has its Headquarters in Geneva and five regional offices in Africa (Nairobi); the Americas (Panama); Asia Pacific (Kuala Lumpa); Europe (Budapest); and MENA (Beirut) as well as representation offices, service centres and delegations across the globe.

IFRC has a zero-tolerance policy on conduct that is incompatible with the aims and objectives of the Red Cross and Red Crescent Movement, including sexual exploitation and abuse, sexual harassment and other forms of harassment, abuse of authority, discrimination, and lack of integrity (including but not limited to financial misconduct). IFRC also adheres to strict child safeguarding principles.

The IFRC is currently present in Nepal through a Country Delegation (CD – first established in 1965 with a presence through regional representation at times), providing support to Nepal Red Cross Society (NRCS) programmes and National Society development (NSD) amongst as well as emergency response, other areas. The longer-term mission of the Nepal Delegation is to facilitate organisational growth, technical capacities, partnerships, and resource mobilisation that enable Nepal Red Cross Society to deliver on its humanitarian mandate in the country through the provision of technical support, advocacy, representation and coordination functions, in accordance with Strategy 2030, the IFRC Renewal and annual Operational Plans.

The Country Delegation also provides integration services to six IFRC members with a presence in Nepal.

Org. Setting and Reporting

The UN Secretary-General launched on 1 January 2019 a bold and new global reform which repositioned the UN Development System to deliver more effectively and efficiently with the achievement of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. As part of this reform, UN Resident Coordinator Offices (UN RCO), under the leadership of an empowered and independent UN Resident Coordinator – the highest-ranking official of the UN Development System and Representative of the UN Secretary-General at country level – support countries in the achievement of their development priorities and the attainment of the SDG’s. In its Resolution A/RES/72/279, the United Nations General Assembly endorsed the transformation of the Development Operations Coordination Office (DCO) as a stand-alone coordination office within the United Nations Secretariat. DCO exercises managerial and oversight functions of the resident coordinator system under the oversight of the Chair of United Nations Sustainable Development Group (UNSDG). In 2026, DCO undertook a recalibration to ensure the RC system remains optimally configured to support the acceleration of the 2030 Agenda and embodies the UN 2.0 shift-anchored in data, digital, innovation, behavioral science, strategic foresight, and a mission driven organizational culture. The Associate Data Specialist contributes to interacting with counterparts, officers and technical staff in relevant organizational units in data engineering, data science and other data specialists, data owners and subject matter experts for the development and implementation of the databases, data collection systems and data analytics that optimize statistical efficiency and quality. It also contributes to the interaction with external counterparts in the UN funds, programs and other UN specialized agencies, consultants, and NGOs other partners to collaborate and exchange information and best practices. The position is located in the United Nations Resident Coordination Office (RCO) in Kathmandu, Nepal, under the direct supervision of the Head of the Resident Coordinator Office.

Job Description

The Position:

The District Project Coordinator is a field-based project coordination position responsible for facilitating implementation of UNFPA-supported integrated sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) and gender-based violence (GBV) interventions across assigned districts and programme municipalities. The incumbent will maintain regular engagement with provincial, district and local authorities; coordinate implementing partners and service-delivery actors; monitor programme quality and results; and support timely follow-up and reporting.

The position connects municipal implementation with provincial and national level systems, institutions and policies. It will help ensure that SRHR and GBV services are planned, financed, delivered and monitored as an integrated, rights-based and government-owned system. The incumbent will work across health, social development, justice, education and protection structures, with particular attention to women, girls, adolescents, young people, persons with disabilities, LGBTQIA+ persons, Dalits and other populations left furthest behind.

The District Project Coordinator reports to the UNFPA Provincial Head. The incumbent receives technical guidance from UNFPA’s SRHR and Gender teams and collaborates closely with WHO, implementing partners and other members of the joint programme team.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The District Project Coordinator translates these outcomes into coordinated action at sub national levels. The District Project Coordinator will be working closely with local governments, district authorities, provincial government agencies, community organizations, development partners and other relevant stakeholders to ensure timely and effective delivery of planned results. The role combines policy advocacy and technical assistance, implementation coordination, service-system strengthening, community engagement, monitoring, reporting and learning, and humanitarian preparedness and response. It is expected to strengthen government ownership, mobilize co- financing from the local governments and private sector, and promote functional referral pathways and accountability for inclusive and integrated SRHR and GBV services in Nepal.

You would be responsible for:

1. Support policy advocacy, planning and budgeting process at Subnational Level

  • Provide hands-on support to assigned municipalities to integrate SRHR, GBV prevention and response, gender equality and social inclusion priorities into periodic and annual plans, sectoral plans, budgets and expenditure reviews.
  • Support evidence-based dialogue with elected representatives and government officials on mobilizing co-financing and prioritizing financial resources on integrated SRHR and GBV services, budget execution and government actions on essential services and frontline functions, including OCMCs, adolescent friendly health services, safe houses, case managers and community psychosocial services.
  • Help local governments to formulate effective laws and policy, policy implementation, and budget execution for improved access and quality and integrated SRHR and GBV services.
  • Support Municipality to harmonize the inter-departmental coordination and collaboration among the sections responsible for health, gender equality, education and finance.
  • Facilitate implementation of relevant national and subnational laws, policies, action plans, standards/SOPs and guidelines, including those related to integrated GBV and SRHR services, GESI, adolescent and youth health and humanitarian preparedness.
  • Support municipalities in implementing local-level policies and guidelines for integrated SRHR and GBV services.
  • Support municipalities to conduct periodic reviews, roll-out accountability tools and capacity building of Health Facility Operation and Management Committee on SRHR and its interlinkage with disaster GBV prevention and response.
  • Conduct advocacy activities with local government on cost sharing strategies for GBV and SRHR service provision and prioritizing gender responsive budgeting at local level.

2. Programme implementation support, coordination and quality assurance

  • Support the implementation of programme activities across assigned districts and municipalities in line with approved annual workplans, budgets, results frameworks, technical standards and partnership agreements.
  • Maintain regular liaison with local governments, district-level authorities, implementing partners, WHO, UNFPA technical and operations teams, health facilities with OCMC services, safe houses, schools, civil society organizations and community networks.
  • Provide day-to-day support to implementing partners and government counterparts in delivering planned activities, following up on implementation issues and facilitating timely completion of agreed actions.

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled.
