Location: Country Office, Kathmandu, frequent field trave- Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading

Contract type: Fixed term contract until February 28, 2026 for six month, possible of extension

Hours of work: Your normal hours of work will be 40 hours per week including recognised meal breaks. This is a full-time role; however, Oxfam offers various flexible arrangements which candidates can discuss with the Recruiting Manager at interview stage

key Responsibilities

Budgeting, Forecasting and Financial Analysis

  • Lead the preparation, review and monitoring of response project budgets in collaboration with the Response Team, relevant budget holders and Head of business support.
  • Provide timely financial analysis of actual expenditure against approved budgets, commitments and forecasts.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date project forecasts and identify potential under/overspending, funding gaps and budget risks.
  • Support budget revisions, reallocations and other financial adjustments in accordance with Oxfam and donor requirements.
  • Provide regular financial analysis and management information to the Response Team to support programme decision-making.
  • Ensure OPAL budgets and CRIMSON are accurate and aligned with approved budgets and grant agreements.
  • Work closely with Programme and Grants colleagues to ensure financial implications of programme changes are identified and addressed promptly.
  • Provide financial advice on resource utilization, value for money and the financial feasibility of response plans and proposals

Donor Financial Reporting and Grant Compliance

  • Prepare, review and coordinate timely and accurate donor financial reports in accordance with donor requirements and agreed reporting schedules.
  • Ensure donor financial reports reconcile with GL, approved project budgets and relevant supporting documentation.
  • Review expenditure eligibility against donor agreements, approved budgets and applicable Oxfam policies and procedures.
  • Provide financial information and analysis required for donor reports, proposals, budget revisions and grant amendments.
  • Maintain an effective financial reporting calendar and proactively follow up on upcoming donor financial reporting requirements.
  • Support donor audits, financial reviews and queries and ensure timely responses and follow-up of agreed actions.
  • Identify and communicate donor compliance risks to relevant Programme, Grants, Partnership and Finance teams.
  • Coordinate with DCM team and ensures Donor Contract Management Systems are updated, with up-to-date information (grant amount, duration of grant, allocation to projects, contract realignments, reporting dates).
  • Ensures monthly project budget monitoring reports are produced and provides financial information and analysis to Budget Holders to contribute on decision-making.

Programme support and Partner Financial Management

  • Assist the programme team for partners’ appraisal and review of finance report from partners to ensure that they are compliant with Oxfam and back donor’s standards and guidelines.
  • Provide financial management support throughout the partner grant/PGA lifecycle, from budget development and due diligence through implementation, monitoring, reporting and closure.
  • Review partner budgets and provide financial input to ensure proposed costs are reasonable, eligible, appropriately budgeted and aligned with donor requirements.
  • Review partner financial reports, supporting documentation and expenditure against approved PGA budgets.
  • Monitor partner expenditure, advances, liquidations and financial performance and follow up on outstanding financial issues.
  • Support Programme and Partnership colleagues in the preparation and revision of PGAs and partner budgets.
  • Communicate with programme team to ensure the OPAL Budget, update finance related information’s, do follow up and ensure the KPI issue resolution like matching figures with CRIMSON.
  • Review and process partner disbursement requests in accordance with approved agreements, financial procedures and programme requirements.
  • Ensure partner financial reports are reconciled with Oxfam records and relevant donor reporting requirements.
  • Identify financial, compliance and grant-management risks and escalate issues requiring management attention.
  • Support partner capacity strengthening in financial management, budgeting, reporting and internal controls.
  • Coordinate with Programme, Partnership, Grants and Compliance teams on partner financial management and grant-related issues.
  • Ensures all the finance transaction documents at Oxfam and partners are maintained in accordance with the Nepal audit standards and are safe till 8 years after completion of projects.
  • Support financial monitoring visits and reviews of partner organisations where required
  • Financial Transaction Management and Controls Ensure timely, accurate and compliant processing and review of financial transactions relating to the response project.
  • Review expenditure transactions to ensure they are properly authorised, adequately supported, correctly coded and charged to the appropriate project, grant and budget line.
  • Ensure project expenditure complies with Oxfam policies, donor requirements, approved budgets and applicable financial procedures.
  • Review payment requests, staff advances, partner advances, liquidations, procurement-related financial transactions and other response project expenditure.
  • Monitor outstanding advances, prepayments, accruals and other financial balances and ensure timely clearance.
  • Review and approve financial transactions within delegated authority levels.
  • Conduct regular review of project ledger transactions and identify unusual, incorrect or potentially ineligible expenditure.
  • Ensure timely reconciliation of project financial records with relevant supporting documentation and financial systems.
  • Coordinate with Finance Officers and transaction-processing teams to resolve transaction errors and outstanding issues.
  • Maintain appropriate financial documentation and audit trails for response project transactions.
  • Support month-end and project financial closure activities.
  • Ensure financial records are maintained in accordance with Oxfam, donor and applicable statutory requirements.
  • Review cash-flow requirements and support effective cash and bank management for the response project, including timely top-up and cash-flow forecasting where applicable.
  • Financial Coordination, Capacity Building and Team Support (integrated across the above responsibilities Provide guidance and coaching to Finance colleagues, response budget holders and relevant programme staff on financial policies, budgeting, donor requirements, transactions and grant financial management.
  • Contribute to training needs analysis and deliver practical finance training where required.
  • Promote strong financial controls while providing timely, solutions-oriented support to programme delivery.
  • Where the role has direct reports, manage performance, development and workload in line with Oxfam policies and values.
  • Undertake other duties reasonably assigned by the Line Manager that support effective and efficient response delivery.

skills, experience and knowledge

Essential

  • Recognized professional qualification in accounting and finance such as CA, ACCA, CIMA or MBA.
  • Comprehensive knowledge and a minimum of 5 years of proven senior level experience in financial management activities, such as: budgeting, forecasting, and reporting as well as evidence of effective decision making skills and a critical focus on the delivery of agreed results within time and budget constraints and to expected standards.
  • Strong knowledge of accounting standards, GAAP, and statutory requirements, strong numeracy skills and attention to details
  • Sound knowledge and experience of Restricted funds management and ability to work with/manage finances of multi-donor grants.
  • Strong computer literacy, and proven experience of computerized accounting packages, preferably PeopleSoft.
  • Strong analytical and conceptual thinking skills with a proactive approach to identifying and resolving problems and suggesting improvements; able to understand complex issues and translate them into simple workable actions and plans.
  • Excellent people management abilities, with motivational, talent development and change management skills. Able to manage and develop other people’s performance
  • Excellent communication skills, in written and verbal English, with strong persuasive skills.
  • Ability to build strong and credible relationships internally within Oxfam and externally with other organizations, as appropriate.
  • Ability to work in demanding situations under pressure in a team or independently with minimum supervision and delver against team objectives.
  • Proven experience as a team worker and demonstrably cooperative with members of own team, other team and partners.
  • Commitment to the aims, objectives and organizational culture of Oxfam.

Desirable

  • Knowledge or appreciation of Nepal in terms of its political, economic and social trends plus a good understanding of the key development and humanitarian issues in the Country.
  • Fluency in spoken and written local languages.
  • Willingness and ability to travel at short notice and/or to work extra hours as necessary, often in difficult circumstances

Key Attributes

  • Ability to demonstrate sensitivity to cultural differences and gender issues, as well as the commitment to equal opportunities
  • Ability to demonstrate an openness and willingness to learn about the application of gender/gender mainstreaming, women’s rights, and diversity for all aspects of development work
  • Commitment to Oxfam’s safeguarding policies to ensure all people who come into contact with Oxfam are as safe as possible

Organisational Values

  • Accountability – Our purpose-driven, results-focused approach means we take responsibility for our actions and hold ourselves accountable. We believe that others should also be held accountable for their actions
  • Empowerment – Our approach means that everyone involved with Oxfam, from our staff and supporters to people living in poverty, should feel they can make change happen
  • Inclusiveness – We are open to everyone and embrace diversity. We believe everyone has a contribution to make, regardless of visible and invisible differences

Posiiton: Emergency Finance Officer
Location: Kathmandu with frequent travel to project working areas
Position Status: Full-time, Contract

About Mercy Corps

Mercy Corps is a leading global organization powered by the belief that a better world is possible. In disaster, in hardship, in more than 40 countries around the world, we partner to put bold solutions into action — helping people triumph over adversity and build stronger communities from within. Now, and for the future.

The Program Summary

On 26 August 2026, a glacier and rockfall avalanche near the Rasuwagadhi border triggered a catastrophic debris-flow flood along the Bhotekoshi–Trishuli corridor, severely affecting Rasuwa, Nuwakot, and Dhading, districts. Search and rescue operations led by NDRRMA and other responders are ongoing. The disaster has resulted in significant loss of life, injuries, displacement, and extensive damage to infrastructure and livelihoods. Thousands of affected people are facing critical shortages of shelter, water, food, and sanitation supplies. Mercy Corps Nepal is responding to the disaster supporting the affected families with immediate relief and enabling recovery.

The Position (General Position Summary)

The Emergency Finance Officer is responsible for supporting day to day financial operations of the emergency response project ensuring accuracy, timeliness and compliance with Mercy Corps Nepal policiesand regulatory requirements. This position is responsible for processing payments, managing bank-related activities, maintaining accurate accounting records in the financial system, and supporting month-end reconciliations and work closely with partner organization ensuring financial management of partner organization.

Essential Job Responsibilities
The specific duties and responsibilities of the Emergency Finance Officer include, but are not limited to, the following:

FINANCE MANAGEMENT

  • Manage day to day financial operations of the project ensuring compliance with Mercy Corps Nepal policies and other regulatory requirements.
  • Prepare cash flows, monitor project expenditures, and ensure sufficient liquidity for field operations.
  • Process payments, advances and settlements and maintain accurate accounting records and supporting documentation.
  • Manage bank-related correspondence including signatory updates and other communication.
  • Conduct day-to-day data entries into Accounting Software Navigator, ensuring data accuracy and compliance with applicable policies and guidelines.
  • File all vouchers and supporting documents and support proper maintenance of project-related files archive.
  • Review partner/sub-recipient Fund Transfer requests and reconcile with partner financial reports and Navigator data.
  • Prepare photocopies, scans, and other required supporting documents for monthly reporting packages to HQ Finance.
  • Ensure financial management of partner organization and support on financial management capacity building.

COMPLIANCE AND RISK MANAGEMENT

  • Ensure compliance with donor requirements and organizational policies.
  • Support internal and external audits.

COORDINATION AND REPORTING

  • Conduct regular budget monitoring and provides budget Vs expenses analysis to the emergency response coordinator.
  • Support the Interim Senior Finance and Compliance Coordinator in preparation of financial reports, forecasts, and donor financial documentation.
  • Participate in project planning, coordination meetings and emergency response activities as required.
  • Prepare monthly Cash and Bank Reconciliations and get them approved and filed as required.

SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
  • Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
  • Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

Supervisory Responsibility: N/A

Accountability

Reports Directly To: Interim Senior Finance and Compliance Coordinator

Works Directly With: Emergency Response Coordinator and project technical partner team members as required.

Accountability to Participants and Stakeholders

Mercy Corps team members are expected to support all efforts toward accountability, specifically to our program participants, community partners, other stakeholders, and to international standards guiding international relief and development work. We are committed to actively engaging communities as equal partners in the design, monitoring and evaluation of our field projects.

Minimum Qualification & Transferable Skills

  • Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in accounting/ financial management or a relevant business field.
  • Minimum of 3-5 years of relevant experience in finance and accounting. Working experience with I/NGOs is preferred.
  • Knowledge of GoN tax regulations, VAT, and TDS requirements.
  • Demonstrated attention to detail, ability to follow procedures, meet deadlines, and work independently and cooperatively with team members.
  • Proficiency in MS Office programs, particularly Excel and financial/accounting software.
  • Excellent coordination and communication skills.
  • Strong planning, organizational, and reporting skills.
  • Ability to work effectively with an ethnically diverse team in a sensitive environment.
  • Experience in emergency response or disaster management is preferred.

Success Factors

A successful Finance officer should have a clear understanding of finance and procurement ethics as well as the willingness and ability to enforce compliance with Mercy Corps and donor policies and procedures is essential. A demonstrated ability to work quickly and accurately, meet deadlines, and process information in support of changing program activities is necessary. Multi-tasking, prioritizing, problem-solving and simultaneous attention to detail are essential.

S/he will have proven ability to learn quickly, take initiative, and be accountable for results, with an ability and willingness to remain mobile for short-term and/or long-term as necessary within the region, based on programmatic needs. An ability to work independently and as part of a team, with curiosity about and sensitivity to new cultures, a desire and ability to learn and grow, both personally and professionally, and a great sense of humor.

The most successful Mercy Corps team members have a strong commitment to teamwork and accountability, thrive in evolving and changing environments and make effective written and verbal communication a priority in all situations.

Living Conditions / Environmental Conditions

The position is based in Kathmandu, Nepal and it requires up to 40% travel to support country programs, which may include travel to insecure locations where freedom of movement is limited and areas where amenities are limited.

Ongoing Learning

In support of our belief that learning organizations are more effective, efficient and relevant to the communities we serve, we empower all team members to dedicate 5% of their time to learning activities that further their personal and/or professional growth and development.

Team Engagement and Effectiveness

Achieving our mission starts with how we build our team and collaborate. By bringing together individuals with a variety of experiences, backgrounds, and perspectives, we strengthen our ability to solve complex challenges and drive innovation. We foster a culture of trust and respect, where every team member is valued for their contributions, empowered to reach their full potential, and motivated to do their best work.

We recognize that building a strong and effective team is an ongoing process, and we remain committed to learning, improving, and growing together.

Equal Employment Opportunity

Mercy Corps is an equal opportunity employer committed to providing equal employment opportunities to all employees and qualified applicants for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, religion or belief, national origin, age, disability, marital status, veteran status, or any other characteristics protected under applicable law.

Safeguarding & Ethics

Mercy Corps is committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants or others, are treated with respect and dignity. We are committed to the core principles regarding prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the UN Secretary General and IASC and have signed on to The Misconduct Disclosure Scheme. We will not tolerate child abuse, sexual exploitation, abuse, or harassment by or of our team members. As part of our commitment to a safe and inclusive work environment, team members are expected to conduct themselves in a professional manner, respect local laws and customs, and to adhere to Mercy Corps Code of Conduct Policies and values at all times. Team members are required to complete mandatory Code of Conduct elearning courses upon hire and on an annual basis.

As an applicant, if you witness or experience any form of sexual misconduct during the recruitment process, please report this to Mercy Corps Integrity Hotline (integrityhotline@mercycorps.org).

The MEL and Communication Officer support Mercy Corps Nepal’s Emergency Response Program by ensuring monitoring, evaluation and learning systems meet organizational standards, and that program results, learning and best practices are effectively documented and communicated to internal and external stakeholders. Essential Job Responsibilities

The specific duties and responsibilities of the MEL and Communications Officer include, but are not limited to, the following:

ASSESSMENT AND MONITORING

  • Support/lead Rapid Needs Assessments (RNA) and contribute to Multi-Sectoral Needs Assessments (MSNA) to inform targeting and response design.
  • Conduct real-time monitoring of response activities against targets, flagging targeting errors, pipeline breaks, or access gaps for immediate correction.
  • Design and conduct Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) for cash and in-kind assistance, verifying timeliness, amounts received, use, and continued relevance of transfer values against market prices.
  • Develop compressed, workable MEL frameworks appropriate to the response timeline, and facilitate After Action Reviews (AARs) to document lessons for subsequent response phases.
  • Ensure Mercy Corps’ MEL minimum standards are rolled out and followed across the project/program.
  • Build project team capacity on MEL systems, tools and standards.
  • Plan and facilitate learning events and support thematic teams in capturing and synthesizing field-level learning.

DATA COLLECTION AND QUALITY

  • Design and deploy lean, digital-where-feasible data collection tools appropriate to the acute response phase.
  • Conduct data quality checks and spot verification to ensure reported figures are accurate and defensible.
  • Apply data protection protocols appropriate to the heightened vulnerability of affected populations, including consent and secure storage of PII.

ACCOUNTABILITY

  • Work closely with Country CARM focal person to establish and manage Community Accountability and Response Mechanism (CARM), ensuring safeguarding and protection concerns are identified and referred immediately.
  • Ensure community feedback reaches decisionmakers and informs response adjustments in real time.

COORDINATION AND REPORTING

  • Contribute to 4W/5W coordination reporting to relevant clusters and government entities to avoid duplication and coverage gaps.
  • Track output indicators against cluster standards and produce timely situation reports and donor updates in required formats and timeline.
  • Support Emergency Response Coordinator to prepare periodic progress updates, reports and stories, in collaboration project team, ensuring government and donor compliance.
  • Review project guidelines, documents and resource materials, and prepare shareable resources aligned with Mercy Corps’ and donors’ branding guidelines.

COMMUNICATION AND KNOWLEDGE MANAGEMENT

  • Develop and implement a communication plan to document and disseminate program processes and results to stakeholders.
  • Prepare clear, concise, and compelling reports, presentations and communication materials, and manage internal and external communication channels.
  • Identify and engage key audiences donors, participants and partners through targeted communication strategies and build media relationships to secure positive coverage.
  • Serve as a technical lead for communication and knowledge management, designing and implementing effective tools and mechanisms with the wider team.
  • Capture and document program learning and best practices and organize best-practice-sharing workshops and knowledge products for internal and external audiences.
  • Ensure all communications, outreach and visibility materials comply with the Mercy Corps Nepal Branding Guideline.
  • Collect, structure and maintain project information including a standard information package for internal, external, government and media audiences, ensuring materials remain current and accessible.

SAFEGUARDING RESPONSIBILITIES

  • Actively learns about safeguarding and integrates it into their work, including safeguarding risks and mitigations related to their area of work.
  • Practices the values of Mercy Corps including respecting the dignity and well-being of participants and fellow team members.
  • Encourages openness and communication in their team; encourages team members to submit reports if they have any concerns using reporting mechanisms e.g., Integrity Hotline and other options.

Works Directly With: Country MEL focal person, CARM Focal person, and partner’s team members.

Position: Operations and Compliance Analyst, Kathmandu, Nepal, NO-A
Job Identification: 36734
Apply Before: 09/30/2026, 11:59 PM
Job Schedule: Full time
Location: Kathmandu, Nepal
Grade: NOA
Vacancy Type: Fixed Term
Rotational/Non Rotational: Non-Rotational
Contract Duration: 1 Year with Possibility for extension
Required Languages: Fluency in oral and written English and national language of the duty station.

Job Description

The Position:

The Operations and Compliance Analyst provides support on financial management, assurance activities, and financial reporting and will provide dedicated operational support to facilitate the implementation and delivery of projects. The Position provides guidance, technical support, and oversight ensuring that resources are utilized appropriately and in compliance with relevant policies and requirements.

The selected candidate will be based at the UNFPA country office, Kathmandu, and will work under the guidance and direct supervision of the International Operations Manager. The Operations and Compliance Analyst will work closely with and will support UNFPA programme officers and the operations team, to ensure major risks and compliance are managed appropriately and programmes are implemented effectively.

How you can make a difference:

UNFPA is the lead United Nations agency for delivering a world where every pregnancy is intended, every childbirth is safe, and every young person’s potential is fulfilled. The UNFPA Strategic Plan for 2026-2029 articulates the organization’s response to a complex global environment, providing a roadmap for resilience and renewal. It is designed to accelerate the implementation of the Programme of Action of the International Conference on Population and Development (ICPD) and the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals by 2030. This mandate is pursued through a focus on four interconnected outcomes: ending the unmet need for family planning; ending preventable maternal deaths; ending gender-based violence and harmful practices; and adapting to demographic change through evidence and rights-based policies.

In a world where fundamental human rights are at risk, we need principled and ethical staff who embody these international norms and standards and will defend them courageously and with full conviction.

UNFPA is seeking candidates who transform, inspire, and deliver high-impact sustained results, ensuring effective external relations, communications, partnership-building and resource mobilization in a rapidly changing development and funding landscape. We need staff who are transparent, exceptional in how they manage the resources entrusted to them, and who commit to delivering excellence in programme results

Job Purpose:

The position will play a supportive role for smooth running of financial, internal control, assurance, oversight, and audit functions ensuring compliance with corporate policies, rules, and regulations at all levels. Based on the close relationships built with internal and external stakeholders, the incumbent will assist the office to regularly communicate and support implementation of best practices in financial management and accountability tasks. The position will assist the office in budget and expenditure analysis, programme delivery monitoring, operational performance tracking, and management reporting to facilitate evidence-based planning, decision-making, and effective implementation of the country programme. The position will also support management decision-making through analysis of programme performance, operational trends, and compliance risks.

You would be responsible for:

Operational effectiveness, programme compliance, risk management, and quality assurance:

  • Support quality assurance reviews of compliance processes, including follow-up on audit recommendations, management responses and internal oversight findings.
  • Support in ERM related activities for the country office.
  • Support the development and implementation of oversight mechanisms for Country Office operations.
  • Support the assessment of the Internal Control Framework and assist in identifying internal control weaknesses, gaps, inefficiencies and overlaps.
  • Support the identification of deviations from established rules and regulations and bring them to the attention of the International Operations Manager for appropriate follow-up.
  • Support analysis of programme delivery, expenditure trends, implementation rates, and operational performance and provide inputs to identify bottlenecks and possible corrective actions.
  • Support in preparing periodic compliance, assurance, risk management, and operational performance reports and dashboards for Country Office management to support decision-making and strategic oversight.

Support to Implementing Partners Oversight and HACT assurance plan:

  • Support in conducting periodic due diligence for vetting of IPs.
  • Support the assessment of implementing partner risks and contribute to the identification of appropriate mitigation measures under the guidance of the International Operations Manager.
  • Assist in checking accuracy and validity of signatories and bank accounts in the IP agreement, with particular attention to high-risk management areas, such as sub-contracting, procurement, cash management.
  • Assist in the implementation of the approved HACT Assurance Plan under the guidance of the International Operations Manager.
  • Support the implementation of quarterly financial monitoring, in close coordination with relevant Programme Units and Area Offices and assist in validating the completion of programme activities as reported by IPs.
  • Support conduct spot checks and compliance reviews of IPs to ensure that financial, procurement and HR processes are in line with IPs established procedures and the requirements of HACT.
  • Support the review of audit reports and assist in documenting agreed follow-up actions in coordination with programme staff, implementing partners and auditors.
  • Support the review of findings from assessments, monitoring, verification, spot checks and audits, and assist in tracking follow-up actions and implementation of agreed mitigation measures.
  • Support in the regular updating of the United Nations Programme Portal (UNPP) platform by taking care of uploading all required documents and ensuring the quality of the information within it.

Programme Performance Monitoring and Financial Oversight:

  • Support to ensure alignment between approved cash limits and work plan budgets. Provide inputs from a finance and compliance perspective, supporting the accurate allocation of direct and indirect costs, and ensuring that all budgeted items reflect eligible expenditures in line with UNFPA financial guidelines.
  • Support the programme and finance team on timely and accurate review and clearance of work plans and eFace reports, ensuring compliance with UNFPA guidelines.
  • Support the finance team in the OFA reconciliation process avoiding negative OFAs at the end of the year.
  • Contributes to reviews, annual planning exercises, audits, and oversight processes through data analysis and operational reporting.
  • Support the development and maintenance of operational dashboards and tracking tools to strengthen accountability, transparency, and results-based management.

Performing Additional Duties as Assigned:

  • Carry out additional administrative and support tasks as required by UNFPA leadership.
  • Collaborates with team members, programme partners, and sub-grantees to ensure safe implementation of programmes at the community level applying Do No Harm approach.

Qualifications and Experience:

Education:

  • Advanced university degree in Finance/Accounting, Business, or Public Administration or a related field.

Knowledge and Experience:

  • Professional experience in finance or audit, or other directly related fields is advantageous.
  • Experience in the usage of computers and office software packages (MS Word, Excel, etc) and advanced knowledge of spreadsheet and database packages, experience in handling web-based management systems and ERP financials.
  • Prior experience in working with ERP systems (preferably Oracle based) is an advantage.
  • Previous experience in the UN and knowledge of UN internal control, risk management and implementing partner procedures is advantageous.
  • Excellent organizational skills, attention to detail, precision, and accuracy.
  • Strong verbal and written communication skills.
  • Should also possess the ability to formulate business requirements into logical system specifications.
  • Must be able to work in harmony across teams, both internally and externally.

Languages: Fluency in oral and written English and national language of the duty station.

Required Competencies:

Values:

  • Exemplifying integrity,
  • Demonstrating commitment to UNFPA and the UN system,
  • Embracing cultural diversity,
  • Embracing change.

ABOUT THE FRED HOLLOWS FOUNDATION

The Fred Hollows Foundation is an international development organisation working to prevent blindness and restore sight. We continue to carry on the legacy of Professor Fred Hollows, who believed every person had the right to quality eye care, no matter where they live. The Foundation is known around the world as an organisation that works with purpose and determination. With a reputation for excellence, we are well known for making change happen.

The Foundation has grown to work in more than 25+ countries throughout Africa, South Asia, Southeast Asia, the Middle East and the Pacific, as well as Australia. The Foundation has restored sight to more than 3 million people worldwide. We have an ambitious five-year strategic plan that aims to take us even closer to realising our vision of a world in which no person is needlessly blind, or vision impaired and Indigenous Australians exercise their right to sight and good health. To find out more about our work, please visit our website https://www.hollows.org

ANSAB has been consistently evolving, consolidating, institutionalizing and advancing the approaches and strategies for the promotion of community-based enterprises and value chains, natural resources management and biodiversity conservation, enabling policy environment and multi-stakeholders.

ANSAB is urgently seeking to recruit a qualified, dynamic, and results-oriented individual for the position of Forest Officer under a project entitled “Scaling Conservation of Himalayan Plants and Fungi through Sustainable Trade”.

The forest officer, based in Darchula, will be responsible for the efficient and timely execution of project activities at Darchula and Bajhang districts. QUALIFICATION AND SKILLS

How can you make a difference?

UNICEF Nepal’s Education Section works with the Government of Nepal and development partners to improve access, equity, quality, governance and resilience in school education. The School Education Sector Plan (SESP) 2022-2032 is entering a decisive transition: a realistic and costed second five-year programme for 2027-2032 and a successor Joint Financing Arrangement must be developed while foundational learning, digitalization, inclusive education and federal service delivery are translated into practical sector arrangements. From August 2026, UNICEF serves as the Development Partner focal point, with the Embassy of Finland as co-focal point, creating a time-bound need for strong coordination, analysis, representation and follow-up. The role will also help inform the Local Education Development Partner Group of the work done through the Nepal Education Cluster in terms of the response and early-recovery work following the August 2026 floods.

Join UNICEF Nepal’s Education Section to support the country’s long-standing sector-wide approach at a decisive transition. You will help UNICEF in undertaking its Development Partner focal-point responsibilities, coordinate closely with the Ministry of Education and Sports and the Embassy of Finland, and connect sector dialogue with UNICEF programme and field evidence.

Your key functions and accountabilities will cover:

  • UNICEF core-team and focal-point coordination. Support planning, preparation and follow-up for UNICEF’s engagement with Government, Joint Financing Partners, LEDPG/LEG members and other stakeholders; maintain day-to-day coordination with MoES DACS and the Embassy of Finland; and prepare calendars, agendas, briefs, speaking points, meeting records, decision logs and action trackers.
  • Support to the second SESP programme (2027-2032). Coordinate UNICEF inputs to the Government-led roadmap, evidence review, consultations, drafting and decision calendar; promote foundational learning; facilitate meaningful federal, provincial and local consultation; and synthesize specialist inputs.
  • Support to the successor Joint Financing Arrangement. Organize UNICEF and partner contributions to the review and successor dialogue, improve the visibility of partner financing, coordinate specialist advice and maintain consultation records, comment matrices and action trackers.
  • Subnational participation and accountability. Help provincial education plans, Local Education Plans, budgets, implementation monitoring and frontline learning evidence inform federal dialogue, joint reviews and SESP II design.
  • Programme management, communication and risk management. Maintain an agreed workplan and milestones, provide decision-oriented analysis, identify and escalate risks, coordinate with UNICEF programme and operations colleagues and field offices, and undertake authorized official travel.
  • Education response and early recovery. Support regular updates to the LEDPG and coordination of response and early-recovery initiatives so that evidence and lessons from flood-affected areas inform joint sector reviews and planning.

The Senior Coordinator, Child Protection will lead the implementation, coordination, monitoring, and technical oversight of child protection interventions within the flood response programs. The role will carry out child protection analysis, information management, and reporting while ensuring adherence to safeguarding, child rights, and humanitarian standards.

Creativity:

Position: Inclusive Humanitarian Lead
Employment type: Full-time: fixed-term contract of twelve months

Reports to: Director, Nepal Association of the Blind
Salary: NPR 100,000 per month (gross)
Apply before: 15th September 2026

Background

Nepal Association of the Blind (NAB) is the national umbrella organization of blind and partially sighted people in Nepal. NAB works to promote the rights, inclusion, and empowerment of people with visual impairments through advocacy, capacity building, and service delivery. The Nepal Association of the Blind (NAB), with support from the Norwegian Association of Blind and Partially Sighted (NABP), is implementing Restoring Independence, a twelve-month disability-inclusive response to the August 2026 Bhote Koshi–Trishuli floods in Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading. NAB invites applications from qualified Nepali citizens for the following position.

Major Responsibilities

  • Lead the planning, implementation, budgeting and quality assurance of the project, and supervise the project team.
  • Lead the accessible needs assessment, ensure disability-disaggregated data using the Washington Group Questions, and produce the assessment report for NDRRMA and NABP.
  • Oversee accessible referral, individual need-based support and community-based psychosocial counselling for persons with disabilities.
  • Represent NAB with NDRRMA, local governments, NFDN, local OPDs and the humanitarian clusters, and advocate for disability-inclusive help desks and an accessible disaster response hotline.
  • Lead orientation on disability-inclusive disaster risk reduction, the DIDRR manual and accessible IEC materials.
  • Ensure compliance with NAB’s safeguarding and PSEAH policies, and prepare timely narrative and financial reports.

Required Qualifications

  • Master’s degree in social sciences, development studies, disaster risk management, public health, social work or a related field. A Bachelor’s degree with strong additional experience may be considered.
  • At least five years’ experience in humanitarian response, disaster risk reduction or development programming in Nepal, including two years in a leadership or project management role.
  • Demonstrated experience of disability inclusion, or of working with or within organizations of persons with disabilities.
  • Working knowledge of the UNCRPD, the Act Relating to Rights of Persons with Disabilities 2074, the Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Act 2074, and the IASC Guidelines on Inclusion of Persons with Disabilities in Humanitarian Action.
  • Excellent written and spoken Nepali and English, strong report writing and team management skills, and computer proficiency.
  • Willingness to travel and work in flood-affected areas under difficult conditions.
  • A valid driving license for a two-wheeler or four-wheeler will be an advantage/preference, given the frequent travel to flood-affected areas.

The UN Secretary-General launched on 1 January 2019 a bold and new global reform which repositioned the UN Development System to deliver more effectively and efficiently the achievement of the 2030 Agenda and the Sustainable Development Goals. As part of this reform, UN Resident Coordinator Offices (UN RCO), under the leadership of an empowered and independent UN Resident Coordinator, support countries in the achievement of their development priorities and the attainment of the SDGs. The position is located in the United Nations Resident Coordination Office (RCO) in Kathmandu, Nepal. Under the direct supervision of the Head of Office and guidance of the RC and in full confidentiality, the Executive Assistant ensures effective and efficient functioning of the RC Front-Office, overall management of the RC’s schedule and logistical requirements, maintenance of protocol procedures, management of information flow, and follow-up on deadlines and commitments made.

Responsibilities

Within delegated authority, the Executive Assistant will be responsible for the following duties:

1. ENSURE EFFECTIVE AND EFFICIENT FUNCTIONING OF THE RC FRONT OFFICE FOCUSING ON ACHIEVEMENT OF THE FOLLOWING RESULTS:

  •  Maintain the Resident Coordinator’s calendar and representation schedule, arrange appointments and meetings of the RC, provide protocol coverage, ensure logistical details of RC participation in events, and act as an interpreter and/or taking minutes of meetings when required.
  •  Coordinate high-quality briefing materials for the RC for appointments, meetings, events, and missions and ensure that all correspondence and documents submitted to the RC are according to UN norms and standards including directives, coordinate comments on behalf of RC for signature and action/follow-up when required.
  •  Draft key correspondence, including notes to files, minutes of meetings and Note Verbales, and provide translation for official correspondence.
  • Prioritize tasks, meeting deadlines, and managing executive schedules effectively.
  • Anticipate issues and resolve them before they affect the executive’s work.
  • Manage RC travel and missions, prepare travel requests, ensure flight bookings and provision of logistics information, and follow up on trip reports and travel claims.
  • Maintain contact lists of high-level partners, UN Agencies, and Diplomatic Corps.
  •  Assist in organizing official events: travel (booking flights, request for security clearance, arrangements at airport, etc.) for local and high-level visitors as required.
  •  In collaboration with the RCO team, prepare and maintain checklists and templates for relevant processes (high level visits, meetings preparation etc).
  •  Provide all similar services and support to RC a.i.
  •  Remain effective in fast-changing environments and shifting priorities.
  •  Act as a trusted partner who anticipates needs and helps executives stay focused on priorities.

2. ENSURE PROVISION OF EFFECTIVE COMMUNICATIONS SUPPORT TO THE OFFICE FOCUSING ON THE ACHIEVEMENT OF THE FOLLOWING RESULTS:

  • Demonstrated ability to communicate clearly, professionally, and effectively, both orally and in writing, with internal and external stakeholders at all levels.
  • Handle sensitive information with professionalism and trustworthiness.
  • Have proven track record of strong working relationships with government and other external partners including ability to build strong relationships with colleagues, especially decision makers.
  • Maintain the filing system (in TEAMS/Sharepoint) ensuring safekeeping of confidential materials. Use of automated filing system.
  •  Screen RC incoming calls and correspondence.
  • Demonstrate ability to use AI, Strong skills in Microsoft 365, Teams, Outlook, Excel, PowerPoint, and collaboration tools.
  • Coordinate the activities of the RC driver.
  •  Support organize and communicate on the various coordination meetings, including UNCT Meetings.
  • Participate in the organization of official UN Days, public events, joint UN events and provide secretariat and administrative support to the UNCT
  • Follow up on deadlines, commitments made, actions taken and coordination of collection and submission of the reports to RC.

3. HUMAN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT:

  • Provide support to the RC in matters such as documentation, visas, travel arrangements, house and school search, etc.

4. OFFICE ADMINISTRATION:

  • Act as an alternate to the RCO Administrative Assistant when required to support RCO in day to-day administrative tasks as required, including contract administration, budget and finance, and human resource management.
  •  Assists with the collection and analysis of data as well as preparation of data presentations and reports for information sharing, responding to queries, knowledge management, planning and decision making.
  •  Assists with visualizations and updating information material such as web pages or brochures.
  •  Ensures that requirements and background information used for data analysis are documented.
  • Performs other relevant duties as assigned.

Competencies

Professionalism:

Ability to perform a broad range of administrative functions, e.g., budget/work programme, human resources, database management, etc.

Ability to apply knowledge of various United Nations administrative, financial and human resources rules and regulations in work situations.
Ability to apply sustainable development theories, concepts and approaches.
Ability to conduct independent research and analysis on sustainable development topics, determine suitability, validity and accuracy of data provided by different sources.
Shows skill in developing sources for data collection.
Shows pride in work and in achievements; demonstrates professional competence and mastery of subject matter; is conscientious and efficient in meeting commitments, observing deadlines and achieving results; is motivated by professional rather than personal concerns; shows persistence when faced with difficult problems or challenges; remains calm in stressful situations; commitment to implementing the goal of gender equality by ensuring the equal participation and full involvement of women and men in all aspects of work.

Communication: Speaks and writes clearly and effectively; listens to others, correctly interprets messages from others and responds appropriately; asks questions to clarify, and exhibits interest in having two-way communication; tailors language, tone, style and format to match audience; demonstrates openness In sharing information and keeping people informed.

Teamwork: Works collaboratively with colleagues to achieve organizational goals; solicits input by genuinely valuing others’ ideas and expertise; is willing to learn from others; places team agenda before personal agenda; supports and acts in accordance with final group decision, even when such decisions may not entirely reflect own position; shares credit for team accomplishments and accepts joint responsibility for team shortcomings.

Education

  • Completion of a High school diploma or equivalent is required. Bachelors or advanced university degree in business administration, office management, communication or related fields would be an advantage.

Work Experience

  • A minimum of seven (7) years of experience in administrative support, coordination, logistics or front office functions is required.
  • The minimum years of relevant experience is reduced by two (2) years for candidates who possess a first level University degree.
  • Demonstrated experience in supporting senior officials or executive offices, including protocol arrangements is desirable.
  • Demonstrated experience in organizing meetings, missions and high-level events, including coordination with internal and external stakeholders is desirable.
  • Work experience with the United Nations, international organization, diplomatic mission or government institution is desirable.
  • One(1) year or more of experience in data analytics or related area is desirable.

Posiiton: Lab In-Charge
Required Number: 1
Location: Surkhet
Qualification: M.Sc. MLT/BMLT with valid NHPC License
Experience: 4-5 Years in Related Field

Job Description:

Key Responsibilities:

1. Internal Inventory Management

Oversee and manage the inventory of laboratory supplies, reagents, and equipment, ensuring stock levels are maintained and efficiently utilized to prevent shortages of overstocking.

2. Instrument and Reagent Optimization

Ensure optimal utilization of laboratory instruments and reagents to maximize efficiency and minimize waste, while maintaining the accuracy and quality of test results.

3. NABL (ISO 15189:2022) Compliance

Conduct and maintain laboratory practices in strict adherence to NABL (ISO 15189:2022) standards, ensuring that all processes, documentation, and operations meet accreditation requirements.

4.Quality Control and Assurance

Implement and monitor quality control procedures, including performing daily internal control runs and analyzing Levey-Jennings (LJ) curves. Take corrective actions when needed and document all steps to ensure accurate and reliable test results.

5. Turnaround Time (TAT) Management

Monitor and manage the turnaround time (TAT) for all laboratory services, ensuring timely processing, analysis, and reporting of test results to maintain operational efficiency.

6. Equipment Maintenance and Troubleshooting

Conduct daily maintenance of laboratory instruments, perform necessary repairs, and ensure timely validation to prevent malfunctions. Document maintenance activities and address issues promptly.

7. Data Management and Documentation

Accurately record and manage test results, ensuring that comprehensive and organized documentation is maintained in line with regulatory and organizational standards, including recording re-runs and corrective actions taken.

8. Training and Mentorship

Provide training and guidance to junior staff and interns, ensuring they are well-versed in laboratory procedures, quality control practices, and safety protocols.

9. Staff Management and Duty Rosters

Manage duty rosters for lab staff to ensure adequate coverage, maintain smooth workflow, and promote a positive working environment that fosters teamwork, communication, and high morale.

10. Lab Operations Management

Oversee the overall management of the lab, ensuring smooth day-to-day operations.

Resolve any issues that arise while promoting continuous improvement and enhancing patient engagement and service utilization.

11. Patient Interaction

When necessary, interact with patients to collect samples, provide clear instructions, ensure their comfort during procedures, and offer post-report counseling as needed.

12. Safety and Regulatory Compliance

Adhere to all safety guidelines and regulations, ensuring a safe working environment for all laboratory personnel while maintaining compliance with health and safety standards.

13. Quality System Improvement

Recommend improvements to the quality management system and testing kits to the Head of Department (HOD) for better performance, accuracy, and patient care.

14. Analytics and Management Reporting

Analyze lab performance data, including test volumes, error rates, and TAT. Prepare regular management reports on key performance indicators (KPIs), financial metrics, and quality improvement initiatives. Use data-driven insights to enhance lab efficiency and decision-making. Report to management on weekly basis.

15. Budget Management

Assist in managing the lab’s budget, ensuring optimal allocation of resources, controlling expenses, and contributing to the financial health of the department.

16. External Vendor and Supplier Management

Liaise with external suppliers and service providers for equipment procurement, reagent supplies, and outsourced services. Negotiate contracts and ensure timely deliveries while maintaining quality and cost-effectiveness.

17. Audit Preparation and Compliance

Coordinate with internal and external auditors to prepare for laboratory audits. Ensure all documentation and processes meet the required standards for NABL and ISO compliance.

18. Strategic Planning and Development

Contribute to the strategic planning of the laboratory by identifying new technologies, methodologies, and services that can enhance lab performance and patient care. Assist in long-term goal setting and resource planning.

Position: Induction Furnace Manager
Location: Pokhariya, Birgunj, Parsa, Narayani, Nepal
Reports to: Head – Meltshop

Role Summary

The Induction Furnace Manager owns the complete performance of the Steel Melting Shop (SMS) induction furnace operations, from heat planning to tapping, ensuring consistent achievement of production targets, optimal power consumption, and strict metallurgical quality control.
This role demands a hands-on leader capable of setting up disciplined furnace operations, stabilizing processes, and driving efficiency in a greenfield/startup plant environment. The incumbent will play a critical role in building systems, training teams, and establishing benchmarks for productivity, cost, and safety.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end induction furnace operations, including melting, refining, and tapping cycles
  •  Develop and execute heat plans, tapping schedules, and furnace campaign strategies
  •  Drive power panel optimization to achieve best-in-class energy consumption (kWh/tonne)
  • Ensure precise alloy addition control to meet required chemistry and minimize rework
  •  Oversee charge mix optimization (scrap, sponge iron, alloys) to improve yield and reduce cost
  •  Manage refractory lifecycle, including lining practices, performance monitoring, and procurement
  •  Coordinate closely with charge preparation, maintenance, and quality teams for seamless operations
  • Lead shift scheduling, manpower deployment, and productivity management on the shop floor
  •  Troubleshoot electrical, mechanical, and process issues affecting furnace performance
  •  Establish and monitor process control parameters including temperature, slag chemistry, and melt time
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives to reduce downtime, improve yield, and stabilize operations
  •  Ensure strict adherence to safety standards and incident prevention protocols
  •  Maintain accurate production reporting, heat logs, and performance analysis

Technical Expertise Required

  •  Strong hands-on experience in induction furnace operations (medium/high frequency)
  • Deep understanding of metallurgy: scrap behavior, alloying, slag control, and temperature management
  •  Proven track record in power consumption optimization (kWh/tonne reduction)
  •  Expertise in refractory management, lining practices, and campaign life improvement
  •  Knowledge of furnace power systems and panel operations
  • Experience in charge mix design and yield improvement techniques
  • Familiarity with pollution control and compliance norms in SMS operations

Key Performance Indicators (KPIs)

  • Achievement of daily induction furnace production targets
  • Power consumption (kWh per tonne)
  • Refractory cost per tonne and campaign life
  •  Chemistry compliance rate (first-time right heats)
  •  Tapping temperature accuracy
  • Reduction in downtime and process deviations
  • Improvement in yield and material efficiency

Minimum Qualifications & Experience

  • B.Tech in Metallurgy (preferred) or relevant engineering discipline
  • Minimum 10 years of hands-on experience in induction furnace operations
  •  Strong experience in:
    o Refractory management
    o Charge mix optimization
    o Meltshop process control
  • Prior exposure to plant setup, commissioning, or startup operations will be a strong advantage

Leadership Expectations

  •  Strong shop-floor ownership with a bias for action
  • Ability to build, train, and lead teams from the ground up
  •  Decisive problem-solving in high-pressure production environments
  •  High accountability for output, cost, quality, and safety metrics
  •  Willingness to work in a startup plant setup with evolving systems and processes

What We Are Looking For

A results-driven furnace expert who doesn’t just manage operations but builds and stabilizes them—someone who understands the realities of the shop floor, can optimize every heat, and is committed to delivering consistent performance from day one.

Interested candidates may send their CV to: hr@primesteel.com.np

Description

iDE is an international nonprofit organisation dedicated to ending poverty. Our work in agriculture, sanitation, climate change resilience, and gender equality stands out because we don’t simply hand out handouts. Instead, iDE believes in powering small-scale entrepreneurs and building robust market ecosystems that lay the groundwork for low-income and marginalised people to prosper on their own terms. iDE currently works in 11 developing countries, with over 500 staff spread around the globe. To date, iDE has impacted more than 40 million people.

Since 1992, iDE Nepal has been actively fostering prosperity by establishing value chains and innovative business models in key sectors, including agriculture, nutrition, market systems development, water and sanitation, climate resilience, and gender equality. Our approach aims to catalyse the development of beneficial, cost-effective products and services that contribute to sustainable growth and enhanced well-being. Our long-standing presence in Nepal is a testimony to adaptive learning, continual innovation, and commitment to delivering meaningful impact. iDE Nepal’s holistic approach to market development is what truly sets us apart.

Building on this experience and expertise, iDE Nepal is seeking a leader who can translate its market-based approach to nutrition into strategic, high-quality implementation and sustainable impact across the region.This position will provide overall strategic, technical, and operational leadership for the Transforming Lives through Nutrition (Transforming Lives) Project, implemented in Dang, Nawalparasi West, Kapilvastu, and Rupandehi Districts. The position will also support implementation of future projects in the region.

He/She will lead the field team, strengthen the capacity of implementing partners, and represent iDE Nepal in relevant forums. The role will ensure effective project implementation, field coordination, monitoring, learning, reporting, and partner support, while maintaining quality, compliance, and achievement of project results. The position will provide technical leadership on nutrition-sensitive and climate-resilient food systems, strengthen private-sector and government partnerships, and promote innovative, scalable, and market-based solutions. Using iDE’s Market Systems Development approach, the position will support outcomes across nutrition, food security, climate-smart agriculture, and WASH, while generating evidence and learning to inform future programming and scale. The position will be based in Butwal, with frequent travel to project locations.

Key Responsibilities

Planning , Management, and Representation

  • Provide strategic leadership and technical support for effective project management and delivery, ensuring quality, compliance, and alignment with organizational priorities.
  • Lead project planning, including development of DIPs, implementation guidelines, operational plans, and adaptive management in response to changing contexts.
  • Ensure integration of GESI, risk management, safeguarding, and other organizational standards across project implementation.
  • Coordinate closely with project, technical/thematic, partner, and Country Office teams to ensure effective implementation and timely resolution of operational issues.
  • Build and maintain effective relationships with government, private sector, development partners, community stakeholders, and other relevant actors, and represent iDE Nepal in key forums and events.
  • Ensure effective communication and coordination with relevant stakeholders and promote collaboration, learning, and resource sharing across the region.

Team Management

  • Provide leadership, guidance, and performance management to team members, ensuring clear roles, accountability, and alignment with organizational objectives.
  • Assess staffing and capacity-building needs and work with HR, line managers, and technical leads to strengthen team capacity and performance.
  • Coordinate team planning, workload, and resource allocation to ensure efficient and effective delivery of project activities.
  • Support staff development, performance appraisal, and resolution of team-related issues in coordination with the Country Office.

Monitoring, Reporting and Learning

  • Oversee project monitoring and supervision in coordination with project and technical leads, ensuring effective implementation and compliance with financial, administrative, and HR requirements.
  • Prepare project progress reports on a monthly, quarterly, and annual basis and share with the direct report and the thematic/technical/project leads
  • Conduct regular field and joint monitoring visits with partners and stakeholders, provide coaching and support, and address implementation issues in a timely manner.
  • Monitor project progress, indicators, budgets, and implementation quality against approved plans, logframes, and theories of change, and prepare timely monthly, quarterly, and annual reports.
  • Contribute to Monitoring, Evaluation, Learning and Research and ensure documentation and sharing of key results, good practices, lessons learned, and evidence.

Safety and Security

  • Monitor contextual, operational, and security risks and ensure appropriate mitigation measures are in place.
  • Maintain and regularly update regional security plans and ensure compliance with organizational safety and security policies and procedures.
  • Serve as the regional focal point for safety and security incidents, ensuring timely communication, response, and coordination with the Country Office.
  • Support security assessments, audits, and implementation of recommended actions, while safeguarding organizational assets, information, and documents.

Requirements

  • Master with 4 years’ experience on Sr. Officer level or Graduate with 7 years’ experience at officer level in Agriculture, Nutrition, Social Science, Development Studies, or a relevant discipline.
  • Relevant experience in the development sector, with significant exposure to project leadership, planning and implementation; coordination; community mobilization; monitoring and supervision at field level
  • Experience working in the agriculture and nutrition sector with a market systems development approach.
  • Strong leadership, teamwork, coordination, and interpersonal skills.
  • Excellent communication, networking, negotiation, mediation, and relationship-building skills.
  • Strong problem-solving, decision-making, analytical, and listening skills.
  • Well-organized, proactive, adaptable, reliable, accountable, and able to manage multiple priorities.
  • Strong computer skills, including MS Office, Google Workspace, and digital communication tools.
  • Demonstrated ability to work respectfully and effectively with people from diverse backgrounds and cultures.
  • Strong commitment to GESI, diversity, inclusion, and respectful workplace practices.
  • Humble, professional, diplomatic, and committed to fostering a culture of mutual respect, trust, and collaboration.
  • Having a two-wheeler valid license would be an added advantage.

Benefits

As per the iDE norms.

iDE Nepal is an Equal Opportunity Employer. Women and Members of Disadvantaged Caste, Ethnic and Religious Groups are Strongly Encouraged to Apply.

Interested and qualifying applicants can submit their application Letter and CV in English, with both phone and email contact details of at least 3 professional references by September 14, 2026.

Posiiton: District Coordinator

The Organisation

Plan International is an independent development and humanitarian organisation that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We believe in the power and potential of every child but know this is often suppressed by poverty, violence, exclusion and discrimination. And it is girls who are most affected.

Working together with children, young people, supporters and partners, we strive for a just world, tackling the root causes of the challenges girls and vulnerable children face. We support children’s rights from birth until they reach adulthood and we enable children to prepare for and respond to crises and adversity. We drive changes in practice and policy at local, national and global levels using our reach, experience and knowledge.

For over 85 years, we have rallied other determined optimists to transform the lives of all children in more than 80 countries.

We won’t stop until we are all equal.

ROLE PURPOSE

Plan International is a development and humanitarian organization that advances children’s rights and equality for girls. We strive for a just world, working together with children, young people, our supporters and partners in over 75 countries. As District Coordinator for Nepal Flash Floods you will be responsible for overall implementation of project activities in Nuwakot. You will required to support the emergency responses activities at the field level by capacitating Plan as well as Partner Staff for smooth implementation.

Dimensions of the Role

The post holder will ensure all project activities are implemented in the project area with quality and on time. The position holder is responsible to work closely with the Partners and other stakeholders for smooth implementation and coordinate day to day operations at District level.

The post holder will work with operational support departments (Finance, Logistics & Procurement, People & Culture, Fundraising, Security, IT, Systems) to support integration of emergency response in to standard tools, guidance and systems.

The role will represent Plan International in relevant external fora and inter-agency coordination groups at the District level.

Responsibility for upholding and implementing relevant aspects of all Plan policies and procedures, including the ‘Say Yes! To Keeping Children Safe’ Policy.

Accountabilities

1. District Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Establish and maintain effective coordination with relevant district authorities, government line agencies, local stakeholders, and other relevant actors.
  • Facilitate regular coordination meetings and information-sharing related to project implementation.
  • Represent the project at relevant district-level coordination forums, as appropriate.
  • Identify emerging implementation issues and facilitate timely resolution in coordination with relevant stakeholders.

2. Partner Support and Implementation Oversight

  • Provide regular technical and operational support to implementing partners to facilitate effective project delivery.
  • Monitor partner implementation against approved plans, targets, timelines, budgets, and agreed quality standards.
  • Conduct regular field visits and monitoring to assess progress, identify gaps, and provide constructive feedback.
  • Follow up on agreed actions and ensure timely implementation of recommendations.
  • Support partners in identifying and addressing operational, technical, and contextual challenges.

3. Quality Assurance and Compliance

  • Ensure project implementation is aligned with approved project documents, organisational policies, donor requirements, and relevant government standards.
  • Monitor compliance with donor and internal requirements throughout implementation.
  • Strengthen documentation, reporting, and evidence of project activities and results.
  • Identify compliance and quality risks and work with partners and relevant internal teams to address them.
  • Contribute to periodic project reviews, assessments, reporting, and learning processes.

4. Complaint Handling and Feedback Mechanism

  • Operationalise and strengthen the project’s Complaint Handling and Feedback Mechanism at district and community levels.
  • Ensure project participants are aware of available channels for providing feedback, raising complaints, and reporting concerns.
  • Ensure complaints and feedback are recorded, referred, followed up, and closed in a timely, confidential, and appropriate manner.
  • Monitor trends and recurring issues from feedback and complaints and support programme improvements based on findings.
  • Ensure that feedback mechanisms are accessible, inclusive, safe, and appropriate for different groups of project participants.

5. Safeguarding and Protection of Project Participants

  • Strengthen safeguarding measures throughout project implementation and partner engagement.
  • Ensure partners and project teams understand and comply with relevant safeguarding, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA), Child Safeguarding, and other applicable organisational standards.
  • Promote safe, dignified, inclusive, and do-no-harm approaches in project activities.
  • Support identification and mitigation of safeguarding risks associated with project implementation.
  • Ensure safeguarding concerns are handled through appropriate reporting and referral mechanisms, maintaining confidentiality and survivor-centred approaches.
  • Promote awareness among project participants, partners, and staff regarding their rights and available safeguarding and reporting channels.
  • Ensure that Plan International’s global policies for Safeguarding Children and Young People and Gender Equality and Inclusion are fully embedded in accordance with the principles and requirements of the policy including relevant implementation standards and guidelines as applicable to area of responsibility. Including, but not limited to, ensuring staff and associates are aware of and understand their responsibilities under these policies and Plan International’s Code of Conduct (CoC); relevance to area of work, and concerns are reported and managed in accordance with the appropriate procedures

  • Senior Technical Advisor- Disaster RisK Management & Climate Change Adaptation and Humanitarian Response Manager at country office and Direct reports to Emergency Response Manager
  • National Organisation disaster risk management network

Externally:

  • Interagency working groups and coordination fora.

ROLE PURPOSE

The position holder will be responsible to coordinate and manage logistics and procurement support for humanitarian and emergency response operations. The position will ensure the timely, efficient, transparent, and compliant procurement of goods and services, overseeing warehouse, fleet, transportation, inventory, and other logistics functions. including administrative support in compliance with Plan International Nepal’s policies and procedures for smooth functioning the Nepal Flash Floods in Project area.

Dimensions of the Role

  • Budget accountability: N/A
  • Reports to : Operation Manager
  • Internal and External interfaces:


Accountabilities

Logistical Support

  • Coordinate overall logistics support for humanitarian and emergency response activities.
  • Ensure timely provision of logistics services, supplies, transportation, warehousing, and other operational support.
  • Coordinate with programme and response teams to understand priorities and anticipate logistics requirements.
  • Identify logistics constraints, risks, and access challenges and propose practical solutions.
  • Coordinate with relevant suppliers, logistics networks, and other stakeholders as required.
  • Provide leadership role for planning and coordinating entire procurement system ensuring policies, and procedures.

Procurement Management

  • Lead and coordinate procurement of goods and services in accordance with organizational procurement policies, donor requirements, and applicable regulations.
  • Ensure procurement is conducted transparently, competitively, ethically, and cost-effectively.
  • Identify reliable suppliers and negotiate competitive prices, delivery terms, and service agreements.
  • Monitor procurement lead times and ensure timely delivery of emergency and programme supplies.
  • Apply emergency procurement procedures and thresholds when activated.
  • Ensure proper procurement documentation and filing for audit and compliance purposes.
  • Bills/invoice is forwarded to Finance within plan policy after the goods/services satisfactorily received.

Warehouse & Inventory Management

  • Manage and oversee response warehouses and ensure proper storage and handling of relief and programme supplies.
  • Ensure proper receipt, storage, packing, dispatch, and delivery of supplies.
  • Conduct regular physical inventory counts and reconcile stock records with physical stock.
  • Ensure appropriate storage conditions, security, safety, and efficient use of warehouse space.
  • Monitor stock levels and provide timely alerts regarding shortages, excess, damaged, or expired items.
  • Maintain proper documentation for all stock movements.
  • Ensure relief items are dispatched to programme locations and partners in a timely manner.

Fleet & Transportation Management

  • Coordinate fleet and transportation requirements for humanitarian response activities.
  • Develop vehicle allocation and movement plans based on operational priorities.
  • Monitor vehicle utilization, fuel consumption, maintenance, repairs, insurance, and documentation.
  • Ensure vehicles are safe, roadworthy, and properly maintained.
  • Coordinate transportation of relief items, equipment, and personnel to response locations.
  • Identify appropriate transportation solutions considering road conditions, access restrictions, security, and cost.
  • Maintain accurate fleet records, vehicle logs, fuel records, and maintenance schedules.
  • Coordinate with drivers and transport service providers and ensure compliance with organizational procedures.

Partner Logistics & Procurement Support

  • Provide technical support and guidance to partner organizations on procurement, logistics, warehouse, fleet, and inventory management.
  • Support partners to develop and strengthen logistics and procurement systems and procedures.
  • Provide coaching, mentoring, and technical guidance to partner logistics staff.
  • Support partners to comply with organizational, donor, and humanitarian standards.

Cash Fund Transactions

  • Manage cash fund transactions and accurately maintain record of expenditures and cash balance on a daily basis
  • Process for cash fund replenishment once spending exceeds 50%
  • Ensure payment requests are approved by concerned authority and has supporting documents before releasing payment out of cash fund
  • Ensure cash fund is kept safely and used for official transactions only
  • Promptly issue ORF for cash refund to Plan, made by staff or external parties and hand over the case to Finance for Bank deposit

Provide general administrative support in Field Office

  • Arrange the hotel booking, accommodation and hall for any official visits/events/workshops
  • Proper documentation and record keeping of field office related legal documents
  • Review and forward claims submitted by the staff members medical claims

Technical expertise, skills and knowledge

Knowledge and Experience

  • Master Degree in management with 3 years of experience or a Bachelor’s Degree with 5 years of experience in the relevant sector; Having experience working in Emergencies is an added advantage
  • Clear understanding of the development sector, its operating and regulatory environment (in Nepal)
  • Clear understanding of the socio/political economic and cultural issues of Nepal, specifically post located districts of the country.
  • Clear in-depth technical and practical knowledge and understanding of the relevant job domain.

Skills Required

  • In depth knowledge of financial system, financial management and reporting.
  • Updated knowledge in taxation laws and statutes of the country.
  • Operational planning & execution
  • Analysis & reasoning and solution driven
  • Managing work relationships (internal/external)
  • Communicating, one to one, in groups both in writing, verbally, presentations and reports, in English, Nepali and relevant local languages.
  • Preparation and management of budgets and assessment of financial implication in work situations
  • Facilitation, negotiation and networking
  • Persuasion and ability to influence
  • Ability to problem solve, handle setbacks and pressure

The National Federation of Women Living with HIV and AIDS (NFWLHA), formerly known as the Women’s Network against HIV & AIDS (WONAHA), was initially established as a loose network in 2006 and was officially registered in 2007 with a vision to create a just and equitable society for women and children infected and affected with HIV, so that they can live a productive, empowered and dignified life, free from stigma and discrimination. Underpinned by guiding principles of gender equity and human rights, evidence-based planning, programming, and policy advocacy, NFWLHA has broadened its strategic intervention areas over the last nine years, focusing mainly on strengthening and capacity development of the network, knowledge management for evidence-based policy advocacy and community system strengthening. Currently, there are 35 community-based organizations (CBOs) affiliated with NFWLHA representing Nepal’s seven provinces, all led by women living with HIV (WLHIV).
