Shree Latinath Madhyamik Vidyalaya Raskot

NEEDS Nepal is a non-profit, non-governmental a social organization that has been actively working in the social sector for the past 27 years. The organization was established in 1999 as a youth group and has since then engaged in various social transformation, good governance, and development initiatives. NEEDS Nepal is registered with the Government of Nepal and has partnered with numerous government, I/NOGs, bilateral agencies to implement programs that focus on empowerment, socio-economic development, and social transformation for marginalized and vulnerable communities such as children, women, youths, persons with disabilities, Dalit, and Janajati and other marginalized.

Project Brief

NEEDS Nepal, in partnership with Oxfam in Nepal, has been implementing “Strengthening Community Preparedness, Rapid Response and Recovery in Nepal (SCOPR3)”. The project started in January 2024 and will be completed in December 2026. The project is being implemented in 40 different communities disaster management committee (CDMCs) of four municipalities of two districts Beldandi RM, Dodhara-Chandani municipality and Bhimdatta municipality of Kanchanpur and Parshuram municipality of Dadeldhura district. The purpose of this project is to ensure that communities affected by recurrent disasters in highly vulnerable areas have enhanced capacities for disaster preparedness, response, and recovery, and are better equipped to co-lead on relief and recovery efforts in collaboration with local authorities.

NEEDS Nepal is seeking a qualified and dynamic with experience on livelihood and enterprise development candidate for the project.

The summary of ToR is given below:

Job Title: Livelihood and Enterprise Development Officer (LED-Officer)

Location: NEEDS-Nepal Central Office, Kanchanpur

Post holder reports to: Project Coordinator, SCOPR3, NEEDS

People’s management responsibility: Yes; Social mobilizers

Project Name: Strengthening Community Preparedness, Rapid Response and Recovery (SCOPR3)

Project Locations: 40 communities from Parsuram municipality from Dadeldhura district, Bhiagmdatta municipality, Beldandi RM and Dodhara-Chandani municipality from Kanchanpur district.

Job purpose

To strengthen the economic resilience of vulnerable and disaster-prone communities- particularly women-by supporting local enterprise and livelihood development so they become more financially stable and better able to withstand disaster impacts.

Specific task and responsibilities

  • Business Development: Identify and assess potential business opportunities within the community. Facilitate the establishment and growth of enterprises through market research and analysis.
  • Strengthen the Value chain: develop the value chain and strengthen as per enterprise. To promoting the enterprise and create the enabling environment to strengthen the value chain.
  • Organizational Strategy and visioning: Develop the Livelihood and enterprise sector strategy of organization for sustainability. Capacity development livelihood and enterprise resource material preparation.
  • Capacity Building: Provide training and workshops to enhance the skills of entrepreneurs. Offer guidance on business planning, financial management, and marketing strategies.
  • Financial Assistance: Assist in securing funding and financial resources for startup businesses. Collaborate with financial institutions and government agencies to facilitate loans and grants.
  • Networking: Build and maintain relationships with local businesses, government agencies, and non-profit organizations. Connect entrepreneurs with relevant stakeholders and resources.
  • Livelihood Improvement: Implement programs that contribute to the improvement of livelihoods in the community. Focus on sustainable and inclusive economic development initiatives.
  • Monitoring and Evaluation: Develop and implement systems to monitor the progress and impact of enterprise development programs. Evaluate the effectiveness of interventions and make recommendations for improvements.
  • Community Engagement: Engage with the local community to understand their needs and aspirations. Foster a collaborative approach to enterprise development, involving community members in decision-making processes.
  • Market Access: Facilitate access to markets for local products and services. Explore opportunities for partnerships and collaborations to enhance market reach.
  • Sustainability Focus: Promote all dimensions of sustainable business practices (technical, social, environmental, political commitment). Encourage the adoption of ethical and socially responsible business approaches.
  • Data Management: Maintain accurate records and data related to enterprise development programs. Use data for reporting, analysis, and informed decision-making.
  • Educational Initiatives: Develop educational initiatives to enhance the entrepreneurial skills of community members. Encourage a culture of continuous learning and adaptation.
  • Additional: as per immediate requirements and requested by your line manager.

Requirements

  • At least bachelor’s degree in agriculture and relevant to micro-enterprise with having minimum 2 years experiences in micro enterprise and livelihood related projects as a officer/Project Coordinator.
  • Possess working experiences in Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) projects and hold knowledge on correlation between DRR and livelihood will be asset.
  • Good experiences in all aspects of rural sector micro-enterprises development.
  • Report writing skills in English and Nepali both language.
  • Coordination skills with pertinent stakeholders.
  • Basic knowledge on MS office package, and Canva.

Safeguarding & PSEA

NEEDS Nepal has a zero-tolerance policy and approach to any abuse, sexual harassment, or exploitation of, a vulnerable adult or child by any of our staff, volunteers, consultant, and suppliers. All individuals and institutions have committed to respecting the core principles regarding the prevention of sexual exploitation and abuse laid out by the organization safeguarding policy, Zero tolerance Policy, PSEA& code of conduct that is associated with the organization.

NEEDS Nepal has expected from all the staff to share this commitment through Safeguarding, PSEA Policy, and Code of Conduct. All staff must be committed to ensuring that all individuals we come into contact with through our work, whether team members, community members, program participants, or others, are treated with respect and dignity.

How to apply

Qualified & eligible national citizens are highly encouraged to apply with their updated CV along with a motivation letter & expected salary in gross per month to the following email address, hr@needsnepal.org.np by 9th August 2026.

Women, ethnic minorities, and local applicants are highly encouraged to apply. No telephone calls will be entertained and this automatically disqualifies in the recruitment process.

NEEDS Nepal will reserve all rights to make the final decision. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the further recruitment process. The remuneration and other benefits package shall be as per NEEDS Nepal HRM policy & guidelines.

Human Resource Management Committee

NEEDS Nepal

Work closely with : Different departments – Construction, Fellowship, Finance, Procurement and Human Resource

ROLE SUMMARY

The District Lead is responsible for improving education quality in UWS schools at the district level by working closely with government officials, teachers, and communities to ensure all programme activities
align with UWS Nepal standards. The position holder will coordinate with stakeholders for school construction, ensure smooth implementation of education programmes, coordinate teacher training, and support procurement processes. TheDistrict Lead reviews and approves expenses within their authority and ensures timely submission of documents to the Finance team. In addition, the position holder handles administrative tasks, leads and supervises the district team, and supports HR functions such as developing job descriptions, setting KPIs, and conducting staff performance appraisals with support from the HR Team.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. Programme Implementation and Quality Assurance [40%]

  • Lead and oversee implementation of all UWS Nepal programmes in the district, ensuring alignment with organizational strategy, annual plans, and quality standards; monitor progress and troubleshoot implementation challenges.
  •  Provide regular, accurate updates on programme progress, achievements, and challenges to the Senior Education Manager and Executive Director, and promote evidence-based, continuous
    improvement.
  • Lead design and delivery of teacher professional development (pre-service and in-service training), ensuring content is practical, context-sensitive, and aligned with national education priorities; adapt/translate training materials as needed.
  • Mentor and coach Education Officers (EOs), School Mobilizers (SMs), and teachers to strengthen facilitation, classroom practice, and community engagement skills; facilitate peer-learning and
    lesson-sharing among teachers.
  • Track trainer schedules and quarterly training deadlines; monitor classroom practices and schoollevel interventions that contribute to improved student learning outcomes.
  • Maintain accurate records of programme activities, training, and monitoring visits, and use data/feedback to inform decision-making, document lessons learned and refine programme approaches.
  • Monitor school construction progress; coordinate with relevant departments to ensure the timely delivery and stockpiling of construction materials.

2. Government and Stakeholder Engagement [30%]

  • Build and maintain strong working relationships with local government Education Units and other stakeholders to ensure programme alignment with local, provincial, and federal education priorities.
  • Represent UWS Nepal in district-level meetings and coordination forums, in close coordination with the UWS Nepal Board.
  • Strengthen collaboration with School Management Committees (SMCs), Parent-Teacher Associations (PTAs), school leaders, and communities to secure partnerships and support programme continuity and sustainability.
  •  Engage local government bodies on school construction, repair, and maintenance activities, and coordinate with other UWS Nepal departments to ensure joined-up engagement with local government.
  •  Coordinate and monitor school construction, renovation, repair, and maintenance projects to ensure quality, timely completion, and compliance with approved standards, budgets, and timelines.
  •  Ensure infrastructure projects meet safety, inclusivity, accessibility, disaster resilience, and environmental standards while maintaining proper documentation and project handover.

3. Financial and Human Resource Leadership (20%)

  • Support preparation of District budgets and work plans; monitor periodic expenditure against approved budgets, providing justification for variances and ensuring alignment with programmematic
    progress.
  • Review and approve expenditures submitted by Field Teams within delegated authority, escalate items beyond threshold, and ensure submissions are supported by adequate, compliant documentation.
  •  Support the Finance Team in organizing financial records and supporting documents for review and audit purposes and help identify and flag financial risks.
  •  Oversee timely submission and approval of Field Staff leave records and timesheets, providing day-today HR support with the field-based HR focal person.
  •  Lead the district team in HR management process annual goal setting, KPIs, timely performance appraisals, and updating job descriptions fostering an inclusive, accountable, performance-oriented
    work culture.

4. Child Protection and Safeguarding [10%]

  • Serve as the District Child Protection and Safeguarding (CPS) Focal Person, escalating any CPS concerns to the National CPS Lead within 24 hours.
  •  Ensure CPS policies, procedures, and standards are understood, implemented, and monitored across all district operations, and promote a culture of safeguarding, accountability, and respect among staff,
    schools, and partners.
  • Coordinate and facilitate CPS training for EOs, SM, and Fellows, and monitor safeguarding risks linked to programme, training, construction, and recruitment activities.
  •  Support responses to concerns and follow-up monitoring at the direction of the National CPS Lead, and maintain secure, confidential CPS documentation and records.

EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE AND COMPETENCIES

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Development Studies, Social Sciences, Public Administration, or a related field(s)
  •  Minimum 5 years of relevant professional experience, including at least 2 years in a leadership, supervisory, or district-level coordination role.
  •  Experience of Managing construction projects will be strong advantage.
  •  Demonstrated experience in education programme implementation, teacher professional development, school improvement, or community-based development initiatives.
  •  Strong understanding of Nepal’s education system, local governance structures, and community engagement approaches, with proven experience working with local governments, SMCs, PTAs, and
    community stakeholders.
  •  Experience in team leadership, staff supervision, coaching, performance management, and capacity development.
  • Working knowledge of budgeting, expenditure management, financial compliance, and operational administration.
  • Understanding of child protection and safeguarding principles and organizational accountability mechanisms.
  • Excellent communication, facilitation, negotiation, and stakeholder management skills, with strong report writing and problem-solving abilities.
  •  Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications and digital reporting tools; fluency in both Nepali and English.
  •  Willingness and ability to travel extensively within the district, including remote and hard-to-reachareas. Possession of a valid two-wheeler driving license will be an added advantage

Job Title : School Mobilizer
Department : Programmeme
Base Location : Jitpur Simara Municipality, Bara
Reports to : District Lead
Duration : Fixed term until December 2026 with the possibility of extension, subject to satisfactory performance and the availability of funding

ROLE SUMMARY

The School Mobilizer (SM) is responsible for providing field-level support to UWS Nepal supported schools within the assigned cluster. Working under the guidance of the District Lead, the SM serves as the key liaison between schools, communities, and UWS Nepal. The role focuses on supporting the effective implementation of education programmes, strengthening communication and coordination with concerned school stakeholders, collecting and maintaining school data, supporting the use of educational resources and digital tools, and promoting child protection, safeguarding, and inclusive education practices. The SM works collaboratively with schools to identify needs, facilitate support, and strengthen programme implementation.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

1. School Support and Programme Implementation

  •  Conduct regular visits to assigned schools and maintain positive working relationships with school leadership, teachers, and stakeholders.
  • Support schools in the implementation of UWS education programmes, activities, and initiatives.
  •  Assist schools in the utilization of educational resources, learning materials, and programme tools provided by UWS Nepal.
  •  Identify challenges affecting programme implementation and communicate them to the District Lead for need-based support and follow-up.
  •  Support schools during assessments, events, campaigns,training, and other educational activities as required.

2. Data Collection, Documentation and Reporting

  •  Collect, verify, and maintain school-level data as required by UWS Nepal, including student attendance, enrollment information, assessment, training records, meeting minutes, and other relevant documents.
  •  Maintain accurate records of school visits, activities, observations, and stakeholder engagements.
  •  Support schools in completing required reporting formats and documentation.
  • Submit timely reports and updates to the District Lead according to established reporting schedules.
  •  Ensure confidentiality and safe handling of student and school information.

3. Teacher and School Capacity Support

  •  Facilitate communication between teachers, schools, and theDistrict Lead regarding professional development activities.
  • Support classroom observation processes led by the District Lead and assist with follow-up actions when required.
  •  Encourage participation in teacher training, mentoring, and professional learning opportunities organized by UWS Nepal.
  • Share relevant educational resources, guidance, and information with teachers as directed by the District Lead.

4. Community Engagement and Stakeholder Coordination

  •  Maintain regular communication with School Management Committees (SMCs), Parent Teacher Associations (PTAs), Mothers’ Groups, Child Clubs, School Retention Team, and community
    stakeholders.
  •  Support schools in strengthening parent and community engagement in children’s education.
  •  Follow up with families of students identified by schools as having attendance or participation concerns.

5. Child Protection, Safeguarding and Inclusion

  • Promote awareness and implementation of UWS Nepal’s Child Protection, Safeguarding, and Inclusion Policies at the school level.
  •  Immediately report child protection or safeguarding concerns through established organizational reporting mechanisms.
  •  Support the identification and referral of children who may require additional support or protection services.
  •  Assist in maintaining records related to safeguarding cases in accordance with confidentiality requirements.
  • Promote inclusive practices that support the participation of all learners regardless of gender, disability, ethnicity, language, or socio-economic background.

6. Coordination and Other Responsibilities

  • Participate in team meetings, training sessions, planning workshops, and review meetings.
  •  Foster positive relationships with local government representatives and education stakeholders.
  • Carry out other education-related duties assigned by the District Lead that are consistent with the purpose of the role.

EXPERIENCE, KNOWLEDGE AND COMPETENCIES

  • At least intermediate level (10+2) in Education, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or relate field(s).
  •  Minimum of 1 year’s working experience with schools, communities, educational projects, or development programmes.
  •  Understanding of Nepal’s education system and local education governance structures, including SMCs and PTAs.
  •  Good understanding of child protection and safeguarding.
  •  Strong communication, facilitation, and interpersonal skills.
  •  Ability to build and maintain positive relationships with school and community stakeholders.
  •  Experience in data collection, documentation, and report preparation.
  • Basic digital literacy and ability to use mobile applications, databases, spreadsheets, and online reporting systems.
  •  Ability to travel regularly to assigned cluster schools.
  •  Good problem-solving and organizational skills.
  •  Fluency in Nepali, working knowledge of English is an asset

Location: Kathmandu

About the role

We are looking for an experienced professional to lead the implementation of the Scaling Index-Based Flood Insurance for Smallholder Farmers in the Kankai River Basin project. The role will coordinate with government agencies, insurance companies, technical partners, and local stakeholders to design and deliver innovative climate risk insurance solutions. The position will also oversee project planning, stakeholder engagement, partnership development, and risk management to ensure successful project implementation.

About you

You have experience in climate risk financing, insurance, disaster risk management, or a related field, with strong project management and stakeholder coordination skills. You are an effective communicator with excellent analytical and report writing abilities, capable of managing multiple priorities and building strong partnerships.

Why join us?

The opportunity to work for an organisation that is making a positive difference to the lives of people worldwide, a friendly and supportive culture, working with values driven and highly engaged colleagues, work life balance and flexible working – these are just some of the reasons we think Practical Action is a great place to work.

About us

Practical Action exists to change the systems that keep people in poverty and vulnerable to the impacts of climate change, nature loss and pollution. We work alongside communities to build resilient livelihoods and thriving, inclusive societies.

Our Values

We are People Centred, striving to create an equal, fair, accessible, dignified and respectful environment for everyone we work with – from colleagues and communities, to supporters, suppliers and stakeholders.

We are Impact Driven, existing to make a positive difference, so everything we do is driven by our energy to create lasting value for the people and communities we serve.

We are Transparent and trustworthy, acting with integrity, honesty, and strong ethics, building mutual trust with everyone we work with to achieve the highest standards.

We are Innovative, and champion learning, curiosity and fresh thinking, bringing local knowledge to create global impact.

We are Resilient changemakers working for sustainable development, meeting challenges head-on, and evolving through the lessons learnt.

Position: Procurement and Logistics Officer
Project: Educated, Empowered, and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society and Sponsorship communication program
Duty Station: JSDP. Sindhuli field office, Kamalamai-6, Sindhuli
Working area: Office based with some travel to working area and outside.
Contract type: 11 months with possible to extension
Expertise: Bachelor’s Degree in Business Management, Finance, Accountancy and other relevant field with 3 years of working experience in the development sector i.e. NGO/INGO of relevant field.
Reports to: Project Coordinator
Accountable to: Board of JSDP Sindhuli

Janajati Society Development Program, Sindhuli (JSDP) is a district based non-profit making development organization. JSDP is registered under Organization Registration Act 2034, in 2064 at District Administration Office, Sindhuli. Janajati Society Development Program (JSDP) Sindhuli has been working in the different developmental initiatives for sustainable development at Sindhuli district, since its establishment. It is established for the socio- economic improvement of the deprived, socially excluded, and marginalized people of the district. Janajati Society Development Program, Sindhuli (JSDP) foresees a rightful, gender equitable and socially inclusive society where peace, progress and prosperity are established.

Project Introduction:

The “Educated, Empowered and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society in Sindhuli” is a consortium project with Plan International Nepal, HANDS Nepal and JSDP, Sindhuli for two years focusing Education and ECD, and Protection as themes, and youth empowerment, climate crisis, WASH and humanitarian as cross cutting themes. It targets public schools and marginalized communities of 33 wards from six local governments (LGs) of Sindhuli districts, which starts on July 2026 and will end on June 2028. The project adapts the learnings from previous projects and focuses to enable children, adolescents, and youth especially girls from marginalized communities in Sindhuli District to access quality, safe, inclusive, and gender-responsive education, to get support for transition to home to schools, to thrive in a safe, non-violence and non-discriminative environments and to nurture through parenting education, thereby reducing child, early, and forced marriage (CEFM) and supporting a dignified transition to adulthood. To enable children, adolescents, and youth, especially girls from marginalized and vulnerable communities in Sindhuli District, the project will focus;

  • To improve equitable access to quality, inclusive and child-friendly ECED and school education through strengthened learning environments, teacher capacity, child participation and family engagement.
  • To strengthen nurturing care, positive parenting and nutrition practices that promote holistic early childhood development and school readiness.
  • To strengthen community-based child protection systems and promote gender equality through increased awareness, participation and prevention of violence, GBV and child, early and forced marriage.
  • To strengthen the capacity of local governments and stakeholders to develop, implement and institutionalize evidence-based education, ECED and child protection policies, plans and budgets.

Major Responsibilities:

A. Finance related (30%)

Working Area: Sindhuli district
Responsible to: District Project Coordinator (DPC), HANDS Nepal YETI Project.

Background

Human & National Development Society (HANDS) Nepal, established in 2001, is a non- governmental, non-political, non-profit organization focused on integrated community development and natural resource management. With a vision of a prosperous, equitable, and ethical society, HANDS Nepal’s mission is to implement initiatives fostering inclusive and equitable development. For over 25 years, the organization has promoted sustainable development, addressing areas such as governance, education, child rights, WASH, climate change, disaster risk reduction, health, and livelihoods. HANDS Nepal aims to empower marginalized groups, particularly women, children, and Dalits, to access basic needs and lead dignified lives. Through partnerships with multiple agencies and over 42 projects impacting more than 200,000 people across thirteen districts, HANDS Nepal strengthens local governments, promotes participatory governance, and ensures marginalized communities can shape their futures.

Project: Youth Empowerment for Transformation and Innovation (YETI) Project

HANDS Nepal, Sindhuli has been working in a long-term partnership with Plan International Nepal since 2012. Currently, the organization is collaborating with Plan International Nepal to implement the Youth Empowerment for Transformation and Innovationn (YETI) Project. The project goal is Economic empowerment of young girl, adolescent women and marginalized youths driving inclusive, climate-resilient, and market-driven economies. The planned intervention will be reaching to young people from targeted communities. The project will work equipping young people with the knowledge, skills, and confidence needed to initiate and manage sustainable business enterprises. It emphasizes fostering an entrepreneurial mindset that enables youth to identify, develop, and scale innovative business ideas aligned with emerging local market opportunities. Likewise, the project will work on strengthening and institutionalizing enterprise development support systems that enable youths to access business development and support services for entrepreneurship, and business growth. The aim is to strengthen a coherent, accessible, and sustainable support ecosystem that systematically connects youth with enterprise development services and markets. Similarly, the project focuses on enabling young people particularly young women and marginalized youth to access and effectively use appropriate financial services that support their transition from training to sustainable entrepreneurship.

Furthermore, focuses on building a policy and institutional ecosystem that enables youth especially young women and marginalized groups to thrive as entrepreneurs and innovators.

General Responsibilities

The Technical Assistant – Agriculture is responsible for providing field-level technical assistance to farmers/youth entrepreneurs to improve agricultural productivity, climate-resilient farming practices, agribusiness development and market linkages. The position supports the implementation of project activities related to crop production, extension services, demonstrations, capacity building, monitoring, and coordination with local governments and private sectors to promote sustainable and market-oriented agriculture.

Key Responsibilities

1. Agriculture Production and Technical Support

  • Support farmers/youth entrepreneurs in selecting suitable crops and agricultural enterprises.
  • Provide field-level technical support on the production of vegetables, spices, fruits, and other high-value crops by promoting Good Agricultural Practices, improved crop management techniques, quality seed use, and efficient input utilization.
  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor crop performance and provide timely technical advice.
  • Support in adopting improved irrigation methods, crop diversification, post-harvest management, and value addition practices to enhance productivity and profitability.
  • Provide regular technical coaching and mentoring to strengthen their technical knowledge and practical skills.

2. Agribusiness and Enterprise Development

  • Support youth entrepreneurs in preparing agribusiness plans, enterprise development plans, and investment proposals for agricultural enterprises.
  • Assist farmers in conducting basic cost-benefit analyses, gross margin calculations, enterprise budgeting, and farm record keeping to improve farm profitability and business decision-making.
  • Promote market-oriented production systems, value addition, grading, packaging, storage, and collective marketing to enhance farmers’ income.
  • Facilitate linkages between farmers, cooperatives, input suppliers, financial institutions, buyers, and other market actors to strengthen agricultural value chains.

3. Coordination and Stakeholder Engagement

  • Coordinate with Municipal Agriculture Sections, Ward Offices, agricultural service providers, cooperatives, community organizations, private input suppliers, and other relevant stakeholders for effective implementation of agricultural activities.
  • Support farmers/youth entrepreneurs in implementing project activities according to approved work plans.
  • Participate in municipal coordination meetings, agricultural campaigns, exhibitions, and stakeholder consultations as required by the project.

4. Documentation and Reporting

  • Prepare monthly progress reports, field visit reports, training reports, success stories, case studies, lessons learned, and other documentation required by the project.
  • Develop and update seasonal agricultural calendars and IEC materials to support project implementation.

Required Qualifications and Experience

  • Diploma in Agriculture or 10+2 in Agriculture (JTA) from a recognized institution.
  • Minimum one (1) year of relevant professional experience for Diploma holders or three (3) years for JTA in agricultural extension, crop production, farmer training, or agriculture and rural development projects.
  • Prior experience working with NGOs and/or INGOs will be considered an added advantage.

Core Competencies and Skills

  • Strong technical knowledge of crop production and soil management.
  • Community facilitation and coordination skills.
  • Proficiency in MS Word, Excel, documentation and reporting

Safeguarding and GESI Commitment

  • Demonstrated commitment to safeguarding, child protection, gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, environmental sustainability, and compliance with Plan International and HANDS Nepal safeguarding and GESI policies.

Other Conditions

  • The organization reserves the right to assign additional responsibilities relevant to the position and project needs.

It is established for the socio- economic improvement of the deprived, socially excluded, and marginalized people of the district. Janajati Society Development Program, Sindhuli (JSDP) foresees a rightful, gender equitable and socially inclusive society where peace, progress and prosperity are established.

Project Introduction:

The “Educated, Empowered and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society in Sindhuli” is a consortium project with Plan International Nepal, HANDS Nepal and JSDP, Sindhuli for two years focusing Education and ECD, and Protection as themes, and youth empowerment, climate crisis, WASH and humanitarian as cross cutting themes. It targets public schools and marginalized communities of 33 wards from six local governments (LGs) of Sindhuli districts, which starts on July 2026 and will end on June 2028. The project adapts the learnings from previous projects and focuses to enable children, adolescents, and youth especially girls from marginalized communities in Sindhuli District to access quality, safe, inclusive, and gender-responsive education, to get support for transition to home to schools, to thrive in a safe, non-violence and non-discriminative environments and to nurture through parenting education, thereby reducing child, early, and forced marriage (CEFM) and supporting a dignified transition to adulthood. To enable children, adolescents, and youth, especially girls from marginalized and vulnerable communities in Sindhuli District, the project will focus;

  • To improve equitable access to quality, inclusive and child-friendly ECED and school education through strengthened learning environments, teacher capacity, child participation and family engagement.
  • To strengthen nurturing care, positive parenting and nutrition practices that promote holistic early childhood development and school readiness.
  • To strengthen community-based child protection systems and promote gender equality through increased awareness, participation and prevention of violence, GBV and child, early and forced marriage.
  • To strengthen the capacity of local governments and stakeholders to develop, implement and institutionalize evidence-based education, ECED and child protection policies, plans and budgets.

The Program Coordinator (PC) is responsible for leading the project, which includes technical expertise on protection, education, pre-school campaign and sponsorship communication. S/he has to mobilize JSDP’s team and effective collaborate with HANDS Nepal and Plan International Nepal. Program Coordinator provides technical, conceptual and strategic support to JSDP Sindhuli for program cycle management in planning, implementing and monitoring “Educated, Empowered, and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society in Sindhuli” and “Sponsorship Communication Program”, following child centered community development, right based approach and gender transformative approach. It is established for the socio- economic improvement of the deprived, socially excluded, and marginalized people of the district. Janajati Society Development Program, Sindhuli (JSDP) foresees a rightful, gender equitable and socially inclusive society where peace, progress and prosperity are established.

Project Introduction:

The “Educated, Empowered and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society in Sindhuli” is a consortium project with Plan International Nepal, HANDS Nepal and JSDP, Sindhuli for two years focusing Education and ECD, and Protection as themes, and youth empowerment, climate crisis, WASH and humanitarian as cross cutting themes. It targets public schools and marginalized communities of 33 wards from six local governments (LGs) of Sindhuli districts, which starts on July 2026 and will end on June 2028. The project adapts the learnings from previous projects and focuses to enable children, adolescents, and youth especially girls from marginalized communities in Sindhuli District to access quality, safe, inclusive, and gender-responsive education, to get support for transition to home to schools, to thrive in a safe, non-violence and non-discriminative environments and to nurture through parenting education, thereby reducing child, early, and forced marriage (CEFM) and supporting a dignified transition to adulthood. To enable children, adolescents, and youth, especially girls from marginalized and vulnerable communities in Sindhuli District, the project will focus;

To improve equitable access to quality, inclusive and child-friendly ECED and school education through strengthened learning environments, teacher capacity, child participation and family engagement.
To strengthen nurturing care, positive parenting and nutrition practices that promote holistic early childhood development and school readiness.
To strengthen community-based child protection systems and promote gender equality through increased awareness, participation and prevention of violence, GBV and child, early and forced marriage.
To strengthen the capacity of local governments and stakeholders to develop, implement and institutionalize evidence-based education, ECED and child protection policies, plans and budgets.

GENERAL RESPONSIBILITIES

The main responsible of the Protection Officer is to work as the project focal person for the allocated local government/s of the Educated, Empowered, and Thriving Girls for a Safe and Inclusive Society project. S/he should assist Project Coordinator with the project cycle management of the project in Sindhuli including planning and budgeting, implementation, monitoring and supervision, and reporting. S/he should support the field supervisor for day-to-day project planning and implementation. S/he should coordinate key stakeholders including local governments, schools, health institutions, security agencies, child/ girls/ youth clubs/ networks, and so on. S/he should support GESI, Monitoring, and Documentation Officer to prepare knowledge management products, project learning, and challenges.

Other Duties,

Implementation and Stakeholder Coordination(30%)

  • Lead implementation of child protection, safeguarding and GBV prevention interventions in assigned municipalities.
  • Ensure compliance with Child Protection Policy, Safeguarding Policy, PSEAH and Code of Conduct.
  • Promote safe programming and child safeguarding throughout project implementation.
  • Support confidential identification, documentation and referral of child protection concerns.
  • Assist PC to coordinate local government authorities (Rural/Municipality), communities and all local stakeholders to run the program smoothly
  • Support field supervisors for the project implementation and mobilization of community volunteers, and children/youth clubs/networks.
  • Ensuring continuous communication and sharing project information with the right holders and communities’ representatives regarding the implementation of works in order to ensure flawless progress of activities
  • Liaise with all project staff to ensure that project interventions are in a timely with concrete project plan and budget as per finalized project documents
  • Support to PC for knowledge management product preparation and documentation of learning, challenges, best practices, and opportunities of the project.
  • Strengthen Community Based Child Protection Mechanisms (CBCPMs).
  • Reactivate and support Ward Child Rights Committees (WCRCs).
  • Facilitate regular coordination meetings with community protection networks.
  • Strengthen referral pathways among municipalities, police, judicial committees, safe houses and health facilities.

Capacity Development(10%)

  • Develop the capacity of the project team, right holders, and stakeholders by conducting or using resource persons on different types of activities based on the project theme.
  • To actively engage in the implementation of the project activities, the beneficiary selection process under the guidance of PC

Planning, Supervision, and Monitoring of field activities (30%)

    • Conduct effective monitoring of each activity regularly which ensures meeting the goal and outcome of the project
    • Manage the project budget and ensure project expenditures are in-line with the agreed project plan and budget
    • Ensure the timely implementation of field works as per the predefined schedule.
    • Prepare case studies both positive and negative with a special focus on lesson learning
    • Monitor the conformity of the field works (training, field visits, meetings, etc) with the standards of the organization, and as per the agreed activity planned and contracts.
    • Prepare monitoring/evaluation tools and indicators to measure the output/outcome of the project
    • To check the quality of project intervention.

Data collection and reporting (20%)

  • Support GESI and MD Officer for project data management in time through direct involvement and mobilization of field supervisor.
  • Ensure effective communication between the organization or project teams through the line manager on any new developments, possible problems, or conflicts during the activities and important decisions and directives
  • Prepare monthly/quarterly/annual progress reports of the project.
  • Ensure effective communication between the organization, and project teams and report immediately on any new developments, changes, financial aspects, and important decisions and directives
  • To conduct frequent field visits, focus group discussions, and key informant interviews

Accountability (10%)

  • Make sure that field activities are undertaken timely as mentioned in the project document in the assigned project sites.
  • Make sure that records are correctly maintained and that reporting is done on time.
  • Make sure that efficient coordination with all concerned agencies is maintained in the project sites.
  • Maintain performance appraisal of a field supervisor as per the HR policy of JSDP, Sindhuli.

As per JSDP, Sindhuli board decision

Experience: S/he has an experience in a similar position in the development project cycle management of Protection. S/he should have 3 years of working experience in the development section i.e. NGO. Preference will be given to the candidate working in Child Protection and working with different child club and networks.

Competence:

  • Sound management knowledge and skills of project staff mobilization, project planning implementation, and monitoring.
  • Language: Ability to write clearly and concisely in English and Nepali
  • Communication: Sound communication skills, managing work relationships (internal/external), coordination, and networking.
  • Proven IT skills: Word, Excel, Outlook, PowerPoint, and skill of computer applications/
  • Two wheeler driving license is required.
  • Female, Dalit, Adibashi/Janajati and Madeshi candidates are strongly recommended to apply.

Level of Contact with Children and Program Participants: High

Application Procedure

If eligible, drop your CV with cover letter to HR Department of JSDP Sindhuli within 7 days office hour of notice publication (no later than 7 August, 2026) to jsdp_vacancy@jsdpsindhuli.org.np or Documents can be submitted in office of JSDP Sindhuli kamalamai-6, Ratmata Sindhuli in office hour within the mentioned time frame. If the last day of application falls on public holiday, the application can be submitted on the next day as well.

Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for the next stage of the selection process. Requested to submit updated CV including cover letter clearly mentioning the position applying in the subject line. No telephone inquiries will be entertained and any inappropriate recommendation might automatically disqualify the candidate from further processing. JSDP Sindhuli respects child rights and strictly follows the child protection policy of the organization.

JSDP Sindhuli is an equal opportunities employer and strictly follows the merit-based selection. Qualified female candidates or those from disadvantaged communities are strongly encouraged to apply.

JSDP Sindhuli reserves right to qualify/disqualify applications in any case.

Nepal Public Health Institute Private Limited is a registered consulting company in Nepal committed to advancing public health through research, capacity building, digital health innovations, policy support, and knowledge management. As part of its digital transformation initiative, NPHI is developing an online learning and knowledge management platform using WordPress and LearnPress to host online courses, digital resources, and professional development opportunities.

To support this initiative, NPHI seeks to engage a qualified WordPress Consultant to develop, customize, and optimize the platform.

Objective
To develop and customize a secure, scalable, and user-friendly WordPress-based Learning Management System (LMS) that meets the functional and technical requirements of Nepal Public Health Institute.

Scope of Work
The consultant shall be responsible for:

Website Development

  • Develop and configure a professional WordPress website.
  • Install and configure themes and required plugins.
  • Ensure responsive design for desktop, tablet, and mobile devices.
  • LearnPress LMS Development
  • Install and configure LearnPress.
  • Customize courses, lessons, quizzes, certificates, and user dashboards.
  • Configure instructor and student roles.
  • Customize LMS functionalities based on project requirements.

Plugin & Theme Customization

  • Customize existing WordPress themes and plugins.
  • Develop custom functionalities where required.
  • Resolve plugin conflicts and compatibility issues.
  • Ensure compatibility following WordPress core updates.
  • Performance & Security
  • Optimize website speed and performance.
  • Implement website security best practices.
  • Configure backup and recovery mechanisms.
  • Optimize database and caching.

Technical Support

  • Conduct testing and bug fixing.
  • Support deployment to the production server.
  • Provide technical documentation.
  • Provide basic training and handover to the team.
  • Payment integrations.

Deliverables
The consultant shall deliver:

  • Fully functional WordPress website.
  • Customised LearnPress LMS.
  • Responsive website compatible with major browsers.
  • Plugin compatibility testing and issue resolution.
  • Optimized website performance.
  • Technical documentation.
  • Source code and configuration files.
  • Knowledge transfer and technical handover.Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Software Engineering, or a related field (preferred).

Confidentiality
The consultant shall maintain the confidentiality of all information, documents, databases, source code, and other materials obtained during the assignment. No project-related information shall be shared with any third party without prior written approval from NPHI.

Intellectual Property
All outputs, including source code, databases, website designs, custom plugins, documentation, and other materials developed under this consultancy shall become the exclusive property of Nepal Public Health Institute Private Limited.

Captivating Nepal is a non-profit organization dedicated to breaking the cycle of poverty and fostering long-term community development by empowering marginalized groups, with a primary focus on women and children. Through core interventions in education, healthcare, anti-trafficking, and sustainable livelihoods, the organization works to build resilient and self-reliant communities. A key initiative, the Captivating Village Program (CVP), helps out-of-school children, particularly vulnerable girls, re-enroll and complete their education by providing essential support. To ensure sustainable impact, CVP enhances classroom quality through teacher training, mitigates human trafficking risks by expanding economic and educational opportunities, and offers family livelihood and skill-building programs to achieve financial independence for women and youth. Additionally, Captivating Nepal addresses holistic well-being by conducting child health camps and psychosocial screenings to respond to critical child and adolescent mental health needs across its project areas.

Position: Program Officer

Required number of position: 1

Duty Station: Gaththaghar, Bhaktapur (50% field visits to project sites)

Expected Start Date: As soon as possible

Contract Type: 12 months (3 months’ probation period)

Report to: Program Manager

Job purpose

The Program Officer who will be responsible for the effective planning, implementation, and monitoring of Captivating Nepal’s programs activities in the project site. The Program Officer will ensure the successful delivery of education, healthcare, women’s empowerment, and livelihood support initiatives, aimed at addressing key challenges such as school dropouts, human trafficking, and gender inequality. The role requires coordinating program activities, managing partnerships, overseeing project staffs, and ensuring alignment with organizational goals. The Program Officer will also contribute to improving the quality of education, promoting skill development, supporting sustainable livelihoods, and addressing child and adolescent mental health concerns, ultimately contributing to the empowerment and well-being of marginalized communities.

Roles and Responsibilities

1. Program Planning and Coordination:

  • Develop, implement, and manage the overall strategy and action plans for the Captivating Village Program across all project sites
  • Ensure alignment of program activities with Captivating Nepal’s mission and goals, ensuring a holistic approach to education, healthcare, women’s empowerment, and sustainable livelihoods.
  • Conduct needs assessment, prepare report and design the program activities based on the assessment.
  • Prepare Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP) for the project and regularly follow up with the progress made based on the DIP prepared.
  • Coordinate with local government authorities, community leaders, and stakeholders to ensure smooth program execution and adherence to local needs.
  • Build and maintain strong relationships with local communities, schools, women’s groups, and other stakeholders to ensure active participation and support.

2. Program Implementation:

  • Oversee the day-to-day implementation of program activities at all project sites, ensuring high-quality delivery and timely completion.
  • Facilitate the return of school dropouts to education and ensure continued educational support for vulnerable children, especially girls.
  • Lead the design and delivery of skill development and income-generating activities for out-of-school youth and marginalized communities.

Posiiton: Disaster Risk Reduction / Management and Early Warning System Analyst

Job Schedule: Full time
Locations: Kathmandu, Nepal
Agency: UNDP
Grade: NPSA-8
Vacancy Type: National Personnel Service Agreement
Practice Area: Disaster Risk Reduction and Recovery
Bureau: Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific
Contract Duration: 1 Year

Required Languages

Fluency in English and Nepali is required

Mobility required/no mobility: no mobility required

Job Description

Tiered Approach

In line with the commitment to safeguard capacity and support personnel already in the Organization, a majority of UNDP UNCDF/UNV vacancies are advertised using a tiered application process whereby:

Tier 0: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV IP staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments, whose posts will be abolished, or contracts will be terminated or not renewed during 2026.
Tier 1: Other UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding permanent (PA) and fixed-term (FTA) appointments
Tier 2: UNDP/UNCDF/UNV staff holding temporary appointments (TA), personnel on regular PSA contracts, and Expert and Specialist UN Volunteers
Tier 3 or no tier indicated: All other contract types from UNDP/UNCDF/UNV and other agencies, and other external candidates

Please make note of the Tier(s) indicated in the vacancy title, if any, and ensure that you satisfy the eligibility to apply.

Background

While climate change is observed across Nepal, the rate of temperature increase is more pronounced at higher altitudes. This temperature rise accelerates the rate of glacial retreat, increasing the size of glacial lakes located in these high-altitude areas and, in turn, their likelihood of breaching in the form of Glacial Lake Outburst Floods (GLOF) which cause severe flooding, landslides and mudflows that damage infrastructure and private assets, and disrupt transportation networks, agricultural production, power supplies from hydropower plants and tourism activities. Damages from GLOFs are often irreparable for decades, with considerable economic costs, particularly to downstream populations. The risk of GLOFs is further exacerbated by increasing temperatures which increase the rate of snow and ice melt and the proportion of precipitation falling as rain, which increases the volume of the lakes, thereby reducing the amount of ‘freeboard’, which increases the likelihood of overflow and the intensity of resulting floods.

The Thulagi, Lower Barun, Lumding Tsho and Hongu 2 Lakes are at exceptionally high risk of breaching having already exhibited considerable increases in volume, accelerated degradation of their ice-cored moraines, and a reduced amount of ‘freeboard’ as a result of climate change. Combined, these factors have destabilized the lakes, exposing the Gandaki Basin and the Dudhkoshi and Arun Sub-basins to the threat of a GLOF event. Without intervention, these glacial lakes could breach at any given moment, adversely impacting vulnerable Nepalese communities.

In response to this risk, USD36 millions of GCF funds, alongside USD14 million in cofinance, will be directed to reduce the risk and impacts of GLOFs at the four priority glacial lakes by shifting towards a proactive approach to GLOF risk reduction in Nepal. The proposed project presents an integrated approach to GLOF risk management in Nepal by addressing institutional and technical capacities, physical protection (both grey and green infrastructure approaches), hazard monitoring and early warning. This integrated approach will utilise GCF funds to: i) lower the water levels of four glacial lakes to reduce their risk of breaching; ii) implement Eco-Disaster Risk Reduction interventions in mountain ecosystems to mitigate the residual flood impacts from a GLOF; iii) establish and implement early warning systems to alleviate damages and prevent the loss of lives from GLOFs; and iv) strengthen the technical and institutional capacity of Nepal’s Department of Hydrology and Meteorology to plan for and respond to GLOFs and floods. These interventions will catalyse a shift from a need- and project-based approach towards proactive and pre-emptive approaches, engendered through strengthened capacity among institutions and communities.

The project will be implemented following UNDP’s support to National Implementation Modality (NIM), with Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) under Ministry of Energy, Water Resources and Irrigation (MoEWRI) of Nepal serving as the Implementing Partner. Under this modality, UNDP is supporting DHM in recruiting key positions for the establishment of a Project Management Unit, which will be based in Kathmandu, Nepal. Members of the PMU will collectively be responsible for overall planning and budgeting, collaborating with other ministries, sectors and government entities to implement the project performance management system; bidding for the provision of project consultancy services; coordination with the responsible parties in terms of bidding of goods and services; disbursement and implementation of project audits, operation of accounts, monitoring and preparation of overall project reports (annual), and safeguards policy monitoring reports.

Duties and Responsibilities

The DRR/M-EWS Analyst will ensure that the project’s multi-hazard EWS interventions are technically sound, socially inclusive, and institutionally sustainable. Service providers will design and install systems, while the Analyst ensures quality assurance, coordination, and integration into national DRR frameworks.

Provide technical oversight of EWS design:

  • Oversee interventions related to the generation and dissemination of early warnings, verifying quality of materials, techniques, and final finishes.
  • Review and validate EWS designs, SOPs, and protocols.
  • Ensure early warnings are inclusive and reach vulnerable communities.
  • In collaboration with the Hydrological and Meteorological experts, support the technical and institutional capacity development of DHM to produce early warnings and disseminate them to government agencies and productive sectors.
  • Oversee the development of community-based response plans, multi-hazard-based risk assessments (integrating community knowledge and science-based assessments), and training of communities on disaster risk management.
  • Oversee the development of climate-responsive Municipal Disaster Preparedness and Response Plans.

Oversee system installation and operation:

  • In collaboration with the Hydrological and Meteorological experts, monitor and guide contractors during installation and commissioning of EWS components.
  • Certify deliverables and ensure proper documentation for payments.

Contribute to knowledge management and build institutional and community capacity:

  • Conduct training for government personnel and community groups.
  • Support drills, simulations, and awareness campaigns.
  • Develop knowledge and awareness material on access and response to early warnings, including for the establishment and mobilisation of youth groups and volunteer’s corps.
  • Document good practices and lessons for replication.

Oversight and reporting:

  • Certify completion and quality of works related to the installation and operation of hydrological equipment, ensuring documentation is in place for payments, handovers, and audit requirements.
  • Maintain equipment records, compile periodic technical reports, and provide updates to PMU/PIU in line with UNDP/GON/GEF standards.
  • Ensure that all project data and information on physical and financial progress related to DRM and EWS systems are duly maintained with transparently, expediently, and effectively in line with UNDP rules and regulations
  • Contribute to annual workplans and budgeting within the PMU as related to DRM and EWS systems, applying adaptive management principles.
  • Monitor the progress of DRM and EWS interventions according to annual work plan, ensuring that targets are fully met and the reporting requirements are fulfilled, and provide technical inputs to donor reports and evaluations.
  • Contribute to the inclusion of EWS in Environmental and Social Management Plans (ESMPs).

Ensure Gender and Social inclusion considerations in the project and facilitate knowledge sharing

  • Mainstream GESI considerations in disaster risk reduction (DRR) and early warning systems (EWS) by ensuring risk assessments, preparedness, and response strategies address the specific needs of women, men, youth, elderly persons, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities.
  • Strengthen inclusive participation by engaging diverse community groups—including women’s groups, disability organizations, and indigenous representatives—in the design, testing, and dissemination of community based EWS and DRR interventions.
  • Ensure accessibility of information and communication systems by developing and promoting gender- and disability-responsive early warning messages in local languages and formats that are understandable and usable by all.
  • Collect and utilize sex, age, and disability disaggregated data to identify differential vulnerabilities and capacities, ensuring evidence-based recommendations for inclusive DRR and climate resilience planning.
  • Identify, synthesize and document best practices and lessons learned that are generated from the project and implementing partners.

Disaster Information Management System (DIMS) and Data Management for Early Warning Systems

  • Lead and support the planning, development, and operationalization of a Disaster Information Management System (DIMS) to systematically manage data generated from Early Warning Systems (EWS), hydrometeorological monitoring, risk assessments, and community-based DRM interventions.
  • Establish data management frameworks, standards, and protocols to ensure the consistent collection, validation, storage, analysis, visualization, and dissemination of disaster risk and early warning data in line with national systems and international best practices.
  • Ensure interoperability and integration of EWS-related data with existing national platforms and information systems of the Department of Hydrology and Meteorology (DHM) and other relevant government entities.
  • Support the development of dashboards, decision-support tools, and reporting mechanisms to enable timely, evidence-based decision-making for preparedness, response, and anticipatory action.
  • The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organisation

Institutional Arrangement

The PMU will be headed by the Project Coordination Specialist (PCS). The Disaster Risk Reduction/Management and Early Warning System Analyst will report directly to the Project Coordination Specialist. The PMU will operate under the overall guidance of the National Project Director (NPD) — as assigned by MoEWRI.

Competencies

Core

  • Achieve Results: LEVEL 1 Plans and monitors own work, pays attention to details, delivers quality work by deadline
  • Think Innovatively: LEVEL 1 Open to creative ideas/known risks, is pragmatic problem solver, makes improvements
  • Learn Continuously: LEVEL 1 Open minded and curious, shares knowledge, learns from mistakes, asks for feedback
  • Adapt with Agility: LEVEL 1 Adapts to change, constructively handles ambiguity/uncertainty, is flexible
  • Act with Determination: LEVEL 1 Shows drive and motivation, able to deliver calmly in face of adversity, confident
  • Engage and Partner: LEVEL 1 Demonstrates compassion/understanding towards others, forms positive relationships
  • Enable Diversity and Inclusion: LEVEL 1 Appreciate/respect differences, aware of unconscious bias, confront discrimination

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies Digital

  • Geospatial analysis:

Skilled in techniques which study entities using their topological, geometric, or geographic properties.

Business Management

Partnerships Management

Build and maintain partnerships with wide networks of stakeholders, Governments, civil society and private sector partners, experts and others in line with UNDP strategy and policies

Risk Management

Identify and organize action around reducing, mitigating and proactively managing risks

Procurement

Knowledge of strategic sourcing concepts, principles and methods, and ability to apply this to strategic and/or practical situations

Minimum Qualifications of the Successful NPSA Min. Education requirements

  • Advanced University Degree (master’s degree or equivalent) in Disaster Risk Management, Engineering, Environmental Sciences, or other relevant discipline is required.
    or
  • A first-level university degree (bachelor’s degree) in the above-mentioned fields in combination with additional 2 years of relevant experience will be given due consideration in lieu of master’s degree.

Min. years of relevant work experience

  • Applicants with master’s degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field of study are not required to have professional work experience.
  • Applicants with a bachelor’s degree (or equivalent) are required to have a minimum of two (2) years of working experience in disaster risk management and early warning systems

Desired skills in addition to the competencies covered in the Competencies section

  • Experience in DRR, EWS, and hazard risk management.
  • Experience in developing operational protocols and training.
  • Experience and understanding of gender and social inclusion in early warning systems and anticipatory action
  • Experience with World Meteorological Organization (WMO) frameworks and Sendai DRR targets.
