Position: Business Analyst

We are looking for a Business Analyst to bridge the gap between business needs, customer requirements, UX, and technology teams. The role will be responsible for understanding and analyzing business and customer needs, translating them into clear and actionable requirements, and supporting the successful delivery of new products, features, and enhancements

Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field.
  • 3–5 years of relevant experience as a Business Analyst, Product Analyst, Systems Analyst, or in a similar role.
  • Proven experience in business requirement gathering, requirement analysis, BRD preparation, stakeholder management, and cross-functional coordination.
  • Experience working with UX/UI, Engineering, QA, and business teams in a product or technology-driven environment.
  • Hands-on experience in supporting the end-to-end product development lifecycle, from requirement gathering to testing, deployment, and post-release analysis.
  • Experience in Agile/Scrum methodologies and working with cross-functional technology teams will be an advantage.
  • Experience in FinTech, digital payments, banking, e-commerce, or other digital platforms will be preferred.

Job Description

Business Requirement & Product Development

  • Prepare and maintain Business Requirement Documents (BRDs) for new products, services, features, and product ideas.
  • Gather, analyze, validate, and document business and customer requirements, ensuring alignment with business objectives and user needs.
  • Collaborate with UX/UI teams to define and refine end-to-end product journeys based on business requirements and customer pain points.
  • Liaise with Engineering and Technology teams throughout the development lifecycle to clarify requirements, resolve queries, and ensure accurate implementation.
  • Coordinate with relevant stakeholders during development, testing, User Acceptance Testing (UAT), and deployment to ensure that requirements are correctly implemented.
  • Support the delivery of fully tested, verified, and business-ready products and features within agreed timelines.

Product Enhancement & Change Requests

  • Identify and analyze customer feedback, user pain points, operational challenges, and business requirements to identify opportunities for product and feature enhancements.
  • Prepare Change Requests (CRs) for existing products and features, clearly documenting the business rationale, requirements, scope, and expected outcomes.
  • Coordinate with UX/UI and Engineering teams to support the design and implementation of product enhancements.
  • Validate completed enhancements against defined requirements and acceptance criteria before release.
  • Support post-release monitoring to ensure that implemented changes address the identified business or customer needs.

Requirement & Stakeholder Management

  • Engage with cross-functional stakeholders to gather and understand requirements, business processes, and pain points.
  • Facilitate requirement-gathering sessions, discussions, and workshops with relevant stakeholders.
  • Analyze and prioritize requirements based on business value, customer impact, feasibility, urgency, and organizational priorities.
  • Translate business requirements into clear and actionable documentation for UX, Engineering, QA, and other relevant teams.
  • Maintain a single source of truth for requirements, scope, decisions, assumptions, and changes throughout the product development lifecycle.
  • Identify requirement gaps, dependencies, risks, and potential conflicts and facilitate timely resolution.

Data Analysis & Continuous Improvement

  • Analyze product, customer, and user metrics following product and feature releases to evaluate performance and adoption.
  • Use data and customer insights to identify trends, gaps, and opportunities for product improvement.
  • Support A/B testing and experimentation by helping define business objectives, hypotheses, success metrics, and analyzing results.
  • Provide data-driven insights and recommendations to support business and product-related decision-making.
  • Continuously evaluate existing processes and products and recommend improvements based on customer needs, business priorities, and performance data.

Continuous Learning

  • Participate in relevant training, workshops, and professional development programs to enhance business analysis and product development capabilities.
  • Stay updated on industry trends, emerging technologies, business analysis practices, and digital product development methodologies.
  • Apply relevant industry knowledge and best practices to improve the quality and effectiveness of business analysis and requirement management.

  • Analytical Skills

  • Customer-centric mindset
  • Strong ownership and accountability
  • Attention to detail

  • Critical thinking and problem-solving

  • Ability to work independently and collaboratively

content.rendered:
NNSWA has been actively working with various community development projects in Sudurpaschim Province of Nepal for more than three and half decades. It has significant years of experience working in the sector of DRRM/CCA and humanitarian response, Education, Health, Livelihoods, HIV and AIDS, Nutrition, Physical Rehabilitation Services for the People with Disability along, Stop Leprosy with other development sectors and has been closely working with different funding partners and all levels of the government. NNSWA is going to implement DRM and HEA RISE Project, in Kanchanpur and Kailali Districts in partnership with World Vision International Nepal. Therefore, NNSWA announces the vacancy for applying for the following position.

Position: Project Coordinator

Required No: (1) One

Base Station: Kanchanpur/Kailali Project Office and frequent visit to Project Implementing Municipalities

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:

The Project Coordinator is responsible for the overall coordination, management, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of the RISE project, funded by the US Government and implemented by Nepal National Social Welfare Association (NNSWA) with the technical support from World Vision International Nepal. The position ensures effective delivery of project objectives, donor compliance and organizational requirements, safeguarding and quality assurance, stakeholder coordination, budget management, and effective humanitarian response maintaining the core principles of humanitarian standards.

Required Qualifications and experience:

Academic Qualification:

  • Master’s degree in environmental science, DRR&M, Social Science or a related field or Bachelor’s degree with substantial relevant experience in DRR and emergency response may be considered.

Experience:

  • Four years of experience in implementing DRR, humanitarian response-related programs and experience in managing projects including people and budget management
  • Experience working with local government authorities, humanitarian clusters, and local communities.
  • Strong knowledge of CBDRR approaches and humanitarian response including early warning system, strengthening local capacity.
  • Understanding of legal documents on DRR&M, humanitarian structure, emergency response mechanisms, and humanitarian principles and standards
  • Proficiency in oral and written communication in English and Nepali.
  • Strong project cycle management and budget management skills.
  • Excellent coordination, networking and stakeholder engagement abilities.
  • Strong analytical, report writing and documentation skills.
  • Experience in data analysis and MEAL system

Position: DRR and Humanitarian Field Officer (RISE)

Required No.: (2) Two

Base Station: Kanchanpur: Krishnapur Municipality and One Rural Municipality-1 Kailali: Gauriganga Municipality and Ghodaghodi Municiplaity-1

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:

The DRR and Humanitarian Officer is responsible for planning, implementing, monitoring, and reporting Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and emergency response activities of the RISE project, funded by the US Government and implemented by Nepal National Social Welfare Association (NNSWA) with the technical support from World Vision International Nepal. This position is required to work closely with district and local stakeholders to support vulnerable communities to strengthen resilience through the implementation of interventions related to disaster preparedness, risk reduction measures, and effective humanitarian response in line with organizational standards, humanitarian principles and donor compliance.

Required Qualifications and experience:

Academic Qualification:

  • Bachelor’s degree in environmental science, DRR&M, Social Science or a related field.

Experience:

  • Two years of experience in implementing DRR, humanitarian response-related programs
  • Experience working with local government authorities and local communities.
  • Understanding of legal documents on DRR&M, humanitarian structure, emergency response mechanisms, anticipatory action framework, and humanitarian principles and standards
  • Proficiency in oral and written communication in English and Nepali.
  • Excellent coordination, networking and stakeholder engagement abilities.
  • Strong report writing and documentation skills.

Position: MEAL Officer

Required No.: (1) One

Base Station:Kanchanpur/Kailali Project Office and frequent visit to Project Implementing Municipalities

GENERAL POSITION SUMMARY:

The MEAL Officer is responsible and executes day-to-day monitoring, evaluation, accountability, and learning processes at the district and community levels under Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR) and emergency response activities of the RISE project, funded by the US Government and implemented by Nepal National Social Welfare Association (NNSWA) with the technical support from World Vision International Nepal. This role ensures that all field data of the project is clean, timely, and compliant with WVI Nepal standards . The officer works directly on the ground, receiving technical templates, guidance, and oversight from the Grant MEAL Coordinator, WVI Nepal and report to the Project Coordinator.

Required Qualifications and experience:

Academic Qualification:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social science, Development Studies, or a field relevant to MEAL.

Details

Mission and objectives

UNDP in Nepal

VISION STATEMENT

UNDP Nepal works with the people and Government of Nepal, and other development partners to pursue equitable and sustainable human development goals through eradication of poverty, increase in livelihood opportunities, improvement in community resilience against conflict, disasters and impact of climate change, while laying down strong foundations for a society based on rule of law with an inclusive and participatory democracy.

Context

Pokhara, Nepal’s tourism capital, faces complex, interconnected challenges including youth out-migration, a fragmented informal economy, environmental degradation, and siloed public services. To address these systemic issues, UNDP Nepal and Pokhara Metropolitan City (PMC) have initiated the Pokhara Green Digital Portfolio, an adaptive framework designed to catalyze long-term, sustainable urban transformation.

The portfolio is structured around three core transformation shifts ( Outputs):

  •  Resilient and Digital Governance as a steering mechanism for the green transition.
  •  Youth-led Entrepreneurship Ecosystem to diversify the local economy.
  • Green Tourism ( Regenerative and circular) to create a sustainable, value-adding economic model.To drive this agenda, UNDP is seeking a dedicated, dynamic expert to be based on the ground in Pokhara. This role is critical for managing day-to-day portfolio implementation, fostering a multi-stakeholder coalition, and translating the strategic vision into tangible, on-the-ground actions. The UN Volunteer will also support user research and coordination for the Service Blueprint and Youth Entrepreneur Persona Study for Business Registration in Pokhara”.

Task description

Under the direct supervision of the Portfolio Manager and the close guidance of the Head of the Field Office (Gandaki and Lumbini Provinces), the Portfolio Coordinator will carry out responsibilities across four key pillars:

3.1 Portfolio Coordination and Dynamic Management

  •  Support the day-to-day coordination and dynamic management of the Green Digital Portfolio and its three strategic shifts by coordinating activities, tracking progress, risks, decisions and follow up actions.
  •  Facilitate the development and regular updating of the Green Digital Portfolio workplan.
  •  Support portfolio monitoring, learning, and adaptation by documenting implementation updates, emerging insights, and evidence for Funding Window dynamic management and reporting.
  • Support regular portfolio review and reflection processes to inform workplan adjustments, partners coordination, and resource mobilization.

3.2 Stakeholder Coordination and Platform Building

  • Act as the primary focal point for building and maintaining strong working relationships with Pokhara Metropolitan City, private sector actors, academic institutions, youth organizations, civil society, and relevant partners.
  •  Support the finalization and implementation of the Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) between UNDP and Pokhara Metropolitan City.
  •  Help co-design and operationalize a practical joint-management mechanism for the portfolio
  •  Facilitate the implementation of the activities assigned to PMC, as part of the joint work plan of the Portfolio.
  •  Arrange, facilitate, and document regular multi-stakeholder meetings, workshops, and coordination sessions to ensure collaborative progress.

3.3 Support to Research and Strategic Development

  •  Coordinate and support the user research for The Service Blueprint and Youth Entrepreneur Persona Study for Business Registration in Pokhara, including coordination with users, municipal counterparts, and technical experts.
  • Support research team for organizing interviews, consultations, user mapping, documentation, and validation activities with youth entrepreneurs and business service actors.
  • Support the research team in synthesizing user needs and pain points into practical inputs for the design of targeted interventions that support young entrepreneurs (e.g., incubation, access to finance, market linkages).

3.4 Gender and Social Inclusion (GESI)

  •  Ensure GESI principles are systematically mainstreamed across all portfolio’s co-design and decision-making processes.
  •  Support and actively work to ensure the inclusion of women, youth, marginalized groups, and less represented enterprise actors in consultation, user research and all portfolio activities.
  •  Support the creation of a safe and respectful working environment for all partners and participants.

Eligibility criteria

Age: 18 – 80

Required experience: 7 years

Nationality: Candidate must be a national, legal resident or hold refugee status in the country of assignment.

Assignment requirements

English, Level: Fluent, Required

Accountability | Adaptability and Flexibility | Creativity | Judgement and Decision-Making | Planning and Organising | Professionalism | Self-Management

Skills and experience

  • At least 7 years of professional experience in project management, local development and partnership building, or multi-stakeholder programme implementation.
  •  At least 3 years of hands-on experience in enterprise development
  •  Demonstrated experience working with municipal governments, private sector entities, and civil society organizations in Nepal.
  •  Research & Design: Experience in user research, service design, business process mapping, and digitization is highly desirable.
  •  Familiarity with system thinking, portfolio approaches /integrated approaches, and learning-oriented implementation is an advantage.
  •  Interpersonal Skills: Culturally and socially sensitive, with the ability to work inclusively with a range of partners.

Area(s) of expertise

Project management, programme development, strategy, Partnerships, resource mobilisation, Governance, elections

Volunteerism is understood as a wide range of activities undertaken of free will, for the general public good, for which monetary reward is not the principal motivating factor.

Living conditions and remarks

This assignment will be based in Pokhara, the capital of Gandaki Province. Pokhara is a major urban center with excellent living conditions, including access to modern housing, amenities, and reliable transportation. The UN Volunteer will be responsible for arranging their own housing and other living essentials. The role requires extensive engagement within Pokhara and may involve frequent local travel. The security situation is stable, but the volunteer is expected to strictly adhere to all UN security guidelines.

Position: Monitoring, Evaluation & Learning Officer (Nepal)

Location: Kathmandu

Lutheran World Relief, which is part of Corus International, has been present in Nepal since 2011. Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class organizations working to deliver the holistic, lasting solutions needed to end extreme poverty once and for all. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our nonprofit and for-profit subsidiaries include IMA World Health and its fundraising brand Corus World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and Farmers Market Brands. In Nepal, Corus operates under Lutheran World Relief. Our more than 400 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world’s most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives.

At Corus we believe that good only grows stronger and we reflect that belief in our workplace culture. We value every employee’s specialized area of expertise and nurture professional growth. We promote an engaging and supportive work environment, where employees feel enabled and driven to innovate, learn and collaborate. And because our subsidiaries often function as partners, our employees have the opportunity to work across our enterprise family.

Job Brief:

This position will be an employee of Lutheran World Relief. The RISE Fund project strengthens disaster preparedness, governance, and resilience in Nepal’s most vulnerable provinces, Karnali and Sudurpaschim. The program runs across multiple sectors to reduce humanitarian risks and build inclusive disaster risk management systems.

The program has four interlinked components:

  • Emergency Preparedness & Coordination – establishing rapid response teams, provincial search and rescue units, and activating emergency operations centers.
  • Shelter & Relief Support – pre-positioning emergency supplies, constructing temporary shelters, and ensuring rapid deployment within 24-72 hours after disasters.
  • Health & WASH Services – training health workers, deploying mobile medical camps, distributing dignity kits, and restoring safe water and sanitation systems.
  • Protection & Logistics – providing mental health and psychosocial support, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and creating an emergency transportation fund for rapid deployment.
  • The project aims to work with the provincial government to enable them to target 13 priority districts and 116 municipalities, directly benefiting over 30,000 individuals and indirectly reaching more than 500,000 people. The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer is a project-based position to support the implementation of anticipated DRR, Health Preparedness, Emergency and Humanitarian Response programming in the Karnali and Sudurpaschim Provinces in Nepal. MEL Officer reports to the DRR, Emergency and Humanitarian Response Manger and will have functional relationship with Senior Program Director,
  • Senior Program Manager (Agriculture and Livelihoods) and Kathmandu based administration and finance team. The position holder is expected to spend 30%of time in field especially in above two provinces and 25% of time in LWR other projects (especially PunarUtthan) working closely with the Senior Manager.

Position Summary:

The Monitoring, Evaluation and Learning (MEL) Officer is responsible for strengthening the project’s MEL system by ensuring high-quality data collection, analysis, reporting, and evidence generation. The position supports project monitoring, assessments, learning, and adaptive management while building the capacity of implementing partners and promoting the use of digital and AI-enabled solutions to improve data quality and decision-making.

Responsibilities:

  • Maintain and regularly update project databases, monitoring tools, indicators, supporting evidence, case studies, and other MEL documentation.
  • Plan, coordinate, and support household surveys, focus group discussions (FGDs), key informant interviews (KIIs), rapid assessments, baseline/endline studies, readiness assessments, outcome harvesting, and other monitoring and evaluation activities.
  • Review the partner’s periodic narrative reports including Performance Monitoring Plan (PMP), Beneficiary Tracking Table, Indicator Tracking Table and Activity Tracking Table and provide inputs on timely basis to ensure the data and information are correct and validated.
  • Ensure the quality, accuracy, completeness, and timely validation of project data in accordance with organizational and donor requirements.
  • Analyze monitoring and assessment findings and support the preparation of high-quality monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor reports in collaboration with the line manager.
  • Facilitate participatory action research, document Most Significant Change (MSC) stories, lessons learned, innovations, and evidence-based best practices for knowledge sharing and adaptive management.
  • Provide training, mentoring, coaching, and technical support to project staff and implementing partners on MEL systems, data collection tools, data quality assurance, and reporting standards.
  • Support the development, strengthening, and regular maintenance of digital MEL databases, dashboards, and information management systems.
  • Promote organizational learning by documenting project achievements, challenges, cross-learning events, and disseminating evidence-based findings to internal and external stakeholders.
  • Provide technical MEL support to other Corus/LWR projects and programs, as assigned, to strengthen organizational monitoring, evaluation, and learning practices.
  • Promote and facilitate the integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), digital technologies, and innovative approaches to improve data collection, analysis, visualization, reporting, and knowledge management across projects.

Supervisory: None

Education and Experience:

  • Bachelor’s degree in social science, public health, public administration or related field.
  • A minimum of three (3) years of demonstrated experience in the field of monitoring, evaluation, learning or project management with I/NGOs preferably in DRR and emergency health projects.

Knowledge, Skills and Abilities:

  • Knowledge of humanitarian standards.
  • Knowledge of health management information system (HMIS) will be a plus.
  • Ability to work effectively both independently and as part of a team.
  • Ability to implement and manage technical project activities and collaborate across multiple teams.
  • Strong skills in programmatic data analysis, report writing and documentation.
  • Strong negotiation, coordination, communication, and interpersonal skills (diplomacy, patience), believing in teamwork with the ability to perform multiple tasks and work under pressure.
  • Fluent in English and Nepali (speaking and writing)
  • Willingness to contribute and trust in teamwork.
  • Proficiency in Office 365 applications including Word, Excel, SharePoint, and PowerPoint.

Physical and Mental Requirements:

  • The physical requirements that may be needed to execute responsibilities may include bending, standing, and walking, etc.
  • The mental requirements that are essential to satisfactorily executing the responsibilities outlined in this job description include, but not limited to: learning new tasks, comprehending, and retaining information, completing tasks independently, effectively communicating verbally and in writing, demonstrating proficiency in using computer software to perform assigned tasks.

While performing the duties of this job in different locations, the employee may be exposed to precarious settings under high-security risks and/or very basic living conditions and outside weather conditions, as well as to infectious diseases.

The Organization:

Lutheran World Relief, which is part of Corus International, has been present in Nepal since 2011. We are a global leader in international development, with 150 years of combined experience across our brands. Our more than 400 employees around the globe are experts in their fields and dedicated to helping the world’s most vulnerable people break the cycle of poverty and lead healthy lives.
At Corus we believe that good only grows stronger and we reflect that belief in our workplace culture. We value every employee’s specialized area of expertise and nurture professional growth. Job Brief:

Position Summary: This position will be an employee of Lutheran World Relief. The RISE Fund project strengthens disaster preparedness, governance, and resilience in Nepal’s most vulnerable provinces, Karnali and Sudurpaschim. The program runs across multiple sectors to reduce humanitarian risks and build inclusive disaster risk management systems.

The program has four interlinked components:

  • Emergency Preparedness & Coordination – establishing rapid response teams, provincial search and rescue units, and activating emergency operations centers.
  • Shelter & Relief Support – pre-positioning emergency supplies, constructing temporary shelters, and ensuring rapid deployment within 24-72 hours after disasters.
  • Health & WASH Services – training health workers, deploying mobile medical camps, distributing dignity kits, and restoring safe water and sanitation systems.
  • Protection & Logistics – providing mental health and psychosocial support, safeguarding vulnerable groups, and creating an emergency transportation fund for rapid deployment.

The project aims to work with the provincial government to enable them to target 13 priority districts and 116 municipalities, directly benefiting over 30,000 individuals and indirectly reaching more than 500,000 people.

CAD Jumla is an autonomous, independent, nonprofit making independent, non-governmental organization (NGO) working in areas of promoting human rights and developmental activities. It was established in 2009 AD, by the enthusiastic youths of Jumla; lawyers, social workers, health worker, journalists, human rights activists and intellectuals to facilitate in promoting human rights and continuing developmental activities based on the principle of “for the Karnali people with the Karnali people and by the Karnali people” for establishing just and prosperous Karnali region by acknowledging the adversity and diversity of the region in terms of geographical remoteness, economic hardships, traditional practices and rich flora and fauna. The organization has been working on need based action orientated multi-disciplinary areas through social mobilization especially focusing on human rights, Women Empower, agriculture and School WASH.

CAD Jumla has been implementing the “Empowered Girls, Safe Community project” in partnership with Plan International Nepal. The project will be implemented in Hima, Sinja and Kanakasundari Rural Municipality of Jumla district. The key goal of the project is that all child, adolescent and young (CAY) particularly girls and young women enjoy their rights to live free from child, early and forced marriage (CEFM).

Position: Monitoring and Evaluation (M&E) Officer- One (Only for Female Candidate)

*Candidates who have previously applied, need not reapply.*

Contract Type: C-SC -7

Duty Station: Based at CAD Jumla field office Sinja Rural Municipality, Jumla (Frequent travel to Hima, Sinja and Kanakasundari Rural Municipalities to project areas)

Job period: Till June 2027 most probably can extend to June 2028

Reports to: Project Coordinator (CAD Nepal & PACE Nepal Jumla)

Technical Reporting: Executive Director (CAD Nepal), Executive Director (PACE Nepal) and MERL Focal Person, Plan International Nepal

Salary and Benefits: As per the organization’s norms commensurate with the project agreement

1. Job Summary: The Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) Officer is responsible for establishing and strengthening the project Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability and Learning (MEAL) system across both consortium partners (CAD Nepal and PACE Nepal). The position will ensure high-quality data management, monitoring, documentation, reporting, accountability mechanisms, learning processes and evidence generation for all project interventions related to Child Protection, Child Sponsorship, Livelihood, Disaster Risk Reduction (DRR), Youth Empowerment and Gender Equality.

The M&E Officer will work closely with both consortium organizations to ensure standardized monitoring systems, quality reporting and effective utilization of project evidence for decision-making.

2. Key responsibilities and tasks

A. Compliance to policies, rules/regulations and guidelines

Adhere policies, rules & regulations and guidelines of CAD Nepal, PACE Nepal and Plan International Nepal including safeguarding children and program participants.

B. Monitoring Evaluation and Learning (MERL) System and Support

  • Ensure the proper implementation of the Result-Based M&E framework and Log Frame; orient field staff and project team on adherence to these frameworks.
  • Develop and maintain project monitoring systems for both CAD Nepal and PACE Nepal, ensuring consistency of monitoring tools across consortium partners.
  • Ensure all monitoring tools are GESI responsive (meaning they are designed to disaggregate data by sex, age, people/children with disability, ethnicity and geography)
  • Support district-based staff conducting baseline, Annual Data Collection, End-Line studies, in house assessment, Child Marriage Prevalence Survey and Knowledge, Attitude, and Practice (KAP) surveys.
  • Provide technical inputs to ensure survey and methodologies are inclusive (e.g. accessible formats for persons with disability, safe space for women etc.

C. Data Management, Quality Assurance & Reporting

  • Track progress against project outputs, outcomes, and indicators.
  • Collect routine project data, compile, and review to ensure quality deliverables.
  • Analyze monthly, semiannual, and annual coverage/people reached (focusing on Sponsored Children and marginalized groups).
  • Disaggregate all qualitative data and conduct qualitative analysis to measure how project interventions are affecting women, men, boys, girls, Dalit, and persons with dasibilties.
  • Prepare Monthly MEL reports and support the Project Coordinator in preparing periodic progress reports and database reports for Plan International Nepal. Support PCs to highlight GESI related achievement, barriers, and adaptive measure in all narrative reports.
  • Ensure the quality and confidentiality of all project data and information. Ensure that data handling practice protect vulnerable respondents from stigma or harm, particularly when collecting sensitive or protection related data.

D. Monitoring, Field Visits & Verification

  • Conduct routine monitoring visits, verify project achievements through field observation and data validation, and provide evidence-based synthesized report.
  • Actively triangulate data by conducting separate Focus Group Discussions (FGDs) with women-only, men-only, and mixed groups to capture diverse voices, including those often excluded from community dialogues.
  • Monitor whether project activities are physically and socially accessible to persons with disabilities and whether they actively challenge harmful gender norms and power imbalances in the community
  • Carry out routine field monitoring and share findings with project staff and the Plan MERL Unit. Ensure findings are analyzed through a GESI lens before sharing, highlighting any unintended negative consequences on marginalized groups
  • Promote use of Quality Monitoring Tools (QMT) and document evidence-based recommendations and action items.
  • Plan and Guide field staffs through regular monitoring and share findings with project staff and the Plan MEL section.
  • Analyze and discuss monitoring findings with the Executive Director, Project Coordinator, and field staff.

E. Capacity Building & Staff Support

  • Enhance the capacity of non-MEL staff on MEL requirements, systems, and proper documentation.
  • Conduct orientation sessions for field staff on GESI-responsive data collection techniques, including how to ask sensitive questions, avoid interviewer bias, and ensure the meaningful participation of women and persons with disabilities in monitoring activities.
  • Provide necessary feedback to project staff and support course correction during implementation.

F. Learning, Documentation & Knowledge Management

  • Prepare and document success stories, best practices, and lessons learned; share these with the team, community, and local/district line agencies.
  • Capture and uplift success stories of transformative change
  • Support field staff in maintaining/updating information at Watch Groups, Child Rights Committees, Inter-Religious Groups, Youth Networks, and Child Clubs.

G. Stakeholder Coordination & Advocacy

  • Establish sound relations and coordination with stakeholders, consortium partner, and the funding partner (Plan International Nepal).
  • Support the project in organizing regular review/reflection meetings and joint monitoring visits with Rural Municipalities and key stakeholders.
  • Ensure that review meetings include GESI focal persons from the Rural Municipality and that feedback from women and marginalized groups is systematically presented to decision-makers
  • Promote Community Engagement and Accountability (CEA) of CAD, PACE and Plan International Nepal. Ensure feedback received from stakeholders is communicated to the Project Lead and Board for better response.
  • Flag any GESI-related grievances or exclusion risks to the Project Lead immediately for remedial action.

H. Others

  • Any other duties towards achievement of project objectives assigned by the line Manager and Program Specialist/concerned staff of Plan International.

3. Academic Qualification, Experience and Competencies

a. Academic Qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree (Preferred Master’s degree) in Public Health, social science and any discipline from recognized institutions with minimum of three years of working experience in similar Position and themes.
  • Experience in Child Protection, SOYEE & DRR and in mountain districts would be an added advantage.

b. Required Professional and Social Competencies

  • Strong inter-personal, communication, negotiation and facilitation skills;
  • Experience in establishing and maintaining collaborative relationships with rural municipalities, community groups and other agencies working in project area;
  • Fluency in both (written and oral) English and Nepali;
  • Proven experience with quantitative and qualitative data collection and analysis
  • Strong capacity and creativity in leading and facilitating participatory methodologies to meaningfully engage beneficiaries, including children, and receiving their feedback through approaches such as social audit
  • Excellent knowledge and skills in Windows, Word, Excel, PowerPoint and data analysis tools and software.
  • Experience in program data management, use of data management electronic devices such as tablets is highly desirable
  • Willing to travel extensively to the project implemented sites and able to accommodate and adjust with local community/ stakeholders;
  • Sensitivity towards issues related to child protection, gender, social equality and poverty alleviation.
  • Sensitive and seriousness with safety and security system.

Link: CV format

Interested results-oriented candidates who meet the above-mentioned required qualifications and experiences can submit applications in the given format at cadrecruit2020@gmail.com by Thursday, July 30, 2026, before 5:00 PM.

Encourage people from disadvantaged and marginalized communities (Women, Dalit, Indigenous, Madhesi, Muslim and people with disabilities) to apply. Local candidates will be given high priority. Only short-listed candidates will be notified for selection process. Telephone inquiries shall not be entertained.

Candidates applying for a job with CAD Jumla must be ready to comply with our Child Protection Policy and Safeguarding Policy on Preventing Harassment, Sexual Exploitation, and Abuse.

content.rendered:
Posiiton: Multimedia Content & Video Production Assistant
Number of Positions: 1
Location: Kathmandu

Organization Description

The Why: NEPAL aspires to graduate from least developing country to a lower middle-income country by 2026. However, the development community’s excessive focus today on socio-political empowerment has not yielded the desired economic transformation. In reaching the 2026 national target, shall we wait for institutions of power to become accountability productive or shall we bolster innovations of people to bring inclusive prosperity? How do we strengthen grassroots-government collaboration in shaping an equal and enterprising future?

The How: DAAYITWA, with a focus on economic empowerment, envisions an enterprising Nepal where every youth has opportunities for a prosperous future. Daayitwa is a part of the Daayitwa Abhiyaan which consists of four organizations: Daayitwa, Governance Lab, Nepal Leadership Academy based in Nepal and Nepal Rising (Daayitwa-US) based in the U.S. Inspired by shared values of innovation, collaboration, and service, it promotes the socio- economic development of Nepal. The movement fosters inclusive and equitable economic growth by accelerating grassroots innovations, strengthening government institutions, and revitalizing a virtuous cycle of democracy and development through grassroots-government collaboration.

Our Focus Areas:

1. Promote enterprise-led employment creation

2. Design evidence-based policies for improved decision-making

3. Build state capability for effective policy implementation

4. Foster stakeholder collaboration for governance innovations

Daayitwa runs several programs and initiatives aimed at our focus area. These key programs include:

Growth Entrepreneurship and Employment Promotion (GEEP) Program: GEEP accelerates rural enterprises for boosting employment and income growth in rural Nepal. GEEP is executed through a partnership among Daayitwa, Gandaki and Koshi provincial governments, 10 local governments and the Nepali diaspora.

Daayitwa Nepal Public Service Policy Fellowship Program: Daayitwa supports bureaucrats and parliamentarians in making policy decisions by conducting policy research, building capability of government and strengthening research ecosystem.

Policy and Governance Research: Daayitwa has conducted research on several topics including youth employment, enterprise ecosystem, as well as women’s political and economic empowerment.

Leadership for Economic Governance Program: Daayitwa enables local governments to promote local economic development by enhancing their policy leadership capability and fostering trustful collaboration with other municipal ecosystem stakeholders.

Mission Asha: Mission Aasha is Daayitwa Abhiyaan’s flagship fundraising campaign, which supports and sustains these efforts by mobilizing resources and amplifying impact.

National Governance Symposium: The National Governance Symposium (NGS) is an annual event organized by Governance Lab at Daayitwa Abhiyaan, with Daayitwa as the organizing partner.

Policy and Governance Dialogues: Daayitwa has been organizing policy and governance dialogues to enhance the governance ecosystem of the country.

Job Description

The What: As the Multimedia Content Creator, you will develop engaging visual, written, and multimedia content that communicates Daayitwa’s programs, amplifies the voices of entrepreneurs and communities, supports fundraising efforts, and strengthens the organization’s digital presence.

Responsibilities:

  •  Produce high-quality video content, including entrepreneur stories, donor stewardship videos, event highlights, field documentaries, and short-form content for social media.
  •  Design engaging social media graphics, infographics, presentations, and digital communication materials.
  • Support the implementation of Mission Aasha’s digital communications and fundraising campaigns across multiple platforms.
  • Develop compelling impact stories by collaborating with entrepreneurs, community members, and program teams.
  •  Maintain a well-organized digital asset library for photos, videos, audio files, and other communication resources while ensuring proper consent and data protection.
  •  Provide creative design and layout support for reports, brochures, policy briefs, newsletters, and other organizational publications.
  • Work closely with program and field teams to identify storytelling opportunities and ensure communication products accurately reflect project outcomes.
  •  Support website content updates, basic SEO, social media scheduling, and digital campaign promotion.
  • Stay updated on digital media trends and recommend innovative approaches to enhance Daayitwa’s visibility and engagement.

Qualifications

  •  Academically compelling, with at least Bachelors (Completed or running) in Mass Communications, Public Relations, Journalism or relevant field
  •  Working knowledge of Canva, Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign and/or other design software
  • Relevant experience in multimedia and designing.
  •  Passionately driven by a strong inner calling for economic empowerment of Nepal
  • Understanding of social issues related to economic prosperity, gender equality, youth employment and community-driven development
  •  Independence in tackling complex problems consistently applying creativity, independent judgment and detail orientation
  •  Self-motivated and able to work with minimal oversight with time management skills
  •  Excellent writer and orator in Nepali and English

Additional information

Compensation: Daayitwa will provide compensation on a monthly rate basis. The rate will be mutually agreed upon, commensurate with the level of the required deliverables, the qualifications and experience of the candidate.

content.rendered:
Position: Resource Development and Program Quality Director
Location: Kusunti, KC Tower, Lalitpur, Nepal

With 75 years of experience, our focus is on helping the most vulnerable children overcome poverty and experience fullness of life. We help children of all backgrounds, even in the most dangerous places, inspired by our Christian faith.

Come join our 31,000+ staff working in nearly 100 countries and share the joy of transforming vulnerable children’s life stories!

Employee Contract Type:

International Assignment (WVI – Paid via GCLA) Fixed Term (Fixed Term)

Job Description:

Resource Development and Program Quality (RDPQ) Director is accountable for four major streams of work:

1) Lead the acquisitions team for all non-sponsorship funding streams, including but not limited to: grants from bilateral, multi-national, foundations, private and major donors; project-non-sponsorship, local corporate social investment (CSI), and other emerging impact investments including service contracts with development banks; in order to increase and diversify the resources of World Vision International Nepal to support country strategy goals to address the needs of the most vulnerable children and communities in Nepal;

2) Lead efforts to ensure all World Vision International Nepal’s Projects meet relevant donors’, government, and World Vision International’s technical quality and compliance requirements (including sponsorship and non-sponsorship funding); and

3) Streamlining World Vision International Nepal’s design, monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning systems contributing to innovative and improved evidence for quality improvement, policy influence, international funding acquisitions and country strategy implementation plan (CSIP)

4) Oversight of the Nepal Innovation Lab, ensuring it is bringing new thinking and innovation into Nepal and the wider region’s programs, in addition to ensuring it is adequately funded in order to operate effectively.

MAJOR RESPONSIBILITIES

Leading efforts to acquire new international funding from existing and new donors. Tasks may include the following but not limited to:

  • Lead the WVI Nepal Resource Development Team, including the Grant Acquisition Manager, to build and achieve strong annual funding targets that are both ambitious and aligned with the international and national funding pipeline.
  • Proactively build multi-year funding strategy in coordination with National Director, with the goal of achieving sustainable funding for World Vision International Nepal through effective prepositioning and quality concept and proposal submission.
  • Implement WVI Nepal’s Acquisition Strategy aligned with Nepal Country Strategy and donor landscape, ensuring the broader World Vision International ecosystem including.
  • Support Offices and Regional Office are committed to supporting the delivery of the strategy
  • Ensure clear and solid internal ‘content’ review and coordination ‘process’, of all new concepts and proposals development in coordination with the Grants Acquisition Manager and cross-function team and World Vision Support Offices.
  • Ensure innovative ideas are incorporated in new concepts or projects proposals development, leveraging WVI Nepal’s Innovation Lab expertise and local and international experiences with the goal of maintaining secure funding source for the Nepal Innovation Lab.
  • Proactively lead and facilitate strategic consortium or partnership agreement with other peer local and INGOs, UN agencies and/or private contractors.
  • In coordination with the National Director, develop and oversee plan of action to position WVI Nepal in order to access local funding landscape – this may involve taking forward a suitable form of local registration.
  • Ensure all projects are aligned to the WVI Nepal country strategy and meet the relevant technical quality standards and compliance, leading team and facilitating Cross-Function collaboration with other departments, tasks may include the following but not limited to:
  • Work closely with Associate Director Program Quality to supervise and advise technical program managers/leads in designing and ensuring all WVI Nepal’s projects meet the quality standards of World Vision International, the relevant sector’s priorities of Government of Nepal, and donor’s standards outlined in project designs.
  • Ensure WVI Nepal’s technical teams remain aligned with current sector priorities, donor requirements, and development standards by actively engaging in relevant technical working groups, government forums, and peer networks; maintaining regular dialogue with sector ministries; promoting the application and sharing of key learnings across teams; and ensuring awareness of and compliance with applicable donor and organizational policies,
  • Support local capacity building and manage performance of all direct reports (GAM, MEAL, PDQ & Innovation Lab Managers), ensuring close collaboration with other WVI departments, including Operations.
  • Provide oversight to the Nepal Innovation Lab, ensuring it is effectively piloting new innovations and scaling up successful concepts in Nepal or across the partnership.
  • Collaborate with other SLT members in ensuring integration of PDQ issues.
  • Promote, engage and collaborate with WV Partnership’s PDQ and Strategy communities
  • Streamline WVI Nepal’s design, monitoring, evaluation and learning systems, contributing to improved evidence for quality improvement, policy influence and international funding acquisitions, tasks may include the following but not limited to:
  • Guide Senior MEAL Manager to ensure coherent measures and monitoring and reporting of all programs (sponsorship, PNS and grants), including alignment with CSIP, OIOS and MEAL global standards
  • Provide high level analytics to Senior Leadership Team on quality of WVI Nepal’s projects and provide technical and strategic recommendations for ongoing improvement.
  • Ensure World Vision’s local partnership approach is implemented effectively and efficiently while continuing to be adapted through best practice to the local context
  • Ensure consistency and quality of all project information from Partner NGOs level, Field Office, National Office and to all donors (internal World Vision Support Offices and external) in order to demonstrate projects impact and contributions of WVI Nepal’s to communities, the Government of Nepal, World Vision Global and donor’s priorities.
  • Ensure WVI Nepal’s relevant project information system comply and provide quality reporting to with World Vision International reporting systems, Power BI and other major systems and acts as an effective knowledge management system.
  • Provide directions, guidance, coaching and technical supports to PDQ team members and ensuring team accountability to deliver and measure the results
  • In collaboration with National Director, External Engagement and Strategy Director, Finance and Corporate Service Director, Field Operations Director and Senior MEAL Manager, support the successful implementation, review and reporting of country strategy and annual business plan, including but not limited to:
  • Co-lead with Field Operations Director in nurturing close communications and partnership with WVI Nepal’s Strategic Support Team/SST, or SOs representative for successful strategy Implementation in WVI Nepal
  • Guide Senior MEAL Manager to ensure coherent measures and monitoring of annual business plan aligned with CSIP and programs M&E
  • Support strategy and Annual Business review process in close collaboration with the National Director and External Engagement and Strategy Director
  • Ensuring World Vision’s local partnership approach is implemented effectively and efficiently while continuing to be adapted through best practice to the local context

KNOWLEDGE/QUALIFICATIONS FOR THE ROLE

Required Professional Experience

  • At least 7-10 years of working in the relevant leadership/managerial position in least developed/developing countries, preferably in Asia region.
  • Familiar with child-focused, multi-sectoral and integrated development programmes. Similar experiences leading and implementing multi-sector in World Vision is an advantage.
  • Proven successful experiences in coordinating and writing winning concept papers or proposals to key donors such as US Government, EU, FCDO, DFAT, GAC, MFAT, Global Fund, Nordic Governments and other donors.
  • Proven analytical skills and relevant experience in facilitating or leading programme design and evaluation, long term programmes plan and strategy development, and streamlining monitoring, evaluation, accountability and learning system in an international organization.
  • Relevant experience on external engagement including with governments and donors for project initiation and maximizing the impact on child well-being.
  • Good understanding on the international needs and development trends and their relevance to Nepal’s development context.
  • Good knowledge of standards and requirement of bilateral and multi-laterals donors.
  • Project or organizational leadership experience managing medium to large team. Cross-cultural team or leadership experience is a plus.
  • Mature personality and able to manage multiple priorities.
  • Ability to manage pressures to meet tight project proposals deadlines and to maintain clarity of programmes and team focus.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.

Required Education, training, license, registration and certification

  • Master’s degree in international development, development studies/management, project management, economics, agriculture, public health, public/social policy, social sciences or equivalent.

Preferred Knowledge and Qualifications

  • Relevant World Vision experience is a plus.
  • Work experiences in Nepal, or South Asia, or South East Asia is preferred

This is a non-accompanied international assignment. Family accompaniment is not provided for this position.

Applicant Types Accepted: Local and International Applicants (IA’s) Accepted

“World Vision is committed to achieving diversity, as the diversity of our teams is critical to our overall success. WV welcomes applications from qualified professionals all over Nepal. Women, people with disability, and members from other marginalized groups are strongly encouraged to apply.”

“Children and vulnerable adults who come into contact with WV as a result of our activities must be safeguarded to the maximum possible extent from deliberate or inadvertent actions and failings that place them at risk of abuse, sexual exploitation, injury, and any other harm. One of the ways that WVI Nepal shows this on-going commitment to safeguarding is to include rigorous background and reference checks in the selection process for all candidates, in accordance to its Child and Adult Safeguarding Policy. WVI Nepal has zero tolerance to child rights’ violations, by employees and/or affiliates.”

WVI Nepal reserves all rights to qualify/disqualify applications in any case.

Applicant Types Accepted: Local and International Applicants (IA’s) Accepted

Job Identification: 35263
Apply Before: 08/05/2026, 11:59 PM
Job Schedule: Full time

Agency: UNDP
Grade: NPSA-6
Vacancy Type: National Personnel Service Agreement
Practice Area: Management
Bureau: Regional Bureau for Asia and the Pacific
Contract Duration: 1 Year with Possibility for extension
Required Languages: English and Nepali
Vacancy Timeline: 2 Weeks

Job Description

Background

The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is the UN’s global development network, advocating for change and connecting countries to knowledge, experience, and resources to help people build a better life. We are on the ground in 170 countries and territories, working with governments and people on their own solutions to global and national development challenges to help empower lives and build resilient nations.

Duties and Responsibilities

The Administration and Finance Associate (AFA) will work under direct supervision and overall guidance of Project Manager and assist in providing administrative and financial management functions for effective and efficient implementation of the project.

Project Administration Support:

  •  Assist Project Manager in timely and effective implementation of HR and procurement plans by preparing all necessary documents as per the UNDP and DIM guidelines.
  • Maintain accurate financial and personnel records of the programme as required by UNDP Nepal office.
  •  Assist Project Manager in undertaking quality assurance of project procurement i.e. technical bids, financial bids, proposals and contracts.
  • Draft internal and external correspondence especially related to procurement, recruitment, resource mobilization, partnership building etc.
  •  Support organizing workshops, seminars, training including arrangement for venue, logistics, transportation, and documentation of events.
  •  Provide logistic support in organizing the Project Board Meetings. Ensure all project-related materials are properly documented and easily accessible.
  •  Maintain a filing system for the project.
  •  Oversee day to day logistic/operation management; room booking for meeting, workshop and seminar, vehicle booking, security clearance, if needed hotel arrangement, preparing meeting minutes.

Financial Management support:

  •  Track progress in the financial delivery of Grants/RPA and contribute to overall financial planning and reporting.
  • Support in preparation of Annual Work Plan (AWP) and Quarterly Work Plan (QWP) preparation as per the requirement of project provision and ensure compliance with donor.
  •  Assist Project Manager in drafting Note to the file, Memorandum of understandings, contracts with implementing partners and other such documents as per UNDP DIM guidelines.
  •  Monitor, and track various contracts to ensure timely payment and extensions.
  •  Provide support to monitor budget expenditure as per approved budget from UNDP Quantum system; analyse the Combined Delivery Report and provide advice as required.
  • Support UNDP Nepal office to prepare quarterly and annual financial reporting as per UNDP Nepal CO requirements.
  • Assist in preparing for project audit and in responding to audit queries.
  •  Provide training to implementing partners related to financial management, audit, reporting and project implementation.
  •  Undertake other financial and administrative tasks assigned by the Advancing Civic Engagement for Democratic Participation Project Manager, and UNDP Portfolio Manager.
  •  Ensure Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) considerations are incorporated in the project activities and project budget is made GESI Responsive.

Support knowledge building, knowledge sharing and capacity building relevant to the assigned project:

  • Provide support in the dissemination and sharing of relevant data and lessons learned within the CO and regionally. Keep pulse on emerging best practices nationally, regionally, and internationally that relate to the work of the assigned project.
  • Make sound contributions to knowledge networks and communities of practice. Support compiling and systematizing project knowledge, products and tools as well as their wide distribution to partners.

The incumbent performs other duties within their functional profile as deemed necessary for the efficient functioning of the Office and the Organization

Institutional Arrangement

Under the overall guidance and supervision of the Project Manager and UNDP Portfolio Manager, AFA will work closely on a day-to- day basis to facilitate various administrative, financial and program implementation related operational and logistical processes.

Competencies

Core Competencies

Achieve Results:

LEVEL 2: Scale up solutions and simplifies processes, balances speed and accuracy in doing work
Think Innovatively:

LEVEL 2: Offer new ideas/open to new approaches, demonstrate systemic/integrated thinking
Learn Continuously:

LEVEL 2: Go outside comfort zone, learn from others and support their learning
Adapt with Agility:

LEVEL 2: Adapt processes/approaches to new situations, involve others in change process
Act with Determination:

LEVEL 2: Able to persevere and deal with multiple sources of pressure simultaneously
Engage and Partner:

LEVEL 2: Is facilitator/integrator, bring people together, build/maintain coalitions/partnerships
Enable Diversity and Inclusion:

LEVEL 2: Facilitate conversations to bridge differences, considers in decision making

Cross-Functional & Technical competencies

Business Management – Operations Management

Ability to effectively plan, organise and oversee different parts of corporate operations, simultaneously and in an integrated way, in order to convert the organisation’s assets into the best results in the most efficient way. Knowledge of relevant concepts and mechanisms.

Business Management – Communication

Communicate in a clear, concise and unambiguous manner both through written and verbal communication; to tailor messages and choose communication methods depending on the audience. Published on 22 July 2026 Centre for Mental Health and Counselling–Nepal (CMC-Nepal) is a national-level non-governmental organization (NGO) dedicated to promoting mental health and psychosocial well-being. We are pleased to announce an exciting opportunity to join our team as a MEAL Officer in the Psychosocial Counselling and Community Integration for Transitional Justice (PCCITJ) project.

The PCCITJ project is funded jointly by the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation (SDC), CMC-Nepal, and Manas. Its goal is that “conflict victims improve their psychosocial well-being through equitable access to quality MHPSS service during the transitional justice process and later.” The project is being implemented in 22 rural municipalities and municipalities across Bagmati, Lumbini, Karnali, and Sudurpashchim Provinces of Nepal.

Job title: MEAL Officer

Number of positions: 1 (One)

Location: Deukhuri, Dang, Lumbini Province (with frequent field visit)

Position Overview:

The MEAL Officer is responsible for leading the Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability, and Learning (MEAL) components of the PCCITJ project. This includes designing, coordinating, and implementing robust MEAL systems in accordance with project needs that support effective program implementation, learning, accountability, and reporting. The MEAL Officer supports data-driven decision-making for evidence-based programming. S/he maintains strong coordination with project and organizational staff, as well as relevant stakeholders at all levels. S/he works together with the MEAL Coordinator to strengthen the capacity of project staff on MEAL-related functions. The person also supports research initiatives, documentation, safeguarding integration, and financial performance tracking. A key aspect of the role is to promote learning, knowledge management, and innovation to adapt and improve project interventions. The MEAL Officer will be fully engaged (100%) in PCCITJ and will be responsible to the Program Manager.

Major duties and responsibilities

  • Lead end-to-end MEAL functions, including monitoring visits, indicator tracking, quality benchmarking, and evaluation processes.
  • Manage project data systems ensuring accuracy, security, confidentiality, and timely reporting aligned with donor and organizational requirements.
  • Establish and operationalize accountability and feedback mechanisms, integrating safeguarding and ensuring community-responsive actions.
  • Coordinate with government, TJ Commissions, NGOs/CBOs, and community structures to strengthen implementation, referrals, and advocacy.
  • Drive research, documentation, and knowledge generation including studies, case studies, learning briefs, and evidence-based reporting.
  • Build staff capacity on MEAL through training, mentoring, and promoting a culture of learning, adaptive management, and innovation.

Qualification and Experience

  • Master’s degree in Public Health, Statistics, Information Technology and Management Information Systems, Social Work, Social Sciences, Development Studies, or related fields.
  • Minimum of two years of progressive and relevant experience, preferably in health system strengthening, work with conflict victims, or community-based MHPSS projects.
  • Proficiency in MEAL frameworks, tools, and methodologies, including logical frameworks, indicator tracking, data quality assurance, and quality benchmark settings.
  • Strong knowledge of the Health Management Information System (HMIS), DHIS 2, and government monitoring mechanisms.
  • Demonstrated experience in data management, analysis, and visualization using MS Excel, SPSS, and other relevant software.
  • Familiarity with data security protocols and confidentiality standards.
  • Knowledge of safeguarding principles and their integration into MEAL systems.

We are seeking a dynamic, creative, and passionate School Well-being & SEL Program Associate to support the implementation of our School Wellness and Behavioral Health Program across partner educational institutions. This role requires a versatile professional who can facilitate engaging learning experiences, develop educational content, conduct workshops, and collaborate with diverse stakeholders to strengthen students’ social, emotional, and behavioral development.

The ideal candidate is an enthusiastic educator and facilitator who thrives in dynamic environments, enjoys working with children and adolescents across different age groups, and is committed to creating meaningful learning experiences that promote lifelong learning & well-being.

Key Responsibilities

  • Plan, facilitate, and evaluate engaging, experiential, and activity-based Social Emotional Learning (SEL), life skills, and wellbeing sessions for students across different developmental stages.
  • Design, develop, and continuously improve lesson plans, facilitator guides, student activities, worksheets, presentations, and other educational resources aligned with organizational frameworks.
  • Facilitate workshops, orientations, and capacity-building sessions for teachers, parents, school leaders, and other stakeholders on topics related to student wellbeing, mental health, SEL, digital citizenship, resilience, parenting, and positive school culture.
  • Observe, monitor, and assess student participation, engagement, and behavioral outcomes, and adapt facilitation approaches to meet diverse learning and developmental needs.
  • Utilize innovative instructional strategies such as storytelling, role-play, activity bassed learning, discussions, Experiential learning, project-based learning, reflective exercises, and digital learning tools to create meaningful and inclusive learning experiences.
  • Collaborate closely with school administrators, teachers, counselors, parents, and the internal program team to strengthen whole-school wellbeing initiatives.
  • Develop Individualized Support and Intervention plan of students in need.
  • Maintain accurate documentation, session reports, attendance records, assessment data, and program outcomes in accordance with organizational standards.
  • Support the planning and implementation of school events, awareness campaigns, wellness initiatives, and special projects.
  • Contribute to curriculum enhancement, program innovation, research activities, and continuous improvement initiatives.
  • Represent the organization professionally while maintaining positive relationships with partner schools and stakeholders.

  • Bachelor’s degree in Education, Social Work, Child Development, or a related discipline. A Master’s degree will be considered an added advantage.

  • Demonstrated ability to facilitate interactive learning sessions for children, adolescents, teachers, and parents.
  • Strong lesson planning, curriculum development, presentation, and facilitation skills.
  • Excellent interpersonal, communication, public speaking, and stakeholder engagement abilities.
  • Ability to work independently while effectively collaborating within multidisciplinary teams.
  • Strong organizational, documentation, and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple assignments across schools.
  • Creative, adaptable, proactive, and enthusiastic about experiential education and innovation.
  • Willingness to travel to partner schools and work in diverse educational settings as required.
  • High standards of professionalism, integrity, accountability, and adherence to organizational values and code of conduct.

Additional Notes

Work schedules and school assignments may vary depending on organizational and partner school requirements.
This role offers opportunities to grow into training, curriculum development, school wellbeing, program coordination, and leadership positions based on performance and organizational needs.
Fresh graduates with strong communication, facilitation, and learning aptitude are encouraged to apply.

Rural Women Upliftment Association (RWUA) was established on 22 Kartik 2050 B.S. in Sarlahi District, Madhesh Province, Nepal. It is a non-governmental, non-profit social organization working as a catalyst for change in the areas of women’s empowerment , child rights, child livelihood-sensitive, child protection, education, health and community development. With over 34 years of experience, RWUA has been mobilizing communities and promoting positive social transformation. The organization is women-led, with the majority of executive members being women. RWUA is committed to improving the lives of people through economic, social, cultural, and physical transformation. In partnership with various development organizations, RWUA has been implementing several development projects in Sarlahi District. RWUA invites applications from qualified, competent, and motivated Nepali citizens who are reliable, accountable, and committed to delivering results with the highest level of integrity for the following position under the Save the Children partnership with the SAMUNNATI project in Sarlahi District.

Project: Samunnati (Sponsorship Program)

Position Title: Field Coordinator (Health and Nutrition)

Location: As per project requirement

Level: Coordinator

Number of Positions: 1

Key Areas of Accountability

1. Program Planning and Implementation

  • Lead health-related operational planning and budgeting for the health theme under MB and DIP.
  • Contextualize project activities and plans in consultation with the Program Manager and Finance Unit for effective implementation.
  • Maintain 100% Budget versus Actual (BvA) compliance with quality delivery each month and ensure proper financial documentation.
  • Prepare partnership agreements, operational guidelines, consultant Terms of Reference (ToRs), and sustainability frameworks.
  • Support Field Supervisors in understanding activity budgets and managing expenditures effectively.
  • Develop and implement monthly action plans and support Field Supervisors in doing the same.
  • Ensure timely procurement of project materials and equipment.
  • Support the Program Manager in planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, reporting, and overall project management.
  • Coordinate with local governments to leverage resources and budgets for the sustainability of project activities.
  • Supervise and provide regular technical support to project staff during the implementation of project activities, trainings, and workshops.
  • Build and maintain strong professional relationships and networks with government agencies, media, civil society organizations, donor agencies, and communities.
  • Represent the project in meetings, workshops, seminars, and interactions with government agencies, NGOs, and donors.
  • Conduct regular field monitoring visits (approximately 70% of working time) using standard monitoring tools and checklists.
  • Facilitate participatory review and learning-sharing meetings with local government counterparts.
  • Assist in developing and implementing monitoring and evaluation tools to document project achievements and challenges.
  • Ensure effective preparation and implementation of the Institutional Delivery Policy in project municipalities.
  • Facilitate AFS certification in both working municipalities.
  • Conduct Budget for Children analysis and facilitate regular meetings with government stakeholders to increase investment in child-focused services.
  • Support local governments in implementing Child Friendly Local Governance (CFLG) guidelines, action plans, declaration processes, and post-declaration support mechanisms.
  • Conduct policy reviews and facilitate dialogues with stakeholders, including children and youth, at local, provincial, and national levels.

2. Field Monitoring, Coordination, Data Collection, and Reporting

  • Conduct regular field visits to monitor project activities and provide coaching and supervision to project staff.
  • Document and compile research findings, best practices, lessons learned, success stories, and case studies.
  • Lead and support the programme manager in developing monitoring and evaluation tools.
  • Maintain regular coordination with national, district, and municipal-level stakeholders for effective project implementation.
  • Review and verify data collected by field supervisors to ensure accuracy and consistency.
  • Prepare thematic reports and support the programme manager in preparing monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, and annual reports.
  • Organize monthly monitoring activities using programmatic checklists and provide clear recommendations.
  • Follow up on community-based monitoring registers and support updating the Monitoring/Issue Logbook.
  • Track health-related policies and guidelines of working municipalities to ensure alignment with project interventions.

3. Monitoring

  • Track and update thematic activity progress against project objectives and timelines.
  • Monitor project activities for cost-effectiveness and efficiency.
  • Collaborate with local governments to ensure sustainability and innovation in health and nutrition interventions.
  • Conduct participatory reviews and learning-sharing meetings with local government counterparts.
  • Work closely with the Administration and Finance Team to ensure audit compliance.
  • Prepare monitoring reports after field visits and share findings with relevant stakeholders.
  • Assist in developing monitoring and evaluation tools to document project achievements and challenges.

4. Evidence Generation

  • Produce and disseminate IEC materials, policy briefs, factsheets, and learning materials related to health and nutrition.
  • Document innovative approaches and evidence of project impact and achievements.

5. Representation

  • Represent RWUA in health-related forums, meetings, workshops, trainings, and seminars as assigned.
  • Ensure project activities are endorsed and reflected in local government plans and budgets.
  • Follow the organizational chain of command and comply with all organizational policies, including the Zero Tolerance Policy.

6. Other Responsibilities

  • Perform both development and humanitarian roles during emergencies.
  • Undertake additional tasks assigned by the Line Manager under the Sponsorship Program portfolio.
  • Demonstrate and promote the “Do No Harm” principle in all activities.
  • Ensure all OPMIS activities are updated monthly and maintain hard-copy records based on SCI templates.
  • Prepare and submit monthly reports in both hard and electronic copies.
  • Support organizational reporting requirements and organizational events such as AGM, assessments, and reviews.
  • Develop at least one case story or success story each month, along with process documentation.
  • Conduct surveys and develop health profiles.
  • Ensure integrated programming and coordination across all outcomes and sectors.
  • Support proposal development and proposal-writing processes.

Required Skills and Competencies

  • Strong skills in logical framework (Logframe) development and results-based monitoring.
  • Excellent computer skills, including MS Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and other relevant applications.
  • Strong communication, analytical, documentation, and report-writing skills.
  • Basic proficiency in spoken and written English and Nepali.
  • Strong project management skills. on MNCH/Health & Nutrition
  • Knowledge of monitoring and evaluation, research methodologies, and documentation.
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities.
  • Ability to coordinate and collaborate effectively with government agencies, CSOs, and other stakeholders.
  • Experience in data analysis and reporting.
  • Knowledge of child rights, human rights, safeguarding, and SDG-related issues.
  • Excellent networking, advocacy, coordination, and interpersonal skills.
  • Ability to work under pressure and meet multiple deadlines.
  • Demonstrated experience in training design, curriculum development, and facilitation.
  • Experience in small-grant management, monitoring, and reporting.
  • Ability to work effectively in diverse and multicultural environments.
  • Enthusiasm for working with multidisciplinary teams and rural communities.
  • Proven track record of working with local, provincial, and federal government institutions.

Qualifications and Experience

You’ll join a supportive global team working towards Zero Education Poverty, helping shape how UWS measures and demonstrates impact across our programmes.
