Posiiton: Head of Programs

FAIRMED is a Swiss-based international development NGO with its motto, “Health for the Poorest.” The organization works to improve access to health care for marginalized communities and individuals affected by disease, disability, and living in poverty. In Nepal, FAIRMED collaborates with government and other stakeholders on prevention, management and control of Neglected Tropical Diseases (NTDs), and Maternal and Neonatal Health (MNH) as a thematic area. Gender Equality and Social Inclusion (GESI) and Disability-Inclusive Development (DID) are integrated as cross-cutting themes across FAIRMED’s programs. FAIRMED invites applications for the role of Head of Programs, who will lead FAIRMED Nepal’s programs working with Country Coordinator and other team members. The position will be based in the Country Office in Lalitpur with field travels to project sites.

Details / requirements:

About the position

The Head of Programs coordinates and technically leads FAIRMED Nepal’s program portfolio under the supervision of the Country Coordinator and in close coordination with FAIRMED Switzerland. The role is responsible for program quality, planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting, as well as project-level budget monitoring and compliance within the program portfolio, in line with FAIRMED’s strategy, project cycle management principles, donor requirements and international standards. The role provides line management to assigned program staff, technical backstopping to project teams, supports proposal development and institutional fundraising, strengthens program partnerships at technical and operational level, and contributes to evidence-based learning, documentation and knowledge management.

As a member of the management team, the position supports Country Coordinator in overall responsibility for strategic leadership, organizational management, representation, legal compliance, duty of care, risk management and overall accountability for FAIRMED Nepal.

Major job responsibilities

  • Lead the quality planning, implementation, monitoring, evaluation, learning, and reporting of FAIRMED Nepal programs in line with organizational strategy, donor requirements, and international standards.
  • Support the adaptation and implementation of FAIRMED’s global strategy, policies, and cross-cutting priorities (Leave No One Behind, Right to Health, Disability Inclusion, Gender Equality, and Social Inclusion) in the Nepal context.
  • Provide technical leadership in health system strengthening, neglected tropical diseases (NTDs), maternal and newborn health (MNH), disability inclusion, and community-based health programs.
  • Strengthen program quality through evidence generation, knowledge management, implementation research, and regular field monitoring.
  • Coordinate program partnerships, contribute to resource mobilization, and support the development of high-quality concept notes and proposals.
  • Oversee project-level budget monitoring, compliance, safeguarding, accountability, and risk management in collaboration with the finance and operations team.
  • Supervise and mentor program staff, promote capacity development, and foster a positive, inclusive, and safe working environment.
  • Support the Country Coordinator in representing FAIRMED with government, donors, UN agencies, INGOs, and other stakeholders, and perform other program-related duties as assigned.

Required Qualifications and Experiences

  • Master’s degree in public health, or any other health relevant degree, with at least 10 years of relevant experience in program development and management in the development or health sector.
  • Sound knowledge and experience of working with Nepal’s health system, government structures and relevant coordination mechanisms at federal, provincial and local levels.
  • Experience in formulating and implementing program strategy, project cycle management, proposal development, monitoring, evaluation, learning and reporting.
  • Strong skills in team leadership, supervision, mentoring and capacity development.
  • Good understanding of budget monitoring, financial analysis, forecasting and donor compliance.
  • Excellent analytical, facilitation and communication skills in English and Nepali.
  • Commitment to FAIRMED’s values, Code of Conduct, safeguarding standards, anti-corruption principles and PSEAH requirements.
  • Willingness to travel regularly to project areas and work in challenging contexts when required.
  • Ability to prioritize, manage work pressure effectively in complex or challenging circumstances.
  • Ability to represent FAIRMED’s technical work effectively in delegated forums and contribute to constructive partnerships.

1. Individual Counseling

  • Support students dealing with anxiety, stress, depression, self-esteem concerns, relationship issues, adjustment difficulties, and identity-related challenges.

2. Group Counseling and Student Support Programs

  • Design and facilitate group counseling sessions addressing common student concerns.
  • Conduct psychoeducational programs focused on:
  • Stress and anxiety management
  • Study skills and time management
  • Emotional intelligence
  • Healthy relationships
  • Bullying prevention
  • Self-esteem and confidence building

3. Mental Health Awareness and Prevention

  • Develop and implement preventive mental health initiatives across the school.
  • Organize workshops, seminars, and awareness campaigns for students, parents, and staff.
  • Promote positive mental health practices and emotional well-being throughout the school community.

4. Crisis Intervention and Safeguarding

  • Provide immediate support to students facing emotional crises, self-harm risks, suicidal ideation,
    abuse, trauma, or other urgent concerns.
  • Coordinate with school leadership, parents, and external professionals when necessary.
  • Follow established safeguarding, child protection, and crisis management procedures.

5. Consultation and Collaboration

  • Provide guidance and consultation to teachers, Academic Coordinators, Grade Coordinators, and parents regarding students’ psychological and behavioral needs.
  • Recommend appropriate intervention strategies and classroom accommodations.
  • Participate in multidisciplinary meetings to support student welfare.

6. Assessment and Referral

  • Conduct preliminary assessments to identify students requiring psychological support.
  • Maintain referral networks with psychologists, psychiatrists, therapists, and other mental health professionals.
  • Monitor referred cases and coordinate follow-up support.

7. Documentation and Record Management

  • Maintain accurate, confidential, and secure counseling records.
  • Prepare periodic reports, case summaries, and intervention records while maintaining professional confidentiality.
  • Ensure compliance with organizational policies and ethical counseling standards.

8. Research and Professional Development

  • Stay updated on current developments, research, and best practices in school counseling and child psychology.
  • Recommend evidence-based interventions and programs to enhance student well-being.
  • Participate in professional development activities and trainings.

9. Teamwork and Institutional Support

  • Collaborate effectively with academic and administrative departments.
  • Support school events, student welfare programs, and institutional initiatives when required.
  • Maintain professional relationships with all stakeholders.

10. Professional Conduct and Discipline

  • Demonstrate professionalism, integrity, confidentiality, and ethical behavior at all times.
  • Adhere to the school’s code of conduct, dress code, and workplace policies.
  • Wear official identification during working hours.

  • Minimum 2 years of relevant counseling experience, preferably in an educational institution.
  • Strong understanding of child and adolescent psychology.
  • Knowledge of counseling theories and therapeutic approaches including CBT, Solution-Focused Therapy, and Mindfulness-Based Interventions.
  • Excellent communication, interpersonal, and active listening skills.
  • Proficiency in English and Nepali communication.

Highly attractive and negotiable

KOSHISH, established in 2008, is a non-governmental organization dedicated to promoting mental health and psychosocial well-being in Nepal. Embracing the spirit of “NOTHING ABOUT US WITHOUT US,” KOSHISH advocates for the inclusion and meaningful participation of individuals with mental health conditions and psychosocial disabilities. KOSHISH actively engages in community-based mental health programs, awareness campaigns, and advocacy efforts. Our overarching goal is to mainstream mental health within the broader health system and societal domains, such as social protection, education, inclusion, and employment.

Overall Purpose:

The Receptionist serves as the first point of contact for KOSHISH, creating a professional, welcoming, and inclusive experience for all visitors, partners, and callers. The role is responsible for managing the front office efficiently by receiving and directing telephone calls, welcoming and assisting visitors, maintaining visitor records, coordinating appointments, and ensuring smooth day-to-day front desk operations. The Receptionist also provides administrative support, handles incoming and outgoing correspondence, and help maintain an organized reception area.

We are looking for a smart, confident, and customer-oriented individual with excellent communication and interpersonal skills. The ideal candidate should be proactive, well-organized, able to multitask, and capable of handling inquiries with professionalism, courtesy, and confidentiality while representing KOSHISH’s values and commitment to quality service.

Major Duties and Responsibilities:

Front Office and Visitor Management

  • Welcome and assist visitors, clients, and stakeholders in a courteous and professional manner.
  • Maintain visitor records and ensure visitors are directed to the appropriate staff member.
  • Keep the reception area clean, organized, and presentable at all times.

Telephone & Communication Management

  • Receive incoming telephone calls, respond to general enquiries, and direct calls to the appropriate staff members promptly.
  • Take accurate messages when staff are unavailable and ensure timely communication.
  • Handle incoming and outgoing correspondence, including emails, letters, and courier services, as required.

Administrative Support

  • Provide day-to-day administrative support, including scheduling appointments, coordinating meeting room bookings, maintaining office records, inventory of goods etc.
  • Support staff with routine administrative tasks and assist in the smooth functioning of office operations.
  • Maintain confidentiality while handling sensitive information and represent KOSHISH with professionalism and integrity at all times.

Safeguarding and Ethical Compliance

  • Ensure compliance with KOSHISH’s Safeguarding and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) policies in all administrative and financial processes.
  • Promote a culture of respect, integrity, accountability, and ethical conduct within all financial and administrative activities.
  • Maintain confidentiality and ensure responsible handling of organizational and personal information.
  • Report any safeguarding concerns, suspected misconduct, or policy violations through appropriate channels in line with organizational procedures.

Personal Competency

  • Professional and welcoming attitude.
  • Good interpersonal and customer service skills.
  • Smart, confident, and presentable.
  • Ability to multitask and prioritize tasks effectively.
  • Responsible, reliable, and detail-oriented.
  • Must possess a valid two-wheeler riding license and be willing to travel for official administrative tasks when required.

Technical Competency

  • Minimum +2 level education with 1–2 years of experience in reception, front desk, or administrative roles.

Pravasi Nepali Coordination Committee (PNCC) is a non-profit, non-political organization established in 2009 by returnee migrant workers. PNCC is dedicated to protecting and promoting the rights and well-being of Nepali migrant workers and their families. PNCC operates nationally and internationally with a wide network and in collaboration with government bodies, community organizations, and international agencies to facilitate the issues of distressed migrant workers.

PNCC invites applications from competent Nepali citizens for the following position to implement paralegal services for the Safer Migration (SaMi) Programme:

Position Title: Programme Officer (Full -time)

Location: PNCC head office, Kathmandu, Nepal

Application Deadline: 23 July, 2026 before 5pm

Duration: 11 Months (with possibility of extension)

Organization: Pravasi Nepali Coordination Committee (PNCC)

Position Summary

This position role is focuses on providing para-legal and remedial support to distressed Nepali migrant workers and their families refer by various source such as Migrant Resource Centers (MRCs), Employment Service Centers (ESCs) and others. The position involves handling cases from intake to resolution by coordinating with different stakeholder’s such as PNCC’s outreach coordinator, Nepal embassies, Social organization in Countries of Destination, DoFE, FEB, Consular department, Recruitment Agencies, local government and other related stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities

  • Responsible for providing possible para-legal remedial services support to the distressed Nepali migrant workers primarily referred by Migrant Resource Centers and SaMi national partners.
  • Record the details of cases in the Case Management Information System (CMIS), ensuring documentation of evidence from victims or perpetrators (using video/audio whenever possible) and maintain records of the progress made in the cases.
  • Prepare process documentation, including translations, and writing applications on behalf of migrant workers and their families, to respond to the cases effectively and promptly.
  • Support families of destitute Nepali migrant workers in obtaining compensation and benefits guaranteed by the existing law of Nepal and destination countries.
  • Provide regular updates to Migrant Resources Centers, migrant workers, and members of their families, and referrers. .
  • Establish communication channels with the Nepalese mission through emails and phone calls to both offer and seek support for migrant workers, including the immediate referrals of the cases to the embassies and follow-up on their progress.
  • Prepare and provide working progress reports to the supervisor/management of PNCC regularly.
  • Make regular communication and follow-ups with respective country outreach coordinators, volunteers, embassies, and relevant stakeholders.

Required Qualifications and Skills

  • Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Social Sciences, Development Studies, Public Administration, Migration Studies, or a related field with a minimum of 3 years of relevant work experience in rescue and repatriation/paralegal support for migrant workers and their families.
  • Practical experience in case management and ability to handle MW cases smoothly,
  • Strong knowledge of labor migration issues, migration services, and Nepal’s foreign employment policies.
  • Competency in data entry, collection, analysis, and reporting.
  • Average command of written and spoken English and Nepali.
  • Advanced proficiency in Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and digital communication tools.
  • Adaptability and flexibility of responding distressed migrant worker’s cases whenever required

Application Procedure

Posiiton: Associate Investment Officer

Description

Join Our Mission to Foster Prosperity in Asia

Are you ready to make a difference in the future of Asia and be a catalyst for positive change? We are thrilled to offer a unique opportunity to become an important part of the prestigious Asian Development Bank (ADB). At ADB, our mission is simple yet powerful: to alleviate poverty and promote sustainable development in the Asia-Pacific region.

Organizational Setting and Reporting Relationship
The position of Associate Investment Officer is assigned to the Private Sector Infrastructure Finance Division 1 (PSIF1) within the Private Sector Operations Department (PSOD). You will be based at our Resident Mission Office in Kathmandu, Nepal (NRM).

You will report to the Country Director, NRM and to the designated PSIF1 International Staff and Officer, as applicable.

Your Role

As an Associate Investment Officer, you will provide technical support and coordination in the processing of ADB’s private sector investments and technical assistance in Nepal and other South Asian countries. You will also assist and participate in the identification, development, approval, implementation, and administration of private sector infrastructure financing projects.

You will:

a. Project Processing

  • Provides analytical support in the areas of credit and financial due diligence, review of contracts and project documents, development of financial models and in general assessing the risk and credit profile of proposed infrastructure investments in the form of debt, equity and guarantees.
  • Performs analysis of financial statements and financial projections/models, performs sensitivity analysis and stress testing, in co-ordination with team leaders and external clients.
  • Participates in selected due diligence missions and provides support to Team Leaders in negotiations with project developers, sponsors, and financiers to facilitate the financial closing of transactions and implement projects.
  • Provides logistical support and interacts with external technical advisors, consultants and lawyers representing ADB in specific transactions.
  • Under the guidance of the Team Leaders, undertakes relevant industry and country research, as needed, as part of transaction risk assessment.
  • Assists in drafting initial and final credit memorandum, preparing summaries of project documents, risk assessment analyses and other required documents as may be needed from time to time throughout the project processing cycle.
  • Interfaces as required with internal departments within ADB, including the Office of Risk Management and the Safeguards Specialists, and assist the Team Leader in addressing credit-related and other issues identified by such departments in respect of transactions under processing.
  • Assists in creating, maintaining and updating comprehensive credit files related to transactions under processing.
  • Assists in Investment Committee meetings and other meetings.

b. Project Administration

  • Maintains a database of all projects and financing documents relating to each project. Liaises with the central file keeper to maintain orderly electronically filed documents for each project.
  • Undertakes all activities required to process disbursement requests, including verification of compliance with disbursement conditions and liaison within ADB and with cofinanciers. Verify fee computation.
  • Monitors billing statements of the Controller’s department and payments from the borrowers, and follows up on any delays in payments.
  • Ensures borrowers’ compliance with covenants. Monitors and follows up on the submission of financial statements, technical, insurance, safeguard, and other reports. Review these reports and draw to the attention of dealing officers any perceived issues.
  • Prepares memoranda to obtain management approval for waivers and consents requested by the borrower. Liaises with the Office of the General Counsel, the Office of Risk Management, the technical advisor, and other relevant parties to consider such waivers and requests. Responds to other requests and needs of the borrower.
  • Assists with the preparation of terms of reference (TOR) for the recruitment of consultants for the due diligence.
  • Provides support in identifying a suitable consultant to address the specificities of the country.
  • Provides comments / inputs on draft due diligence reports, bringing to bear PSOD’s experience in operations in India and make appropriate recommendations.

c. Others

  • Assist and participate in the identification and development of projects, undertaking the needed due diligence, risk analysis and mitigation work towards the structuring of loans, equity investment, guarantees or other forms of assistance.
  • Provides inputs for updates on PSOD activities to the Country Director, Nepal Resident Mission.
  • Perform other tasks as assigned and reflected in the workplan.

Qualifications

You will need:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance and/or Accounting, preferably with advanced training.
  • At least 5 years of relevant experience in the field of corporate financing or project finance with a leading international or local financial institution, and/or investment bank.
  • Proven ability to undertake research and analysis on difficult but well-defined tasks, collect and organize required data and information, apply appropriate computer skills in organizing and analyzing the data, and prepare notes, papers, and sections of reports.
  • Good analytical thinking with ability to comprehend causal links, make pros and cons analysis, and analyze factors to reach a decision.
  • Effective report-writing and communication skills in English.
  • Able to guide Administrative Staff to facilitate work planning, delivery and quality review.
  • Able to work collaboratively with teams as a constructive team member.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills.
  • Please refer to the link for ADB Competency Framework for Technical Local grade TL4.

Benefits

ADB offers a rewarding salary and a comprehensive benefits package. The salary will be based on ADB’s standards and comparator markets, taking into account your qualifications and experience.

  • Retirement plan
  • Medical and health benefits
  • Paid leave (including parental)
  • Life and other insurance plans
  • Staff development
  • Additional Information

This appointment is open to internal and external applicants.

This opening is a local staff position. It is open only to nationals and permanent residents of Nepal.

This is a fixed term appointment with option to renew, initially for a period of up to 3 years, or up to the Normal Retirement Date (NRD), whichever comes earlier, for the purpose(s) and conditions determined by ADB, in accordance with Administrative Order No. 2.01 (Recruitment and Appointment). After the initial fixed-term period, ADB may choose to renew the appointment for up to an additional 3 years or not renewed. This decision will be made in the overall interest of ADB, based on factors including but not limited to the requirement of Staff’s particular blend of skills and experience for the medium-term work program of the organizational unit, sufficient funding to cover the renewed period, and Staff’s performance and suitability for employment. There is no limit to the number of renewals up to NRD. However, this appointment is not convertible to a regular appointment.

About Us

ADB is a leading multilateral development bank supporting inclusive, resilient, and sustainable growth across Asia and the Pacific. Working with its members and partners to solve complex challenges together, ADB harnesses innovative financial tools and strategic partnerships to transform lives, build quality infrastructure, and safeguard our planet. Founded in 1966, ADB is headquartered in Manila and owned by 69 members—50 from the region.

ADB only hires nationals of its 69 members.

To view ADB Organizational Chart, please click here.

ADB wants to ensure that everyone is treated with respect and given equal opportunities to work in an inclusive environment. ADB encourages all qualified candidates to apply regardless of their racial, ethnic, religious and cultural background, gender, sexual orientation or disabilities. Women are highly encouraged to apply.

Visit ADB Careers FAQ for more information.

UNICEF is the world’s leading organization working globally for children’s rights. Child rights begin with safe shelter, nutrition, protection from disaster and conflict and traverse the life cycle. UNICEF strive to ensure that all children are born alive, stay safe and keep learning.

UNICEF Nepal Country Office is a medium size office that operates across multiple locations in Kathmandu and four field offices based in Janakpur, Surkhet, Bhairahawa and Dangadhi. The office size and structure of over 200 personnel comprising staff, UN Volunteers, and consultants are assigned to work in these different strategic locations to implement programme priorities to deliver results for children. Providing efficient and effective comprehensive operational services, support, innovations including specifically Information, Communication & Technology (ICT) and digital solutions in the different local/office contexts is critical and indispensable.

As part of ongoing organizational realignment following the recent Programme Budget Review (PBR), UNICEF Nepal is seeking a Digital Impact Officer on temporary contract to bridge temporary gap in the ICT unit.

How can you make a difference?

Join our team as the Digital Impact Officer to carry out broad ICT and digital impact functions and enable the provision of ICT and digital solutions and services and assist in the delivery of results in UNICEF Nepal.

You will lead UNICEF Nepal’s ICT function, provide strategic oversight and manage the ICT unit and team in close consultation with the direct supervisor/Deputy Representative Operations. You will collaborate with different programme sections to guide and support Technology for Development (T4D) initiatives that will strengthen programme delivery and create greater impact for children.

Key functions and responsibilities:

  • Manage ICT infrastructure, networks, telecommunications and enterprise technology platforms.
  • Ensure effective ICT service delivery, technical support, system availability and business continuity.
  • Strengthen information security, risk management, system maintenance and compliance.
  • Support the implementation of digital solutions and Technology for Development (T4D) initiatives.
  • Provide leadership, supervision, technical guidance and capacity building for ICT personnel.
  • Coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to advance ICT priorities, innovation and collaboration.

Position: Physiotherapist

Service type: People with disabilities
Type of Contract: Yearly contract for two years

Reports to: Project coordinator
Supervisory role: 1-3 staff (Occasional

At least two (1) year of relevant professional experience in providing physiotherapy services to persons with disabilities and in rehabilitation programs

Organisation Background:

Human Development and Community Services (HDCS) is a faith-based NGO working in three main sectors of health, education, and community development since 1991. Currently, it manages various projects across Nepal especially in rural regions and provides services through hospitals, health camps, public health programs, disaster preparedness and response, school development programs, teacher training, educational daycare centres for children with special needs, and community radio stations. HDCS is committed to attract and retain the best employees from all ethnicities, gender and backgrounds in its vision to transform the communities.

Purpose:

The Physiotherapist is responsible for assessing the functional needs of persons with disabilities and providing quality facility-based and home-based physiotherapy and rehabilitation services to improve their mobility, independence, participation, and quality of life. The position provides technical guidance, training, coaching, and mentoring to persons with disabilities, caregivers, and family members on rehabilitation, home-based care, assistive device use, positioning, exercise therapy, and home modification. The Physiotherapist facilitates referrals, follow-up care, and multidisciplinary rehabilitation services; collaborates closely with health facilities, local governments, and rehabilitation stakeholders; and promotes the social and economic inclusion of persons with disabilities through community-based rehabilitation (CBR) and appropriate livelihood support.

Responsibilities:

1. Physiotherapy Assessment, Treatment & Rehabilitation Services (40%)

  • Conduct comprehensive functional assessments to identify the rehabilitation needs of persons with disabilities.
  • Develop and implement individualized physiotherapy and rehabilitation plans based on assessment findings.
  • Provide quality facility-based and home-based physiotherapy services using appropriate rehabilitation techniques and interventions.
  • Monitor rehabilitation progress and adjust treatment plans to improve mobility, independence, and quality of life.
  • Promote safe rehabilitation practices and the appropriate use of exercise therapy, positioning, and assistive devices.

2. Case Management, Referral & Technical Support (20%)

  • Facilitate timely referrals and follow-up services to ensure continuity of rehabilitation and healthcare.
  •  Provide technical guidance on home-based rehabilitation, assistive devices, positioning, mobility techniques, and home modifications.
  •  Coordinate with health facilities and rehabilitation professionals to ensure comprehensive rehabilitation services.
  •  Support caregivers and family members with practical skills to continue rehabilitation at home.

3. Community-Based Rehabilitation, Capacity Building & Disability Inclusion (20%)

  • Conduct awareness, education, and behavior change activities on disability-inclusive rehabilitation and healthy practices.
  •  Train and coach social mobilizers, persons with disabilities, caregivers, community members, and local stakeholders on rehabilitation and home-based care.
  •  Promote community participation, disability inclusion, and access to rehabilitation services.
  •  Advocate for the rights, inclusion, and participation of persons with disabilities in community development.

4. Stakeholder Coordination & Partnership (10%)

  •  Collaborate effectively with social mobilizers, Project Coordinator, project staffs, local governments, and multidisciplinary teams.
  •  Participate in case discussions and contribute technical inputs to improve rehabilitation outcomes.
  •  Coordinate with health facilities, rehabilitation centers and hospital for rehabilitation outcomes. • Build and maintain effective partnerships to strengthen rehabilitation service delivery.

5. Documentation, Reporting, Compliance & Safeguarding (10%)

  •  Maintain accurate and up-to-date assessment, treatment, referral, and follow-up records in accordance with organizational standards.
  • Prepare and submit timely reports, progress updates, and project data to the Project Coordinator in compliance with organizational and donor requirements.
  • Document case studies, impact stories, photographs, videos, and key lessons learned to support project learning and knowledge management.
  •  Ensure compliance with organizational policies, safeguarding standards, professional ethics, and quality assurance requirements.
  •  Contribute to project monitoring, organizational learning, and continuous quality improvement through accurate documentation and reporting.

Essential skills:

  •  Clinical Rehabilitation & Disability Inclusion: Sound knowledge of physiotherapy, community-based rehabilitation (CBR), disability inclusion, functional assessment, assistive devices, referral mechanisms, home modifications, and safeguarding.
  •  Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Strong communication, counselling, behavior change, and relationship-building skills with the ability to work effectively with persons with disabilities, families, communities, and stakeholders.
  •  Planning & Problem-Solving: Ability to plan and organize rehabilitation services, manage field activities, solve problems, and adapt to diverse community contexts.
  •  Stakeholder Coordination & Social Inclusion: Ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams, health facilities, local governments, and community stakeholders while promoting disability inclusion and cultural sensitivity.
  •  Documentation & Digital Skills: Ability to maintain accurate records of Person with disability, services, prepare reports, and use digital and hard copy both data collection and reporting tools such as KOBO and MS Office.
  •  Collaboration & Teamwork: Ability to work effectively with multidisciplinary teams, HDCS staff, health facilities, and other stakeholders to provide coordinated and holistic rehabilitation services. • Cultural Sensitivity: A physiotherapist should be able to engage with and respect local cultures, particularly when working in remote or diverse communities. Cultural sensitivity ensures that treatment plans and rehabilitation activities are tailored to meet the unique needs of the community.
  •  Driving & Field Mobility: Valid Category “A” driving license with at least one year of driving experience and willingness to undertake frequent field travel and home visits.

In addition, Field Rehabilitation Team Leader works closely with individuals, families, and communities to promote better health practices, improve access to healthcare services, and enhance the overall well-being, independence, and quality of life of persons with disabilities.

Responsibilities:

1. Health Assessment, Basic Rehabilitation Support & Case Management (35%)

  •  Provide basic healthcare guidance, rehabilitation support, and promote safe health and rehabilitation practices.
  •  Identify and facilitate appropriate referrals and ensure timely follow-up for continuity of care. • Support home modification initiatives and recommend appropriate assistive devices based on individual needs.

2. Community Health Promotion & Disability Inclusion (25%)

  •  Conduct school health assessments, awareness sessions, counselling, and community education on health, hygiene, nutrition, and disability-inclusive practices.
  • Promote positive behavior change and community participation to improve health and well-being.
  •  Support community meetings, workshops, and awareness campaigns on health and disability issues.

  • Build effective partnerships and promote collaboration to improve access to quality rehabilitation and health services.

4. Documentation, Reporting, Compliance & Knowledge Management (20%)

  • Document case studies, impact stories, photographs, videos, and lessons learned to support project learning and knowledge management.

Essential skills:

Human Development and Community Services (HDCS) is a faith-based NGO working in three main sectors of health, education, and community development since 1991. Currently, it manages various projects across Nepal especially in rural regions and provides services through hospitals, health camps, public health programs, disaster preparedness and response, school development programs, teacher training, educational daycare centres for children with special needs, and community radio stations. HDCS is committed to attract and retain the best employees from all ethnicities, gender and backgrounds in its vision to transform the communities.

Purpose:

The Field Officer (Livelihood and MNCH) provides technical leadership, technical training, supportive supervision, and field-level coordination to ensure the quality implementation of the SHINE Project in Rukum-west. Reporting to the Project Coordinator, the position strengthens the capacity of Social Mobilizers/Technical Facilitators, local governments, health facilities, community groups, and other stakeholders through technical training, coaching, mentoring, and supportive supervision to improve maternal, newborn and child health (MNCH), nutrition, livelihoods, Apply here https://lnk.ink/iRIUC agriculture, and entrepreneurship outcomes. The Field Officer supports project planning, quality assurance, monitoring, documentation, and reporting while promoting safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion (GEDSI), accountability, and community ownership throughout project implementation.

Responsibilities:

1. Technical Leadership, Planning & Quality Implementation (25%)

  • Lead the technical planning, coordination, and quality implementation of MNCH, nutrition, livelihoods, agriculture, livestock, and entrepreneurship interventions in line with the Detailed Implementation Plan (DIP) and project objectives.
  • Provide technical guidance to ensure project interventions are implemented according to organizational standards, government policies, and donor requirements.
  • Support the Project Coordinator in preparing annual, quarterly, and monthly work plans and implementation schedules.
  • Identify implementation gaps, risks, and technical issues, and recommend appropriate corrective actions to improve programme quality.
  • Ensure timely and effective delivery of project activities while maintaining high standards of quality and accountability.

2. Capacity Building, Coaching & Supportive Supervision (20%)

  • Design, organize, and facilitate technical training, workshops, orientations, demonstrations, and learning events for Social Mobilizers/ Technical Facilitators, technical facilitators, local governments, health workers, FCHVs, farmer groups, and other stakeholders.
  • Provide regular coaching, mentoring, and supportive supervision to Social Mobilizers/ Technical Facilitators to strengthen technical knowledge, facilitation skills, and quality service delivery.
  • Develop and adapt technical training materials, facilitation guides, job aids, and learning resources to support effective project implementation.
  •  Conduct regular field monitoring visits and provide constructive feedback to improve staff performance and programme quality.
  • Promote continuous learning, knowledge sharing, and capacity strengthening among project staff and community stakeholders.

3. Community Engagement & Stakeholder Coordination (15%)

  • Strengthen collaboration and maintain effective working relationships with local governments, health facilities, schools, cooperatives, community groups, farmer groups, and other relevant stakeholders.
  • Facilitate transparent beneficiary identification and selection processes in accordance with project criteria and organizational policies.
  •  Promote community participation, ownership, and inclusive engagement in project planning and implementation.
  •  Coordinate multi-sectoral activities with government line agencies and community institutions to enhance programme effectiveness and sustainability.
  • Represent the project in local coordination meetings and technical forums as delegated by the Project Coordinator.

4. Monitoring, Reporting & Knowledge Management (15%)

  •  Monitor project progress against approved plans, indicators, and targets, and recommend corrective actions where necessary.
  •  Ensure timely and accurate collection, verification, analysis, and reporting of project data using KOBO and other organizational systems.
  •  Maintain accurate project records, beneficiary databases, monitoring information, and supporting documentation.
  • Prepare high-quality monthly, quarterly, and annual reports, including case studies, success stories, lessons learned, and best practices.
  • Contribute to organizational learning through documentation, reflection, and knowledge-sharing initiatives.

5. Quality Assurance, Compliance & Technical Support (15%)

  •  Ensure compliance with organizational policies, donor requirements, government regulations, and project implementation guidelines.
  • Promote safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion (GEDSI), accountability, and protect
    ion principles across all project activities.
  •  Support the effective management and utilization of project resources, including technical equipment, agricultural inputs, and training materials.
  • Identify implementation challenges, provide practical technical solutions, and ensure timely follow-up to improve programme performance.
  • Support project reviews, monitoring visits, assessments, evaluations, and audit processes as required.

6. Organizational Support & Representation (10%)

  • Support the Project Coordinator in planning, coordination, and implementation of project priorities and organizational initiatives.
  • Foster teamwork, collaboration, and effective communication within the project team and with partner organizations.
  • Maintain professionalism, integrity, confidentiality, and ethical standards in all aspects of work.
  • Represent HDCS professionally in meetings, workshops, and community events when delegated by line manager
  •  Perform other duties and responsibilities assigned by the line manager or management in support of organizational priorities.

Essential Skills & Competencies:

  • Technical Leadership: Demonstrated ability to provide technical guidance and ensure quality implementation of MNCH, nutrition, livelihood, agriculture, livestock, and entrepreneurship interventions.
  • Training, Facilitation & Capacity Building: Proven ability to assess learning needs, develop training materials, facilitate technical training, and strengthen the capacity of project staff, local governments, health workers, community groups, and other stakeholders.

  •  Cultural Sensitivity: Respect for local cultures and the ability to work effectively with women, children, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities in Rukum West.
  • Monitoring, Documentation & Reporting: Ability to monitor project performance, ensure data quality, analyse information, prepare technical reports, and maintain accurate documentation using digital platforms such as KOBO and MS Office.
  • Knowledge Management & Learning: Ability to document and share lessons learned, best practices, case studies, and impact stories to support organizational learning.
  • Integrity & Inclusion: Demonstrated commitment to HDCS values, ethical conduct, safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, accountability, and the HDCS Code of Conduct.
  • Communication & Interpersonal Skills: Excellent verbal, written, presentation, facilitation, and relationshipbuilding skills with the ability to communicate effectively with diverse audiences.
  •  Problem Solving & Decision Making: Ability to analyse field-level challenges, make sound technical decisions, recommend practical solutions, and adapt interventions to changing contexts.

Similarly, the position holder will provide technical support to conduct baseline, midterm and final evaluation and periodical indicator survey of the assigned projects. The post holder will also be responsible to manage information/data and update regularly; will be responsible to ensure country as well as SCI global reporting requirements. Similarly, the position holder will be responsible for developing PNGO staff capacity on MEAL functions under the field office. Position: Communications Officer – HICAS
Location: Kathmandu

Background

The Communications Officer is being hired under the Integrated Climate Adaptation Solutions for the Hindu Kush Himalaya Region (HI-CAS) project at ICIMOD, funded by Global Affairs Canada (GAC) – Department of Foreign Affairs, Trade and Development (DFATD). The project aims to improve climate-resilient, nature-positive livelihoods while strengthening the leadership and agency of rural women and Indigenous Peoples and Local Communities (IPLCs) in Bangladesh, Bhutan, and Nepal.
The project is housed under Strategy Group Resilient Economies and Landscapes which focuses on delivering environmentally sustainable, but economically viable and socially inclusive solutions for some of the world’s most marginalised and vulnerable people. With a focus at both local and landscape levels, it builds understanding of the implications of rapid socio-economic, climate and environmental changes on mountain livelihoods and economies that are challenged by their remote, fragile, and hazard-prone settings. The project itself will be implemented through the adoption of gender-responsive and locally tailored climate adaptation solutions – grounded in feminist and human rights-based methodologies – that place the rights, agency, and leadership of IPLCs at the centre. These evidence-informed Integrated Adaptation Solution Packages (IASPs) will combine springshed management, renewable energy technologies to power irrigation systems, and agrobiodiversity practices. They will be complemented by capacity building and knowledge sharing to drive institutional policy and action. These initiatives will also help to attract sustainable investments in climate action and development – particularly in the water, energy, and agrobiodiversity sectors – with a strong focus on women’s and IPLCs’ leadership.
The HI-CAS project will be implemented in two upazilas (sub-districts) in Bandarban and Khagrachari districts in the Chittagong Hill Tracts of Bangladesh; two gewogs (blocks) in Paro and Punakha dzongkhags in Bhutan; and two municipalities, Roshi and Dhankuta, in Nepal. Over its four-year duration, the project aims to benefit approximately 40,000 IPLCs and other vulnerable groups by reducing their exposure and sensitivity to climate change impacts while fostering ecosystem health and climate mitigation outcomes.

Position Overview

The Communications Officer will be responsible for boosting awareness of the outcomes and impact of the HI-CAS project by supporting the documentation and communication of the project results in line with the commitments ICIMOD has made in the HI-CAS Project Performance Measurement Framework, which is nested within our Strategy 2030: Moving Mountains and our Medium-Term Action Plan V (2023-2026):Embracing Change and Accelerating Impact and related Results Framework 2023-2026. It will also contribute to the wider communications efforts of ICIMOD’s Strategic Group: Resilient Economies and Landscapes, where the position sits.

ICIMOD’s Communications Officers are creative, result-driven and motivated professionals who are passionate about the power of amplifying impact and driving policy and practice change through strategic communications, influencing and engagement. Working under the direct supervision of the Senior Project Coordinator HI-CAS, and co-supervised by the Head of Communications, the post holder will work closely with communication staff in the Strategic Group (and its respective Action Areas and Interventions) teams, and with the ICIMOD central Communications Unit, to deliver communication and knowledge products for the HI-CAS project. The role holder will ensure communications facilitate access to knowledge and the ability for ICIMOD to use evidence-based advocacy and influencing messaging in policy dialogues. All efforts will be guided by a strong GESI commitment, rooted in a feminist approach that challenges power imbalances, promotes women’s leadership, and centres the rights, voices, and knowledge of IPLCs.
You will be focused on working directly with communities, partners, and ICIMOD staff to tell the story of HI-CAS through a variety of media. You will be tasked with amplifying community experiences and evidence generated by the project to inform wider advocacy efforts and drive the uptake of approaches used in the project. This is an exciting opportunity for someone who values delivering impact through written, oral, and visual communication and engagement approaches and methods, is passionate and experienced in feminist solutions for mountains and people, and is committed to helping build a greener, more inclusive, climate-resilient Hindu Kush Himalaya as ICIMOD moves into its next Strategy 2030 period. It will require very close teamwork and strong collaboration skills. The ideal candidate should have knowledge of feminist methodologies, GESI-responsive communication strategies, and experience working with IPLCs.

Requirements

Person Specification/Competencies

Essential

  • Master’s degree in journalism, marketing, research for development approaches, communications, or other relevant field with a minimum of 3 years of experience in a similar Communications role or bachelor’s degree in combination with four years of qualifying experience may be accepted in lieu of a master’s degree.
  •  Understanding and experience of GESI-related issues and activities and how these can be effectively communicated. Awareness of indigenous people-centric communication methods and approaches.
  • Exceptional written and verbal communication skills.
  • Demonstrated ability to produce and edit various forms of content.
  • Proficiency in using digital and social media platforms.
  • Excellent organisational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects simultaneously.
  •  Proficiency in MS Office Suite, content management systems, and basic graphic design software.

PREFERRED

  •  Knowledge of the languages and cultures of the HKH region
  • Experience working on multi-cultural, multi-country communication tasks
  • Excellent interpersonal and time-management skills

Benefits

Remuneration

This is an international position at ICIMOD. The starting annual gross salary for this position is USD 21,419/- (negotiable based on experience and qualifications). Gross salary comprises basic salary, provident fund, family/post adjustment allowance, and child/dependency allowances. Salaries and benefits at ICIMOD are competitive compared with other international organisations. We offer a comprehensive benefits package which includes insurances (medical, life and accidental), children’s education grant for a maximum of two children below 18 years of age, severance pay, paid leave (30 holidays and 10 public holidays per year) and a daycare facility.

For expatriates, there is a tax exemption in Nepal; they are responsible for their home country’s tax payments. Expatriate staff are entitled to housing allowance, annual home leave ticket, shipment of personal effects, and an installation and repatriation allowance.

Method of application

Applicants are requested to apply online before August 04, 2026 (11:59 PM Nepal Standard Time) through .

Posiiton: Customer Relationship Specialist
Location: Lalitpur

At Alaya, we pride ourselves on our guiding values of Care, Passion, and Oneness. We offer tailored solutions to our clients, helping them achieve their financial goals with confidence. As a member of our team, you will collaborate with like-minded individuals, celebrate your unique talents, and forge lifelong connections. Our dedication to excellence has earned us numerous awards, including the 2023 HRD Asia 5-Star Employers of Choice Award.

About The Role:

The Customer Relationship Specialist plays an important role in maintaining strong relationships with clients after the settlement of their home loans. This role is focused on providing excellent post-settlement support, proactively communicating with clients, resolving queries, identifying opportunities for loan reviews, and supporting client retention.

You will work closely with clients, brokers, lenders, and internal teams to ensure clients continue to receive the right support after their loan has settled. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys customer service, relationship building, problem-solving, and working in a fast-paced environment where proactive communication and attention to detail matter.

What You Will Be Doing:

  • Client Relationship Management: You will build rapport with clients after loan settlement, regularly touch base with them, and act as a trusted point of contact for their post-settlement needs.
  • Post-Settlement Support: You will assist clients with loan-related queries, progress payments, fixed-rate expiry, loan feature changes, and other after-settlement concerns.
  • Loan Review and Retention: You will monitor client loans, review and re-price loans on a semi-annual basis, negotiate interest rates with banks, and support client retention by identifying refinancing or repeat business opportunities.
  • Proactive Communication: You will ensure clients are updated regularly and do not need to chase for updates. You will also make sure emails and client queries are responded to within the expected timeframe.
  • Lead Generation and Business Support: You will identify opportunities for new business, referrals, product reviews, and repeat business while supporting brokers with relevant client information.
  • Team Collaboration: You will work closely with team members, cross-train where needed, and support the team in completing tasks accurately and on time.

About You:

At Alaya, we hire based on our Guiding principles:

  • You enjoy building strong relationships and providing helpful, timely, and professional support to clients.
  • You take ownership of your work and understand the importance of accuracy, follow-up, and proactive communication.
  • You are solution-focused and can remain calm and professional while handling client queries, objections, or complex situations.
  • You are eager to learn, open to feedback, and willing to understand loan-related processes in depth.
  • You work well with others and believe in supporting the team, sharing knowledge, and contributing to collective success.
  • You are comfortable working under pressure and can manage multiple tasks while maintaining a high level of service quality.
  • If you prefer to only respond when asked or wait for instructions before taking action, this role may not be the right fit.

What We Are Looking For:

  • Qualification: Bachelor’s degree required.
  • Experience: Experience in customer service, client communication, administrative support, or a similar role would be preferred.
  • Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to connect with clients professionally through phone calls and emails.
  • Customer Focus: A genuine interest in helping clients, understanding their needs, and providing a positive customer experience.
  • Attention to Detail: Ability to manage client information, loan details, emails, and follow-ups with accuracy and care.
  • Problem-Solving Skills: Ability to identify issues, manage objections, escalate red flags when needed, and focus on practical solutions.
  • Tech Readiness: Experience using Gmail and Google Workspace tools such as Google Drive, Docs, and Sheets.
  • Work Style: Able to work with minimum supervision, manage pressure, stay organised, and complete tasks within expected timelines.
  • Mindset: A great attitude, strong desire to learn, accountability, dependability, and willingness to grow within a collaborative team.

Why Alaya?

At Alaya, our team is our most valuable asset. We are passionate about creating a work environment where care for one another, passion for excellence, and a sense of oneness drive everything we do. Here’s what you can expect:

  • Growth Opportunities: We are committed to your personal and professional development.
  • Inclusive Culture: Be part of a team where your ideas and contributions are valued, and where you can make a meaningful impact.
  • Meaningful Work: Play an important role in supporting clients beyond loan settlement and helping them continue their financial journey with confidence.
  • Oh also, did we mention, we only work 5 days a week? Mon-Fri.

Besides the list of benefits that the Labour Law mandates, we also offer:

  • Social Security Fund (SSF)
  • Exclusive leaves and bonuses
  • Festival, profit, and book reading bonus
  • Team building activities and social events
  • Accident and medical insurance coverage
  • International working environment exposure
  • Continuous learning and development opportunities
  • Customer Referral – Refer your friends and relatives in Australia to use our services and we’ll reward you!
  • Work hours: 6:00 am to 2:00 pm, including a 1-hour lunch break.

Ready to Join Us?

If you’re passionate about client service, enjoy building long-term relationships, and are eager to grow with a company that values your contribution, we’d love to hear from you.

Posiiton: Project Coordinator

Project Location: West Rukum (Bafikot and Tribeni Rural Municipalities), Nepal
Service type: Mother and Child Health Integrated with Livelihoods
Project Duration: Five years (annual renew as per performance)
Post Level: Mid-level management
Reports to: Program Manager
Supervisory role: 5-7 staff
Qualifications: Master’s degree in public health, Social Science, Development Studies or a related field.

Professional

Experience

  • Minimum of 5 years of relevant professional experience in MNCH, livelihood and entrepreneurship development programs.

Organisation Background:

  • Human Development and Community Services (HDCS) is a faith-based NGO working in three main sectors of health, education, and community development since 1991. Currently, it manages various projects across Nepal especially in rural regions and provides services through hospitals, health camps, public health

programs, disaster preparedness and response, school development programs, teacher training, educational daycare centres for children with special needs, and community radio stations. HDCS is committed to attract and retain the best employees from all ethnicities, gender and backgrounds in its vision to transform the
communities.

Purpose:

The Project Coordinator (PC) is responsible for the overall planning, implementation, coordination, monitoring, documentation, and reporting of the SHINE Project in Rukum West. The position leads quality project delivery in close coordination with local governments, Training Centers, Municipal Health Sections, Municipal Agriculture Sections, and other relevant local government stakeholders to strengthen local health systems, promote sustainable agriculture, livelihoods, and entrepreneurship, and ensure the achievement of project objectives. The role mainstreams gender equality, disability inclusion, safeguarding, and social

inclusion, ensuring equitable access to quality health services, resources, participation, and decision-making opportunities for women, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities while contributing to sustainable community development.

Responsibilities:

1. Project Leadership, Planning & Coordination (25%)

  • Lead the planning, implementation, coordination, and monitoring of the SHINE Project to ensure achievement of project objectives, quality standards, and donor requirements.
  • Develop and implement Detailed Implementation Plans (DIPs), Annual Implementation Plans (AIPs), Annual Procurement Plans (APPs), work plans, and implementation schedules for integrated MNCH, livelihood, and entrepreneurship interventions.
  •  Coordinate and collaborate with local governments, health, education, agriculture, and other stakeholders to integrate project activities into local government plans, secure required approvals, and ensure effective implementation.
  • Ensure timely implementation of project activities, achievement of project outputs and milestones, effective risk management, and timely resolution of implementation challenges.
  • Represent the project in coordination forums, technical working groups, and stakeholder meetings to strengthen partnerships, collaboration, advocacy, and resource mobilization.

2. Programme Quality & Technical Oversight (20%)

  • Lead and ensure the quality implementation of integrated MNCH, livelihood, and entrepreneurship interventions in accordance with project design, national guidelines, organizational standards, and donor requirements.
  • Plan, implement, and oversee project activities through regular field monitoring, supportive supervision, quality
    assurance, and evidence-based review to ensure achievement of project targets and outcomes.
  • Strengthen the technical capacity of project staff, health workers, HFOMCs, teachers, farmers, entrepreneurs, and partner institutions through training, coaching, mentoring, technical guidance, and supportive supervision.
  •  Provide technical leadership and practical solutions to address implementation challenges, improve service quality, and ensure timely and effective delivery of project activities.
  •  Promote innovation, adaptive management, and the integration of gender equality, disability inclusion, safeguarding, climate resilience, and community participation to enhance programme quality, sustainability, and project impact.

3. Monitoring, Evaluation, Documentation & Reporting (15%)

  • Monitor project progress against approved plans, indicators, and the project logframe through frequent field visits, supportive supervision, and data verification.
  •  Ensure project staff collect, verify, and submit timely, complete, and accurate data through Kobo Toolbox and other approved monitoring systems.
  • Prepare high-quality monthly, quarterly, annual, and donor reports based on evidence and verified project data.
  • Document case studies, success stories, impact stories, lessons learned, and evidence of project achievements.
  • Maintain accurate project records, databases, Kobo Toolbox data, and supporting documentation.
  • Use monitoring findings, field evidence, and data to support evidence-based decision-making and improve programme performance.

4. Stakeholder Engagement & Partnership (10%)

  • Build strong partnerships with local governments, communities, development partners, and other key stakeholders to ensure effective project implementation.
  •  Coordinate with local level and other relevant government sections to integrate project activities into municipal annual plans and programmes and obtain necessary approvals and endorsements.
  •  Facilitate coordination meetings, review workshops, joint monitoring visits, and multi-stakeholder forums to strengthen collaboration and accountability.
  •  Represent the project in government, technical, and coordination meetings, and maintain effective communication with key stakeholders.
  • Strengthen community participation, local ownership, and partnerships to promote sustainability, resource mobilization, and effective service delivery.

5. Financial & Resource Management (10%)

  • Monitor project budget utilization, expenditure, and burn rate in close coordination with the Finance and Programme departments to ensure efficient use of project funds.
  • Lead procurement planning and oversee the timely acquisition of goods, services, and equipment in accordance with organizational and donor procurement policies.
  • Ensure efficient, transparent, and accountable management of project resources, assets, and inventories.
  •  Review expenditures against approved budgets, work plans, and procurement plans, and recommend corrective actions to address variances.
  •  Ensure compliance with organizational financial policies, donor requirements, procurement procedures, and audit standards.
  •  Identify opportunities for resource mobilization and collaborate with local governments, development partners, private sector actors, and other stakeholders to leverage additional resources and maximize project impact.

6. Team Leadership & Capacity Development (10%)

  • Supervise, coach, mentor, and manage project staff to ensure high performance, accountability, and achievement of project objectives.
  •  Conduct regular performance reviews, provide constructive feedback, and support individual performance improvement and professional development.
  •  Assess staff capacity development needs and facilitate appropriate training, coaching, mentoring, and learning opportunities to strengthen technical and managerial competencies.
  •  Empower project staff by promoting delegation, ownership, teamwork, innovation, and continuous learning to enhance programme quality and organizational effectiveness.
  • Promote a positive, inclusive, and collaborative work environment by applying the Do No Harm approach and fostering teamwork, mutual respect, and adherence to HDCS values, policies, and code of conduct.

7. Compliance, Safeguarding & Inclusion (5%)

  •  Ensure compliance with organizational policies, donor requirements, government regulations, and project guidelines.
  • Mainstream safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, and accountability across all project activities.
  •  Promote ethical conduct and adherence to the HDCS Code of Conduct, organizational values, safeguarding policies, and accountability standards
  •  Identify, report, and address compliance and safeguarding risks, ensuring timely corrective actions and continuous improvement.

8. Knowledge Management & Organizational Support (5%)

  •  Develop and disseminate IEC materials, project communication products, and visibility materials in line with the organizational Knowledge Management and Communication Strategy.
  • Promote project visibility through radio programmes, social media, audio-visual materials, and impactful videos for awareness, advocacy, learning, and resource mobilization.
  • Capture, document, and share best practices, innovations, lessons learned, research findings, and success stories to strengthen organizational learning and evidence-based programming.
  •  Contribute to building a organization learning culture by promoting knowledge sharing, cross-learning, reflection, and continuous improvement across projects and teams.
  •  Perform other duties assigned by the Line manager in support of organizational priorities.

Essential Skills & Competencies:

  • Project Leadership & Management: Ability to lead, coordinate, implement, and manage integrated development projects effectively.
  •  Technical Competence: Sound knowledge of MNCH, livelihood, entrepreneurship, and community development programmes.
  •  Communication & Representation: Excellent verbal, written, presentation, facilitation, organizational and interpersonal skills in Nepali and English.
  • Planning & Organizational Skills: Strong planning, coordination, prioritization, and time management skills.
  •  Partnership & Teamwork: Ability to build effective partnerships, collaborate with multidisciplinary teams, and foster a positive work environment.
  •  Leadership & Capacity Development: Ability to supervise, coach, mentor, and develop project staff while promoting accountability and teamwork.
  •  Problem Solving & Adaptability: Strong analytical, decision-making, and problem-solving skills with the ability to adapt to changing priorities.
  •  Monitoring, Reporting & Digital Skills: Proficiency in Microsoft Office, Kobo Toolbox, report writing, data management, and evidence-based reporting.
  •  Knowledge Management & Learning: Ability to document and share lessons learned, best practices, case studies, and impact stories to support organizational learning.
  •  Cultural Sensitivity: Respect for local cultures and the ability to work effectively with women, children, persons with disabilities, and marginalized communities in Rukum West.
  • Integrity & Inclusion: Demonstrated commitment to HDCS values, ethical conduct, safeguarding, gender equality, disability inclusion, social inclusion, accountability, and the HDCS Code of Conduct.
  • Field Orientation & Resilience: Willingness to travel extensively and work effectively in remote and challenging field environments.
  •  Driving License: Valid Category “A” motorcycle driving license with a minimum of two years of driving experience

Posiiton: Senior Project Coordinator – UPLIFT Project
Job Identification: 17069
Job Category: Business Transformation
Apply Before: 07/23/2026, 11:59 PM
Job Schedule: Full time
Locations: FO Surkhet – Field office

The Opportunity

Save the Children believes every child deserves a future. In Bhutan and around the world, we give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. We do whatever it takes for children – every day and in times of crisis – transforming their lives and future we share. Save the Children expects that anyone associated with it abides by its Safeguarding and other Zero Tolerance Policies.

The position holder will provide strategic, technical, and managerial leadership for the UPLIFT Project, building on the successes and lessons learned from the POWER 4 AY project, funded by Save the Children Italy. The position is responsible for ensuring the effective implementation of the project through strong program leadership, cross-functional coordination, and effective partnership management with government agencies and partner NGOs (PNGOs) under the Surkhet Field Office

Under the supervision of the Head of Field Program Operations (HoFPOs) and with technical guidance from the Livelihoods Specialist, the position holder will establish and maintain strong coordination with key support functions, including Finance, Logistics, PDQI, POD, and MEAL, at both the Field Office and Country Office levels, as well as with the Bhutan team. The position will ensure timely, effective, and high-quality project implementation through close cross-functional collaboration, proactive coordination, and efficient operational support.

The position holder will ensure the development and implementation of high-quality, results-oriented project plans and ensure effective stakeholder coordination at the field level. The position will foster strategic engagement with the private sector to enhance youth employability through vocational training, micro-enterprise development, and innovative livelihood approaches. The position holder will also establish and oversee robust monitoring systems throughout the project cycle to ensure quality implementation, evidence-based decision-making, accountability, and the timely achievement of project outcomes.

The position holder is responsible for ensuring full compliance with Save the Children International’s (SCI) and donor policies, procedures, and standards throughout the project lifecycle, while adhering to the technical guidance and implementation requirements of Save the Children Italy.

The position holder will be responsible for preparing and submitting high-quality project plans, progress reports, quality review reports, and associated action plans to Save the Children Italy (SC Italy) and other relevant stakeholders, as required. In close coordination with the Country Office Award Management team, the position holder will serve as the primary focal point for communication and coordination with the SC Italy Desk.

The position holder will foster an enabling and collaborative environment that empowers partner organizations to effectively implement project activities, ensuring quality delivery, timely reporting, and compliance with project standards. The position holder will strengthen collaboration with government counterparts, the private sector, and other key stakeholders to maximize project outcomes, promote sustainability, and enhance benefits for target groups. Effective partnership management of the SC Italy-funded project is a key responsibility of this position.

In addition, the position holder will work together with Bhutan Office to develop consolidated project report on annual basis ensuring quality and donor standards.

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

Planning & Budgeting

  • Lead the planning processes and ensures partners have detailed implementation plan including realistic phased budget outlining major activities and timeline for the funds allocated in required planning templates provided by the organization.
  • Ensures appropriate fund allocation and expenditure monthly and take corrective measures by revisiting plans and communicating timely with technical advisor, finance and Award team.
  • Reviews the project’s BVAs and reports on any discrepancies identified in comparison to the Program BVA shared by the Finance team monthly.
  • Monthly monitoring of fund allocation and expenditure, identify variances, and take corrective actions through plan revisions and timely coordination with Technical Advisors and relevant departments.
  • Coordinates with SCI and partner team to design a robust field visit plan, self-assessments and monitoring systems including follow up on recommendations with relevant department and impact areas.
  • Leads the revision of budgets during budget forecast and on exchange rate fluctuations as per organizational procedures.
  • Prepare and implement a private sector engagement plan, including collaboration with business incubators, based on the findings and recommendations of the market assessment and private sector mapping.
  • Coordinates with Thematic Specialist and Advisors for technical assistance, as required.

Technical Assistance and Quality Assurance:

  • Provide oversight and ensure quality of programmes in the field ensure its optimum benefit to the vulnerable population.
  • Provide technical support to implementing partners to ensure the quality implementation of project activities related to private sector-led job placement and incubation-supported micro-enterprise development, while promoting climate-resilient, green job standards and sustainable livelihood practices.
  • Conduct regular field visits to partner organisations and areas, check and ensure the quality, identify best practices, identify issues to be addressed, and share any issues with the technical advisor to seek solutions/alternatives
  • Coordinate to ensure that all project implementation materials /guidelines are reviewed by relevant technical team
  • Provide technical support to implementing partners on life skills, business incubation approaches, enterprise development, business promotion and marketing, green jobs and green skills, and other emerging approaches and cross-cutting issues related to livelihoods promotion and youth employability.
  • Ensure that project quality benchmarks and standards are established, finalized jointly with MEAL, Technical Advisors, and partners, and consistently applied across all levels of implementation.

Programme Operations & Management

  • Lead market assessments, livelihood opportunity mapping, private sector engagement, and onboarding of strategic private sector partners for the project.
  • Ensures programmatic and financial accountability including tracking of program progress and budget expense in the use of funds and achievement of all related projects, in alignment with Annual Plan and Country Strategy Plan.
  • Ensure the program operations manual (POM) and its components are prepared, understood by relevant staff, and kept in place for monitoring.
