The Centre for Mental Health and Counselling – Nepal (CMC-Nepal), a national-level NGO dedicated to promoting mental health and psychosocial well-being, is pleased to announce an exciting opportunity to join our team as a Psychosocial Coordinator and Psychosocial Counsellor under the Empowered Women Prosperous Nepal (EWPN) project and GBV Prevention and Response-Phase 2 Project. The both projects, are supported by the United Nations Population Fund (UNFPA), aims to empower women and promote gender equality in Nepal in 18 districts across four provinces— Sudurpachhim, Karnali, Madesh and Koshi. CMC-Nepal focuses its activities in these projects on enhancing access to mental health and psychosocial support services for women and girls, particularly those affected by gender-based violence (GBV) and other forms of adversity.

Job title: Psychosocial Counsellor

Number of positions: 1 (One)

Location: Rajbiraj, Saptari district

Position Overview: The Psychosocial Counselor (PSC) will play a pivotal role in providing trauma-counseling, support, and care to survivors of GBV. The PSCs work closely with a multidisciplinary team, will empower survivors to heal, rebuild their lives, and access the resources they need to live meaningfully. This position offers a unique opportunity to coordinate with local governments, extend support to CPSWs, Case Managers, FCHVs and establish strong communication and network with the health facilities in the EWPN project activity locations. He/ She will be responsible for providing an effective psychosocial service to the survivors of GBV at the OCMC hospitals.

Roles/ Responsibilities:

  • Identify and assess physical development, health and other needs for well- being based in the age, mental condition, race, ethnicity etc. by filling up of intake forms.
  • Develop and prepare effective GBV response and care plan and strategies for the overall wellbeing, support, and counselling services of the persons in the respective project locations.
  • Prepare action plan to meet individual/ family/ group counselling/ case management.
  • Facilitate/ conduct non- discriminatory survivor centric counselling sessions.
  • Prepare and suggest for the possible activities which are beneficial for the well-being of the GBV survivors.
  • Supervise and work with GBV survivors in individual or group setting to carry out interventions based on the nature of the problem and choosing the best setting that works for the best interest of the survivor.
  • Coordinate to make necessary intervention and referrals to respond promptly in sensitive cases which need additional support.
  • Assess the client’s overall progress on a regular basis and encourage personal development
  • Record and document individual cases and prepare case study and success story regularly.
  • Maintain confidentiality and follow the ethics with promotion of survivor-centric learning strategies.
  • Identify GBV survivor’s attitude towards the family and community and facilitate to develop positive aspects towards their family and community and support for reintegrating them in the community.
  • Deliver OCMC-based psychosocial services and plan for frequent field visits.
  • Follow-up for the well-being of the GBV survivors.
  • Collect, compile, and prepare a detailed qualitative/ quantitative progress report of the services delivered to GBV survivors to the supervisor on monthly basis
  • Support to case managers, CPSWs, & CPSW coordinators as required.
  • Coordinate with LGUs and district level stakeholders.
  • Any other tasks asked by CMC-Nepal/ supervisor as per need.

Qualification and experience requirements:

  • Must have a Bachelor’s degree in any one of the domains such as Psychology, Social Work, Public Health, or Nursing, and be trained on a 6-month psychosocial counselling course under the NHTC or any other recognized professional organization. Candidate with an MA in Psychology/ Counselling Psychology or the one received a PGD course in Counseling Psychology shall apply for the position.
  • At least two years of experience having worked as a psychosocial counsellor, preferably with the GBV survivors.
  • Must be highly motivated to work in multi-cultural/ contextual, and challenging situations, and is expected to have strong leadership and coordination/ communication skills.
  • Must have basic computer skills—MS Word, Excel, PPT, familiar with e-mail correspondence.
  • The candidate should be knowledgeable in writing a report in English and Nepali languages, and is expected to have a learning attitude, and also that two wheelers will be in the priority.

CMC-Nepal is committed for the safeguarding of the children and vulnerable adults and implementation of Children and Vulnerable Adult Safeguarding Policy, including PSEHA policy. The commitment in implementation of the safeguarding will be checked in interview and reference check of the applicant.

Salaries and benefits: As per the project agreement between the UNFPA and CMC-Nepal

Candidates particularly from disadvantaged and socially excluded/marginalized groups and Madhesh Province are strongly encouraged to apply.

Only short-listed candidates will be contacted for further selection process. All the rights for recruitment, selection and cancelation (if required) of this recruitment are reserved by CMC Nepal.

Position: Partnership and Safer Program Coordinator
Job Identification: 15119
Job Category: Programme Operations
Apply Before: 01/22/2026, 11:59 PM
Locations: FO Bardibas – Field office

The Opportunity

Save the Children believes every child deserves a future. In Bhutan and around the world, we give children a healthy start in life, the opportunity to learn and protection from harm. We do whatever it takes for children – every day and in times of crisis – transforming their lives and future we share. Save the Children expects that anyone associated with it abides by its Safeguarding and other Zero Tolerance Policies.

The Partnership and Safer Program Coordinator will work across departments to strengthen partnerships under the field office. The job holder is responsible to support field management team for overall management and strengthening of partnerships management in line with the SCI partnership strategy framework. This position is also equally responsible to build capacity of SCI and partners on safer programming in direct coordination with the CO Safeguarding Focal Person and collaboration with different departments and project teams. The Program Coordinator-Partnership and Safer program is responsible for ensuing partnership managements follow SCI standard processes and the Nepal Country Office’s Partnership Strategy. Furthermore, the position will facilitate partners under the ‘Nepal Partner Graduation Model’ to develop and implement partner organizational capacity development plan following a detailed organizational assessment. The job holder needs to create a learning sharing forum for partners and document the key learning and promising approaches for dissemination across CO teams and SCI regions and offices. The position holder is equally responsible to ensure the smooth implementation of SCI safeguarding policies in SCI staff and partners under field office. S/he needs to work with different departments to plan, implement, monitor and review the projects through the lens of safer programming. In the event of a major humanitarian emergency, the role holder will be expected to work outside the normal role profile and be able to vary working hours accordingly.

KEY AREAS OF ACCOUNTABILITY:

The Partnerships and Safer Program Coordinator contribute to:

Partnership Development and Management

  • Provide orientation on SCI partnership standards and principles to ensure that staff are aware of the various partnerships standards.
  • Support programs in ensuring quality partnership management and knowledge sharing, including regular sector-based partner meetings.
  • Support in facilitating partnership processes related to the identification, assessment, selection of partners ensuring transparency and accountability therein.
  • Work with program team as required to ensure that partner capacity strengthening is properly integrated and implemented in program planning and budget.
  • Support program teams to design and implement good processes/criteria for scoping, selection and assessment of potential partners
  • Work in close coordination with the Partnerships Director to ensure that all staff are aware and oriented on the CO partnerships strategy
  • Provide input into the development of partnership monitoring systems and tools for the CO
  • Work across other key departments and units (MEAL, Finance, Supply Chain, Awards , thematic and program) to ensure a comprehensive partnership capacity building plan in place and its monitoring is in place

Quality Assurance of Partnership Management

  • Lead in quality assurance of Partner Agreements/ MOUs with governmental and non-governmental partners under the field office
  • Work with partners for the preparation of partner contracts such as partner agreements and memorandum of understanding etc.
  • Lead, monitor and support the field office in meeting compliance on partnership standards including quality framework standards and key performance indicators.
  • Ensure all staff are updated on the SCI and CO standard partnership policies, tools, guidelines etc.

Partners and Staff capacity Development

  • Support in designing training /orientation on partnership management for SCI staff under the field office.
  • Lead on implementation of capacity assessments with partners, developing corresponding capacity strengthening plans and coordinating and monitoring the execution.
  • Provide technical advice to partners and programs staff on facilitating organizational capacity strengthening based on plans.
  • Play a lead role in strengthening the capacity of the partner in coordination with different functions under the field office.
  • Lead the roll out and implementation of the Nepal Partner Graduation Model at the field office

Partnerships Risk Management

  • In coordination with field office units conduct partners risk assessment and develop risk mitigation measures in the field office.
  • Support field program team for the settlement of partner disputes and the management and close-out of suspected /confirmed fraud/mismanagement cases.
  • Facilitate Filed Office staff in conducting self-assessment of partnership risks and management.

Partnership Monitoring and Reporting

  • Provide technical support for joint monitoring of partnership and develop a master monitoring plan and tracker for partner.
  • Develop and share quarterly reports on partner capacity development, risk assessment of partners and risk mitigation measures that have been implemented.
  • Lead to organize semi-annual partnership progress review to exchange the learning and promising approaches.
  • Work with programs and ACCM department to ensure documentation and sharing of case studies and promising approaches within partnership management to be shared with different stakeholders

Safeguarding in Partner

  • Organize various training/orientation for SCI and partner staff on safeguarding policies and on the concept of safer programming in direct coordination with the CO Safeguarding Focal Person.
  • Support the capacity development of partner on identifying safeguarding risks in program and develop mitigating measures to minimize and prevent them.
  • Ensure safeguarding elements are included in program quality benchmark (QBM) and support MEAL team to develop QBM from safeguarding lens.
  • Support MEAL and program team to develop monitoring checklist of program by incorporating safeguarding indicators.
  • Conduct regular visits to project sites to ensure that reporting system is working and beneficiaries are well-known on how to provide feedback and report safeguarding concern and issues.
  • Liaise with country office safeguarding lead to ensure uniform messages of safeguarding are disseminated among internal field team, partner and at the community level.
  • Support country office safeguarding lead in managing safeguarding concerns coming from field location and from partners.
  • Work as safer program focal person for field office.

Qualifications and Experience:

  • Master’s degree in Social Sciences or equivalent with minimum of 3 years (2 years for GSI group) of relevant experience in I/NGOs or bachelor’s degree with minimum of 5 years (3 years for GSI group) of relevant experience in an I/NGOs

Essential

  • Thorough understanding and demonstrated commitment to child rights issues and the guiding principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child, including non-discrimination, child participation and the best interest of the child.
  • Having practical experience on partnership management processes, including capacity strengthening and organisational development practices
  • Experience doing project monitoring and investigation.
  • Experience of planning and undertaking training programmes/workshops for partner
  • Demonstrable commitment to Children’s Rights.

Desirable

  • Extensive knowledge about partnership and localization strategy.
  • Familiarity with humanitarian assistance and long-term development work in order to communicate effectively with partners.
  • A full understanding of political, economic and social contexts of the Country
  • Experience of working within challenging environments.

Required No.(s): 1 (Nepalese Citizen Only)

Contract length: Fixed Term

Location: Bardibas field office

The Organisation

We employ approximately 25,000 people across the globe and work on the ground in over 100 countries to help children affected by crises, or those that need better healthcare, education and child protection. We also campaign and advocate at the highest levels to realise the right of children and to ensure their voices are heard.

We are working towards three breakthroughs in how the world treats children by 2030:

  • No child dies from preventable causes before their 5th birthday
  • All children learn from a quality basic education and that,
  • Violence against children is no longer tolerated

We know that great people make a great organization, and that our employees play a crucial role in helping us achieve our ambitions for children. We value our people and offer a meaningful and rewarding career, along with a collaborative and inclusive workplace where ambition, creativity, and integrity are highly valued.

Who we are?

As a global leader, CARE is shaping the future of the humanitarian and development sector. Each year, we deliver support and services to millions of people in over a hundred countries. We do this by focusing on our mission and living the values that drive our organization. A career at CARE is an opportunity to be part of a movement that brings communities together to solve complex problems and foster lasting change throughout the world. We seek individuals who are passionate about humanitarian and development work, collaborate well with others, embrace learning and innovation, and deliver results.

CARE has been operational in Nepal since 1978 and works in partnerships with government and non-government stakeholders across the spectrum of humanitarian action and long-term development programs. We create local solutions to poverty and inequality and seek dignity for everyone every day and during times of crisis. CARE puts women and girls at the center of everything we do because they have proven to be the best hope for creating lasting change in the world.

What it’s like to work at CARE?

CARE is a mission-driven international humanitarian aid and development organization that offers an opportunity to work with people across the world. ​Position Title: Project Officer

​Location: Kathmandu, Nepal

Reports to: Programme Manager

Application Deadline: January 25, 2025

Contract Type: Full-Time

About CBM Global

CBM Global works alongside people with disabilities in low- and middle-income countries to fight poverty and exclusion and transform lives. Check out our website and LinkedIn profile to learn more. Drawing on over 100 years of experience, we work with the most marginalised in society to:

  • Break the cycle of poverty and disability
  • Treat and prevent conditions that lead to disability; and
  • Build inclusive communities where everyone can enjoy their human rights and achieve their full potential.

We work in over 20 countries, investing in long-term, authentic partnerships with the Disability Movement and multiplying our impact by delivering a combination of inclusive community-based programmes, advocacy for national and global policy change and inclusion advice to other organisations. CBM Global is a worldwide federation with the following Members: CBM Australia, CBM Ireland, CBM Kenya, CBM New Zealand, CBM Switzerland, and CBM UK.

About the Role

​

CBM Global Nepal has launched SAMAVESH: Supporting Active Measures Advancing Voices, Equality, Solidarity and Harmony, a three-year EU-funded project aimed at strengthening the meaningful political participation and representation of persons with disabilities in Nepal. Implemented with CBM Ireland, CBM Global Nepal, NFDN, and FWDN, the project will work with Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs), government bodies, political institutions, media, and civil society to build leadership, civic awareness, and disability-inclusive policymaking. Engaging around 700 key actors and reaching over 9,200 direct and 150,000 indirect beneficiaries across Bagmati and Karnali Provinces, SAMAVESH will particularly empower women and youth with disabilities, enhance OPD governance, and contribute to inclusive democratic systems ahead of Nepal’s upcoming federal elections.
​

The Project Officer will be responsible for effective coordination, implementation, monitoring, and reporting of the SAMAVESH Project. The position will serve as the primary focal person from CBM Global Nepal, ensuring high-quality delivery of project activities, partner support, compliance with EU requirements, and strong collaboration with OPDs.

​

This will be your team:

The Country Team that you will be joining has 25 employees. You will report to the Programme Manager and join a team of 5 people. You will have no direct reports.

​

Key Responsibilities

​

A. Project Management & Coordination

  •  Lead day-to-day coordination of project activities on behalf of CBM Global Nepal.
  • Ensure timely and quality implementation of activities ensuring they adhere to the approved work plan, logical framework, EU Grant Agreement requirements including schedules, deliverables and milestones as well as CBM Global standards.
  •  Maintain effective communication and coordination with implementing partners, OPDs, and relevant stakeholders.
  •  Facilitate regular project review meetings, planning sessions, and joint monitoring.
  • Maintain comprehensive and accurate project documentation files (technical and administrative) to support compliance checks and audits.
  • Identify, assess and proactively manage project risks, including operational delays, compliance issues, and partner challenges.
  • Ensure project communication and visibility are delivered in accordance with EU visibility rules and branding guidelines (logo use, disclaimers, public materials).

​

B. Partner Support & Capacity Strengthening

  •  Provide technical and operational support to local implementing partners (NFDN and FWDN), local OPDs and CSOs.
  •  Strengthening partners’ capacity in project management, safeguarding, disability inclusion, and reporting.
  •  Guide partners on compliance with EU contractual conditions, project delivery and CBM Global procedures.
  • Conduct periodic internal compliance reviews of partner implementation and documentation.
  • Monitor sub-grants to OPDs/CSOs for contractual compliance, deliverables and financial eligibility

​

C. Monitoring, Evaluation, and Learning (MEL)

  •  Monitor field activities to ensure progress, quality, and adherence to the project log frame.
  • Conduct internal quality checks of all reports (interim, technical, final) ensuring compliance with CBM Global and EU templates, deadlines and content expectations.
  • Collect, verify, and analyse data for project reporting and learning.
  • Document best practices, case stories, and lessons learned.

​

D. Reporting & Compliance

  • Lead the consolidation and preparation of high-quality technical reports for submission to EU via CBM.
  • Ensure timely reporting from partners, complete documentation, and compliance with donor rules.
  • Support financial tracking and coordinate with the finance team to ensure expenditures align with the approved budget lines and eligibility criteria under EU rules

​

E. Stakeholder Engagement & OPD Collaboration

  •  Facilitate meaningful participation and engagement of OPDs throughout the project cycle.
  •  Maintain coordination with government bodies, civil society, and EU representatives as needed.
  •  Represent CBM in project events, workshops, and coordination forums.

​

F. Humanitarian Action

  •  In the event of a humanitarian emergency and subject to organisational priorities, the post holder may be requested to provide time-bound support to emergency response initiatives, while ensuring continuity of EU project obligations

​

G. Safeguarding

​

Knowledge

Understands the incident management framework and their first responder role in recording, responding and reporting incidents.

Understands the survivor-centred approach and how to apply it when receiving a complaint or responding to an incident. Knows local support services available in the community or region, and how to engage them.

Able to listen and accurately document reported concerns and complaints. Able to respect the confidentiality of safeguarding allegations. Able to appropriately apply the survivor-centred approach.

Reporting to: Director

Project: Advancing Rights and Inclusion in Sexual and Reproductive Health and Education (ARISE)

Duration: 1.5 years

Position Description

Blind Youth Association Nepal (BYAN) is seeking a qualified and experienced candidate for the position of Project Officer based in Belbari, Morang. The Project Officer will work primarily in the field and will report directly to the Director, while carrying out activities under the close supervision of both the Director and the Chapter President.

The Project Officer will be responsible for the effective implementation of the project at the field level, coordinating with partners and stakeholders including government agencies, civil society organizations, organizations of persons with disabilities, children and young people with disabilities, and their parents/teachers. The role requires ensuring that project activities are completed on time, within budget, and to the highest quality standards.

About the Project

The project “Advancing Rights and Inclusion in Sexual and Reproductive Health and Education (ARISE)” aims to strengthen disability-inclusive sexual and reproductive health and rights (SRHR) in Morang and Jhapa of Koshi province by empowering young people with disabilities through access to SRHR knowledge and information, sensitizing parents, teachers, schools, decision-makers, and service providers on the SRHR issues of young people with disabilities, improving SRHR services, and strengthening the disability movement by working with OPDs, CSOs, and other agencies. The project also advocates for improved SRHR policies and their effective implementation at provincial and local levels.

Key Responsibilities

  • Lead the planning, implementation, and day-to-day management of the project in line with organizational values and project objectives.
  • Develop detailed work plans, budgets, and implementation schedules and ensure timely delivery of project outputs.
  • Prepare and maintain high-quality project documentation, including progress reports, financial tracking inputs, case stories, and learning briefs.
  • Coordinate and maintain strong working relationships with provincial and local governments, OPDs, CSOs, schools, health service providers, community groups, and donors.
  • Lead advocacy initiatives at local and provincial levels to promote disability-inclusive SRHR and CSE policies and practices.
  • Mobilize, mentor, and support SRHR champions to deliver community-level SRHR and CSE sessions.
  • Facilitate SRHR, CSE, and disability orientation sessions in schools, health facilities, and community platforms.
  • Oversee the design, production, and dissemination of research and SRHR/CSE-related IEC materials in accessible formats.
  • Coordinate with media agencies and communication teams to promote positive narratives on disability and SRHR.
  • Ensure effective monitoring, documentation, data management, and timely reporting in line with donor and organizational requirements.
  • Ensure safeguarding, ethical standards, and confidentiality are maintained while working with children, young people, and marginalized communities.
  • Perform field-level activities as required and report to the Director, working in close coordination with the Chapter President and Central Office.

Job Specifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Public Health or a related Social Science field with at least two years of relevant professional experience; experience in project coordination or management is preferred.
  • Strong knowledge of national and international frameworks related to SRHR, CSE, and disability, including UNCRPD, SDGs, the Act Relating to Rights of Persons with Disabilities, and the Constitution of Nepal.
  • Demonstrated understanding of SRHR issues faced by young people, particularly persons with disabilities.
  • Experience in advocacy, community mobilization, and stakeholder coordination.
  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) and social media campaigning.
  • Strong organizational, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in diverse and inclusive environments.
  • Proactive, self-motivated, and able to work independently in field-based settings.
  • Fluency in both Nepali and English is required; knowledge of sign language or accessible communication methods is an added advantage.
  • Prior experience working with children and young people with disabilities and/or the LGBTIQ+ community is an added advantage.

Application Deadline

The deadline for submitting applications is 20th Jan, 2026.

How to Apply:

Interested and eligible candidates are requested to send their application, along with an updated CV and expected salary, to hr@byanepal.org with the subject line: “Application for the Post of Project Officer – Morang.”

We encourage online submission of proposals. Phone calls, video calls, and SMS will not be entertained.

BYAN promotes inclusion across gender, caste, ethnicity, Dalit, and disability. Persons with disabilities and LGBTIQ+ individuals are strongly encouraged to apply. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for further processes. The organization reserves the right to reject any/all applications without assigning reasons.

Position: Database Officer

Job Description

Nyaya Health Nepal is looking for a Database Officer to strengthen our data management systems, support evidence-based decision making, and enhance our organizational learning culture. The Database Engineer will join a team of IT professionals working to customize, develop and inmplement Electronic Health Record System at rural low resource settings. Applications are accepted on an immediate, rolling basis.

The Organization: Nyaya Health Nepal

Nyaya Health Nepal (NHN) is a Nepal-based NGO delivering healthcare to underserved communities in Nepal in close partnership with the Government of Nepal. We deliver care to nearly 200,000 people every year through an integrated healthcare approach that strategically uses technology and data to improve continuity of care and reduce morbidity and mortality in rural settings.

Our goal is to leverage insights generated during service delivery to inform public healthcare policy and strengthen Nepal’s health system.

For more details, please visit our website: www.nyayahealthnepal.org

The Opportunity: Are you the right fit?

We are seeking a Database Officer who will oversee the development, maintenance, and optimization of NHN’s data systems. The role requires strong technical skill, attention to detail, and the ability to work in environments that require creativity and efficient problem-solving with limited resources.

Job Specification

Management Structure

Reports To: Senior Impact Manager

Direct Reports: None (may supervise interns/assistants as needed)

Location: Based on Kathmandu but may need to travel to implementation sites

Must-Have Qualities:

  • Strong alignment with NHN culture, ethics, and patient-centered values
  • Solid technical skills in SQL, EHR, DHIS2, and data system development
  • Good time and task management with ability to handle multiple workflows
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Clear communication in English and Nepali
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision
  • Experience in data quality, dashboards, and documentation is an advantage

Big 3 Responsibilities:

1. Database Development, Migration, and Optimization for the Integrated EHR Platform

  •  Perform migration and optimization of existing databases.
  •  Normalize and cluster current databases to improve performance.
  •  Design and develop database architectures for various systems.
  • Collaborate with the team to ensure products are delivered on time and according to requirements, from planning through implementation.
  • Enhance system integrations across platforms such as OpenMRS, OpenELIS, Odoo, DCM4Che and DHIS2.
  •  Provide regular updates to the Team Lead on progress and challenges.
  •  Write complex and diverse queries based on organizational requirements.

2. Agile Development Responsibilities

  •  Estimate the effort required to implement user stories.
  •  Contribute to achieving sprint goals through development tasks.
  •  Implement relevant test cases.
  • Conduct unit tests and initial acceptance testing.
  • Identify blockers and report them to the Scrum Master.
  • Work in a self-organized manner within the team.
  •  Participate in daily Scrum meetings.

3. Quality Delivery and Ownership of the Integrated EHR Product

  • Deliver work only after thorough testing.
  •  Prepare technical documentation for all completed tasks.
  •  Provide technical insights when needed, clearly explaining technical concepts to the Team Lead.
  •  Coordinate and communicate with the global Bahmni coalition if required.

Additional Responsibilities

  • Participate in all project phases, including requirement gathering, design, and development.
  • Design, write, and maintain efficient, reliable database and queries.
  • Support EHR development and implementation, including training staff and clinicians in the effective use of NepalEHR.
  •  Provide feedback to EMR/EHR developers to support product improvement.
  • Assist the team with generating reports from the database.
  •  Optimize existing databases to improve overall system performance.
  • Manage database query components for DHIS integration.

Note: The above responsibilities are not exhaustive. The Database position may be assigned additional duties as directed by the line manager.

Forum for Rural Welfare and Agricultural Reform for Development (FORWARD Nepal) is a nationally recognized non-governmental organization working to enhance sustainable livelihoods, promote inclusive rural development, and strengthen climate-resilient and agriculture-based economies in Nepal. In order to support its programmes and institutional operations, FORWARD Nepal invites applications from qualified and committed Nepali citizens based in Chitwan for the following position.

Position: Admin and Finance Officer – One (Only Female)
Location: Chitwan

Brief job descriptions

The Admin and Finance Officer (AFO) will be responsible for the overall administration and financial management of FORWARD Nepal and its projects, and will be accountable for ensuring transparency, accountability, and an efficient administrative and financial management system in line with organisational policies, donor requirements, and prevailing laws and regulations of Nepal. The AFO will oversee budgeting, financial planning, accounting, cash and bank management, procurement, assets and inventory, payroll, taxation, and statutory compliances, and ensure timely and accurate financial reporting to management, donors, and governing bodies. The role also supports human resource functions, ensuring legal and regulatory compliance, particularly with the Social Welfare Council (SWC), District Administration Office (DAO), and local governments, including registration renewals, agreement management, and timely submission of required reports and documents. In addition, the AFO will support organisational management by strengthening internal control systems, facilitating internal and external audits, and ensuring timely implementation of audit recommendations. S/he will provide clear guidance and capacity support to project teams on financial management, donor compliance, and administrative procedures, and will contribute to institutional strengthening of FORWARD Nepal through effective coordination, documentation, and adherence to organisational manuals, board decisions, and partnership agreements.

Educational qualification and Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Business Studies, Management, or an equivalent discipline, with at least 5 years of relevant work experience in the development/NGO sector or Preferred Master’s degree in similar discipline with 3 years of experience in a similar role within the development sector.
  • Proven experience in administration and financial management of donor-funded projects.

Professional Experiences

  • Demonstrated experience in establishing, implementing and strengthening organisational administration and finance systems, financial policies, procedures, internal controls and compliance mechanisms
  • Proven experience in overall organizational financial management, including budgeting, financial planning, accounting, cash and bank management, payroll, taxation, statutory reporting and financial analysis.
  • Experience in office administration and management, staff management, logistics, procurement, inventory control, asset management and documentation systems.
  • Strong experience in human resource administration, staff recruitment processes, personnel file management, contracts, attendance and leave management, payroll coordination, performance appraisal support and staff compliance with HR policies
  • Hands-on experience in supporting the development, review and implementation of organisational policies and manuals such as financial, administrative, HR, procurement, and safeguarding policies
  • Experience in managing and ensuring compliance with labour laws, social security fund (SSF), income tax, VAT/TDS and other statutory requirements applicable in Nepal
  • Proven track record in donor compliance and project administration, including alignment of organisational systems with donor rules and partnership agreements
  • Experience in coordinating and facilitating internal and external audits, organisational assessments and due diligence processes and ensuring timely follow-up of audit findings
  • Ability to provide technical guidance, coaching and oversight to project and field teams on administrative, financial and HR procedures.
  • Strong coordination experience with management, Board, donors, government offices, banks, auditors and other stakeholders to ensure smooth organisational operations and compliance

Skills and Competencies

  • Strong knowledge of financial policies, internal control systems, and risk management
  • Proficiency in computerised accounting software and MS packages.
  • Ability to provide technical guidance and capacity support to project and field teams on financial and administrative procedures
  • Strong analytical, organisational, and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent communication, coordination, and reporting skills
  • High level of integrity, accountability, and attention to detail

Salary and Benefits

  • Salary and benefits for above mentioned position will be as per project provisions and FORWARD Nepal HR policy.

Application Procedure

Interested female candidates who meet these criteria can submit their application with the latest updated CV, a cover letter, and contact details of two professional references via the link https://forms.gle/Ebv5xrnj2eiUx6io9 by 17th January 2026. Please visit https://www.forwardnepal.org/announcements for further information.

FORWARD Nepal is an equal opportunity employer and strongly encourages applications from disadvantage groups (Women: Dalit, Janajati, Madhesi, People Living with Disability) and local residents during recruitment process.

The Staff Hiring Committee of FORWARD Nepal reserves all rights to make the final decision. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted for a written examination. FORWARD Nepal reserves the right to reject and cancel this vacancy and application without assigning any reason whatsoever.

  • Cover letter clearly indicating suitability for the position
  • Contact details of at least two professional referees

Position: Equity, Rights and Social Safeguards Technical Specialist

Purpose of the role

As the Equity, Rights and Social Safeguards Technical Specialist, you will lead the development, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of ZSL’s approach to Environmental and Social Safeguards (FAIRER) across ZSL programmes in Nepal and India, in line with ZSL’s FAIRER framework, IUCN’s Environmental and Social Management System (ESMS) and national legislation.

With a particular emphasis on leading Free, Prior and Informed Consent (FPIC) processes for the programme, you will ensure that local and Indigenous communities meaningfully participate in decisions that affect their lands, resources and livelihoods. You will also ensure that local people engaged in ZSL’s conservation activities are protected from harm, that concerns can be raised safely and confidentially, and that ZSL staff, partners and representatives uphold the highest standards of behaviour and accountability.

You will work to ensure that activities are implemented equitably, responsibly and in full compliance with environmental and social safeguards, ensuring that all interventions align with ZSL’s FAIRER Safeguards Framework, the IUCN ESMS and national regulations that respect human rights and promote equitable conservation outcomes. The role will be based in-region, located within ZSL’s Nepal office, and will oversee and support ESMS implementation and monitoring in Uttar Pradesh, India, working with ZSL’s implementing partner, the Wildlife Institute of India, under the Integrated Tiger Habitat Conservation Programme (ITHCP) Phase IV project.

You will ensure that ZSL meets its duty of care in relation to the Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), as well as other safeguarding policies as required, and that these align with Environmental and Social (E&S) safeguard compliance and monitoring requirements. You will work closely with the FAIRER Programme Co-Manager, ZSL’s ESMS Officer in Nepal, Project Managers in India and Nepal, and community organisers in both countries.

Key responsibilities: 

  • Manage all Environmental and Social Safeguard requirements, including the design, implementation and review of mitigation measures.
  • Oversee the implementation and monitoring of safeguarding frameworks to prevent and respond to all forms of exploitation, abuse and harassment within the organisation with a focus on community partners.
  • Design culturally appropriate FPIC processes that respect traditional governance, decision-making, and customary land and resource rights, ensuring FPIC is a lived consent process in line with ZSL’s Inclusive Engagement and FPIC safeguard.
  • Embedding ESMS, safeguarding and PSEAH principles into community engagement, education, and conservation activities, ensuring these are aligned with ZSL’s organisational values and global standards.
  • Work with community liaison officers to communicate environmental and social safeguarding instruments with local actors and local partners, ensure safeguarding instruments meet community needs and create positive action interventions to support communities, and in particular, vulnerable groups.
  • Lead on Environmental and Social Safeguarding reporting and documentation in line with the project reporting requirements and updating of safeguarding instruments.

About You

  • A degree (or equivalent professional qualification) in social science/development studies or a similar relevant field (e.g. international politics or political ecology) or relevant experience in implementing E&S safeguarding systems working with local actors.
  • Track record of implementing and managing Environmental and Social Safeguarding Instruments (including FPIC, Grievance Mechanisms, Stakeholder Engagement Plans and Indigenous Peoples Plans) across diverse stakeholder groups and ensuring a duty of care is adhered to.
  • Prior experience of delivering social equity and inclusion processes with experience leading work with a gender equity and social inclusion focus.
  • Ability to think critically and analyse complex and nuanced problems – the post holder will be capable of dealing with complex matters and communicating them effectively and in a timely manner.
  • Knowledge of safeguarding standards (e.g. CHS, IASC, Core Humanitarian Standards) and an understanding of safeguarding and Protection from Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH) principles, frameworks, and best practice in international and community contexts.
  • Fluent English and Nepali (spoken and written)
  • Good knowledge of current and emerging best practice related to National and International Environmental and Social Safeguards instruments, human-rights laws, environmental rules and regulations and Free Prior Informed Consent (FPIC) processes.
  • Good working knowledge and demonstrated experience of international frameworks related to Free Prior Informed Consent and the rights of Indigenous Peoples.

We encourage applications from members of the communities we work with, and from those who share our passion for conservation and collaboration. At ZSL, we value respect, local knowledge, and shared purpose, together, we can make a real difference for wildlife, people and planet.

About Us

We’re ZSL, an international conservation charity. Through our unrivalled animal experts in our two zoos (London Zoo and Whipsnade Zoo), the work of our pioneering scientists, our dedicated conservationists, our purpose is to inspire, inform and empower people to stop wild animals going extinct. Our vision is a world where wildlife thrives and we’re working every day to achieve this. Participate in the research data collection, data management and data analysis of the ongoing research studies. Ensure compliance of the research activities with approved protocol and overall research objectives.

Under the supervision of the Principal Investigator, the Research Officer will involve him/herself to research activities in designated working station and will:

  • Carry out research data collection according to approved research protocols.
  • Perform various core data collection activities including baseline, midline and end-line quantitative and qualitative data collection at various time points.
  • Create presentation slides and posters to help researchers present findings.
  • Assist in development, planning and management of research projects in coordination with Principal Investigator (PI).
  • Meet regularly with PI and others to discuss research study related topics.
  • Assist Project Manager to prepare and finalize project reports to be submitted internally or externally throughout the year.
  • Ethical management of human participants in research studies.
  • Review existing available research study related SOPs and documents.
  • Contribute in the development of relevant research articles (manuscripts and research proposals).
  • Handle logistics support for ordering, inventory, maintenance and repair of equipment and supplies.
  • Actively participate in various workshops and training.
  • Enthusiastic for working in an interdisciplinary team and preparedness to work in other research projects when necessary.
  • Report to line manager for any issues regarding research study related issues.

Person Specification:

  • Bachelor’s degree in public health or other relevant fields with at least 2 years of working experience in related fields.
  • Should possess competency in good clinical practice.
  • Should have sound knowledge and experience of quantitative and qualitative data collection skills.
  • Willingness to travel to data collection sites regularly.
  • Priorities will be given to those holding driving license.
  • Demonstrated skills on handling data collection software like REDCAP, KOBO, MWATER etc.
  • Analytical, observation, technical, and time management skills.
  • Demonstrated experience in the implementation of similar research and data collection methodologies.
  • Excellent oral and written communication skills in Nepali and English.
  • Excellent organizational skills and attention to detail.
  • Demonstrated experience in Microsoft Word, PowerPoint, Excel, and other software.

Application ends January 17, 2026

ABOUT WFP

The World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian organization saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity, for people recovering from conflict, disasters and the impact of climate change.

At WFP, people are at the heart of everything we do and the vision of the future WFP workforce is one of diverse, committed, skilled, and high performing teams, selected on merit, operating in a healthy and inclusive work environment, living WFP’s values (Integrity, Collaboration, Commitment, Humanity, and Inclusion) and working with partners to save and change the lives of those WFP serves.

WHY JOIN WFP?

  • WFP is a 2020 Nobel Peace Prize Laureate.

BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

The United Nations World Food Programme (WFP) is the world’s largest humanitarian organization, saving lives in emergencies and using food assistance to build a pathway to peace, stability and prosperity for people recovering from conflict, disasters, and the impact of climate change.
Working in Nepal since 1963, WFP has extensive knowledge of the socio-economic context of Nepal as related to food and nutrition security, livelihood creation as well as logistics capacity and emergency response. At present, WFP Nepal operates across the country with tailored programming based on present and predicted needs. Being a trusted UN partner, WFP is uniquely well-placed to support the Government, as well as local communities to tackle the underlying factors causing malnutrition in all its forms.

WFP launched its corporate Nutrition Strategy (2024-2030), and since 2024, WFP Nepal implements its country strategic plan which directly aligns with the Government’s 16th Plan, as well as the United Nations Sustainable Development Cooperation Framework for Nepal. WFP supports the Government’s efforts to reduce malnutrition, increase access to food and build sustainable food systems under Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 2 and to enhance global partnerships under SDG 17, whilst supporting SDG 4 on quality education and SDG 13 on climate action. Under the country strategic plan, support is provided through four outcomes:

Outcome 1: Affected and at-risk populations in Nepal meet their food, nutrition and other essential needs before, during and after shocks and other stressors.
Outcome 2: School-age children and adolescents and nutritionally deprived groups in Nepal have improved education and nutrition outcomes and greater access to affordable, nutritious and safe diets, including through social protection programmes, by 2028.
Outcome 3: Smallholder farmers and climate vulnerable populations in Nepal benefit from climate-resilient and equitable food systems, sustainable livelihoods and climate-proof assets and services by 2028.
Outcome 4: Communities vulnerable to and affected by crises in Nepal benefit from improved common services and enhanced capacities of Government and humanitarian and development actors by 2028.
To strengthen the Government’s capacity to implement integrated health and nutrition programming at local levels, WFP is seeking a Programme Associate (Nutrition) to support WFP nutrition programming and technical assistance.

BACKGROUND AND PURPOSE OF THE ASSIGNMENT:

ABOUT WFP

The United Nations World Food Programme is the world’s largest humanitarian agency fighting hunger worldwide. The mission of WFP is to help the world achieve Zero Hunger in our lifetimes. Every day, WFP works worldwide to ensure that no child goes to bed hungry and that the poorest and most vulnerable, particularly women and children, can access the nutritious food they need.

ORGANIZATIONAL CONTEXT

Job holders operate with a high degree of independence, manage more junior staff to ensure that programme and policy objectives are achieved in full. They are usually involved in a wide variety of programme and policy activities and analytical work, some of which may be of a considerable complexity. At this level, job holders are expected to contribute to performance improvement.

JOB PURPOSE

The Government of Nepal, with support from WFP, has implemented the Mid-day Meal Programme since 1974. Today, the programme spans all 77 districts across the country’s seven provinces, targeting more than three million children in over 27,000 schools and providing meals every school day, making it one of the largest social safety nets in the country. Through external support provided through several public and private donors, WFP has provided direct implementation support to the national programme for decades, and, by the end of 2025, will transition its three remaining districts to the national Mid-day Meal programme. From January 2026 onward, WFP will continue providing technical assistance and system strengthening support for an efficient and effective Mid-day Meal programme.

Despite strengthening policy frameworks, growing operational experience, and increased investments, gaps still remain in translating the policy into practice at the sub-national level (Province, District and local government) affecting the continuity, quality, and sustainability of the Mid-day Meal Programme. In late 2024, the government, under the leadership of the Minister of Education, Science and Technology, took the bold decision in developing and approving a national home-grown school feeding framework which paved the way to scaling up the home-grown school feeding approach in 250 of the country’s 753 Municipalities in the next three years starting from 100 Municipalities in fiscal year 2025/2026. This will, among other things, entail strengthening local government capacity to enhance and support the quality of implementation of the Mid-day Meal programme through the home-grown school feeding approach. In collaboration with the Ministry of Education, Science and Technology and provincial and local governments, WFP has successfully tested a context specific home-grown school feeding models that provide multiple benefits for children, the local communities, the country at large and have the proven potential to offset some of the implications of the limited cash allocations from the federal level.

In line with the government’s plans for scaling up the Home-Grown School Feeding framework, WFP aims to continue provide technical assistance in improving the quality of implementation of the national Mid-day meals programme through working closely with local governments and the school community. As such, WFP is seeking multiple Field Coordinators to be based in district headquarters to provide technical assistance to a cluster of local governments.

The Field Coordinators will be responsible to provide overall technical assistance to respective municipalities to strengthen local government and stakeholder capacity to implement the Mid-day Meal programme, and to adopt a home-grown school feeding approach in line with the Government’s home-grown school feeding framework.

Provide training and other capacity strengthening activities for government, school, smallholder farmers/cooperatives and community stakeholders. Support local governments operationalize the home-grown approach through coaching and mentoring, following the National Home-Grown School Feeding Framework. Support local governments to develop and contextualized procedures and guidelines to address the local needs under the Mid-day Meal programme with a home-grown approach including food procurement, contracting between schools and smallholder farmers and their cooperatives. Provide technical assistance on menu planning, social behaviour changes activities and support the monitoring and accountability system for the Mid-day Meal programme. Support strengthens local government capacity to identify potential collaboration and partnership opportunities for home-grown school feeding and related activities at municipal/ward/community level. Hold regular meetings with local governments, school staff and committees, farmers, cooperatives and other stakeholders to review workplan, progress, identify challenges and jointly develop solutions to address them. At least 6 years of relevant experience in implementing technical programmes at field level (i.e., education, agriculture, nutrition, food systems, etc.). The ability to work independently, to be a self-starter, motivated, and able to multi-task is essential for this role, and non-negotiable. Familiarity with the Microsoft Office suite is essential. Driving skills, as well as a valid license are required, as much time will be spent commuting between municipalities and district headquarters.

Rural Women Upliftment Association (RWUA), Haripur-02, Sarlaahi is a non-political, non-profit organization established 33 years ago on Kartik 22, 2050 B.S., with the vision of uplifting marginalized and rural women and communities. Since its inception, RWUA has been working in key areas including women’s empowerment, gender equality, social inclusion, education, health, livelihoods, child protection, Advocacy/lobbying, and transparent local governance, with a strong focus on Dalits, indigenous groups, persons with disabilities, and other marginalized populations. Through community-centred approaches, RWUA has supported capacity development, poverty reduction, counselling on foreign employment, assistance to vulnerable families, and overall empowerment.

RWUA, in partnership with Save the Children, has been funded, Implementing the Sponsorship (SAMUNNATI) Project in Sarlahi District since 2017 in Ishworpur and Haripur Municipalities, focusing on education, health, livelihoods, child protection, and advocacy, policy, and lobby, while continuing its recognised role as a leading gender / Child protection resource centre at district and regional levels.

ROLE PURPOSE:

The Field Coordinator – Education is responsible for executing a range of activities within the education sector, focusing on Early Childhood Care and Development (ECCD) and Basic Education. The role encompasses strategic project planning, implementation, monitoring, reporting, and effective collaboration with local government (LG) counterparts and stakeholders to ensure project deliverables are met.

The incumbent supervises and mentors Field Officers, facilitates research, documents lessons learned, and promotes best practices. The position is accountable for managing field-level education activities, ensuring quality implementation, and preparing comprehensive reports. The Field Coordinator is also responsible for upholding organizational priorities, including safeguarding, zero-tolerance policies, and safety/security measures.

Reports to: Program Manager

Staff reporting to this post: Field Officer

Budget Responsibility: Sponsorship Program

Reporting

  • Submit individual monthly/quarterly work plans and progress reports to the Line Manager.
  • Document and share project learnings, success stories, and case studies on a quarterly basis.

Capacity Development

  • Facilitate training and workshops on education-related activities for teachers, headteachers, MSCs, PTAs, and LG representatives.
  • Enhance the capacity of field officers through targeted training programs.

Evidence Generation

  • Bachelor’s degree in education (B.Ed.) from a recognized institution with at least 5 years of relevant experience. or Prior experience in education implementation and sponsorship programs is preferred. Experience working in multicultural environments.

MOMENTUM Country and Global Leadership (MCGL), funded by the U.S. Government, is a global mechanism that saves lives and improves access to quality, integrated health services by distributing life-saving commodities, medicines, and vaccines, and providing critical health care services for pregnant mothers and children under five. The Finance Officer will contribute to the financial oversight of the MCGL project by tracking project expenditures, monitoring budget performance, and ensuring proper financial documentation is maintained. They will also assist in preparing timely financial reports for submission to Donor, Jhpiego headquarters, and other stakeholders. The Officer oversees the financial aspect of Jhpiego programs in Nepal and ensures that financial systems are sound and compatible with standard accounting practices and follow USG, MCGL, JHU and Jhpiego rules and regulation. This includes assisting day to day financial operations of Nepal Country Office. Implement and maintain an on-site financial accounting and bookkeeping system required to assure the integrity and effective performance of Jhpiego Nepal’s financial operations.

(The Position is open only for Jhpiego’s Internal Staffs.)

Responsibilities

Specific Responsibilities

  • Ensure all expenditures are within the approved budget and have received the necessary authorization.
  • Process payment vouchers, checks, and electronic funds transfers (EFT) in a timely and accurate manner.
  • Monitor expenditures against approved budgets and work plans, providing regular updates.
  • Follow up on accounts receivable and ensure timely liquidation of staff advances. .
  • Maintain organized physical and electronic filing systems for accounting records, ensuring easy access and retrieval of documents.
  • Assist in developing work plans and budgets, participating in ongoing budget tracking and adjustments.
  • Assist in conducting financial and compliance reviews for program activities, ensuring adherence to donor and internal regulations.
  • Ensure office financial operations with particular emphasis on implementing and maintaining on-site financial accounting and bookkeeping system.
  • Assists in monthly financial reporting –
  • Reports on obligations and expenditure of the program budgets, including sub-agreement budgets with partner and donor agencies.
  • Maintain and file vouchers, petty cash, payments, and other financial communication and documentation.
  • Coordinate with Province Team esp Admin & Finance Asst/ Provincial Specialist for collecting/recording expenditure on district-based activities and travel expenses.
  • Assist and support & Guide Province- Admin finance team in program activities related to finance (workshop/training) in Centre and in Province
  • Support internal audits, donor reviews, and external audits as required.
  • Prepare and submit VAT reporting to USG, ensuring accurate and timely reconciliation of VAT claims as per donor requirements.
  • Perform any additional duties as assigned by the supervisor to support financial and administrative operations.

Required Qualifications

Qualifications

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting or Finance or related subject.
  • At least 5 to 6 years of directly relevant experience required
  • Demonstrated proficiency in MS office/ Excel in presenting, analyzing and interpreting data.
  • Understanding of Government of Nepal rules, regulations and policies in accounting and finance; and familiarity with I/NGO and donor-supported projects.

Mount Everest Forest Botanicals Alliance (MEFBA), through private sector investment, is implementing the TerraMrida Landscape Restoration Project – a community-led shade-grown coffee cultivation initiative focused on agroforestry, nursery development, and nature-based climate solutions in eastern Nepal. The project operates in coordination with Diktel-Rupakot-Majhuwagadhi Municipality for local facilitation.

MEFBA invites applications from motivated fresh agriculture graduates for immediate field placement to support on-ground implementation and GIS-based documentation.

Position: Project Field Assistant – Agriculture & GIS

Assignment Duration

  • 4 months (Short-term)
  • Immediate mobilization required

Duty Station: Diktel, Khotang District (Field-based with regular travel to project sites)

Key Responsibilities

  • Support field implementation of coffee agroforestry and landscape restoration activities
  • Conduct GIS-based mapping, GPS data collection, and plot boundary demarcation
  • Assist in baseline surveys, geo-referenced photo documentation, and farmer data collection
  • Support community nursery management and basic nursery records
  • Maintain field documentation, activity logs, and progress reports
  • Data entry, analysis, and reporting using MS Excel and MS Office
  • Coordinate with local farmers, communities, and field supervisors

Required Qualifications & Skills

  • Fresh graduate in Agriculture, Forestry, Natural Resources, or related discipline
  • Independent GIS expertise (QGIS/ArcGIS, GPS handling)
  • Strong proficiency in MS Office, especially Excel
  • Exposure to nursery management or plantation work (preferred)
  • Ability to work in remote rural field conditions
  • Must own a motorbike with valid driving license
  • Strong documentation and reporting skills

Compensation & Facilities

  • Salary: NPR 30,000 per month
  • Free food and boarding at MEFBA project field hostel, Diktel

Career Opportunity

High-performing candidates will be considered for permanent placement with MEFBA after completion of the assignment, with a commensurate salary.

Application & Selection

This is an urgent field requirement. Preference will be given to candidates who can mobilize immediately.

Interested candidates must submit the following to info@forestalliancenepal.com within 31st January, 2026:

1. Updated CV with Facebook Profile link
2. Recent passport-size photograph
3. Structured self-assessment of GIS and field competencies (covering GPS data collection, shapefile creation, KML/KMZ, Excel-based reporting, and field documentation)
4. Scenario-based written response (maximum 1 page) as outlined below
5. (Optional but strongly preferred) Sample GIS or Excel work demonstrating relevant skills

Scenario-Based GIS & Field Documentation Task

(To be submitted as part of the application – max 1 page)

Imagine a coffee-based agroforestry project implemented at a landscape scale. The project consists of a cluster of 50 independent cooperative societies, collectively forming the overall project area. The aggregate farmland of all member farmers constitutes the effective project boundary.

Each cooperative society comprises 25–40 member farmers. Individual farmers cultivate shade-grown coffee under agroforestry systems, with one or more farm plots per farmer.

For project documentation, monitoring, and reporting purposes, the spatial structure of the project is organized hierarchically as follows:

  • Individual farmer-owned farm plot polygons
  • Nested within a Cooperative Society polygon
  • Each Cooperative Society polygon further nested within the overall project boundary polygon representing all 90 cooperatives

Based on this structure, explain step-by-step how you would:

  • Collect and validate GPS data for individual farmer farm plots
  • Digitize farm-level polygon shapefiles
  • Delineate and verify Cooperative Society boundary polygons
  • Ensure correct spatial nesting and topology across all levels
  • Link spatial data with farmer and cooperative attributes in Excel
  • Export and share spatial outputs (shapefiles, KML/KMZ, maps) for reporting and field verification

Briefly mention the GIS tools/software you would use and how you would ensure data accuracy and consistency in a field-based setting.

Applications should be submitted promptly due to immediate mobilization requirements.

About CDM-Nepal

CDM-Nepal is a national non-governmental organization committed to strengthening community resilience, social inclusion, and sustainable development. Through long-term partnerships with local governments, communities, and international donors, CDM-Nepal implements evidence-based and accountable programmes across Nepal.

The Community Resilience Programme (CRP) – Phase IV (2026–2028) aims to enhance institutional, social, and economic resilience of vulnerable communities through locally led, climate-responsive, and inclusive approaches.

Position Summary

The Senior Finance & Admin Officer (SFAO) will be responsible for ensuring sound financial management, administrative efficiency, donor compliance, and statutory accountability of the Community Resilience Programme at the field level.

This is a senior field-based role, requiring strong hands-on experience in NGO financial systems, coordination with local governments (Palikas), donor-funded project compliance, and support during audits, evaluations, and reporting cycles.

Key Responsibilities

Financial Management & Compliance

  • Manage day-to-day financial operations of the project at field level in line with approved budgets, donor agreements, and organizational policies.
  • Ensure accurate bookkeeping, voucher processing, advance settlements, bank and cash reconciliations.
  • Monitor budget utilization, flag variances, and support financial planning and forecasting.
  • Ensure compliance with donor requirements, GoN regulations, taxation (PAN, TDS), and Social Welfare Council (SWC) guidelines.
  • Support internal, external, donor, and government audits and evaluations.

Administrative & Procurement Oversight

  • Oversee procurement processes in line with organizational and donor procurement policies.
  • Maintain proper documentation of contracts, procurement files, assets, and inventory.
  • Manage office administration, logistics, and asset management at the field office.

Coordination & Reporting

  • Coordinate closely with Program Team, Palikas, partners, and external evaluators on financial and administrative matters.
  • Support preparation of donor financial reports, SWC reports, and project closure documents.
  • Provide timely financial information to management for decision-making.

Capacity Building & Team Support

  • Provide guidance and on-the-job support to program staff on financial documentation, advance settlement, and compliance.
  • Strengthen financial discipline and documentation practices at field and community levels.

Required Qualifications & Experience

  • Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Accounting, Management, or related field (Master’s degree preferred).
  • Minimum 5–7 years of progressive experience in finance and administration within NGOs/INGOs.
  • Strong experience managing donor-funded projects (bilateral, multilateral, or faith-based donors).
  • Proven experience in SWC reporting, audits, and project financial closure.
  • Strong command of Excel and accounting software; Nepali typing skills preferred.
  • Demonstrated ability to work independently in field settings under time pressure.

Core Competencies

  • High integrity, confidentiality, and accountability
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
  • Excellent coordination and communication skills
  • Ability to work with local governments and diverse stakeholders
  • Results-oriented with attention to detail

Employment Conditions

  • This position is subject to donor approval.
  • Contract duration will be aligned with CRP Phase IV (2026–2028) and renewed annually based on performance and funding.
  • Salary and benefits will be as per CDM-Nepal’s HR policy and candidate’s experience.

Equal Opportunity Statement

CDM-Nepal is an equal opportunity employer. Qualified women, individuals from marginalized communities, and local candidates from the project area are strongly encouraged to apply.

Application Process

Interested candidates are requested to submit:

  • Cover letter explaining suitability for the position

Being established in 1990, Nepal Federation of Indigenous Nationalities (NEFIN) is the one and only umbrella federation of Organizations of enlisted Indigenous Peoples of Nepal; a legally recognized organization registered under “Organizations Registration Act, 2034” of Nepal.

NEFIN truly represents Nepal’s indigenous peoples who constitute 35% of total country population (Census 2021). From the day one of its establishment, NEFIN has been working for the protection of rights of Nepal’s indigenous peoples over their ancestral domain, traditional lands, territories and natural resources as well as their cultural heritages, history, language, scripts, culture, traditions and identity. It has played a historical role in establishment of federalism, secularism and proportionate representation in Nepal.

In collaboration with its international collaborators, NEFIN is planning to initiate interventions on mapping of ancestral domains, traditional lands, territories and natural resources under the communal use of indigenous peoples of Baglung, Okhaldhunga (Rolpa, Solukhumbu and Dhankuta) districts of Nepal.

Job Title: Admin and Finance Officer

Duty Station: DBI Office, Kathmandu

Reports To: Program Director

Staff Reporting: Administrative Assistant, Office Assistant

Background:

Digo Bikas Institute (DBI) is a research and advocacy organization committed to promote ecological sustainability and social equity at policy and community level. Based in Kathmandu, DBI believes that Nepal (and the rest of the world) can develop meaningfully by identifying and applying alternative ways of meeting human needs without harming the nature and fellow human beings.

Vision
Digo Bikas Institute envisions an ecologically sound, socially just and prosperous society, and that it will continue to be so for future generations.

Mission
Digo Bikas Institute’s mission is to undertake research and action to stimulate informed discussion and strategic thought to advance alternative and local solutions to global problems.

Job Purpose:

This position will be overall responsible to perform the overall financial related tasks and provide support and supervision to administrative and human resources functions in the DBI Office and support area to ensure that the timely information and updates are available as required by Senior Management Team in Kathmandu and other funding partners.

Key Responsibilities:

Responsibility Area 1: Finance:

  • Oversee the financial operations of Kathmandu Office and support areas to ensure timely and accurate financial reports and practices including fund management, payroll, financial disbursements, ledgers etc.
  • Preparing the vouchers of all the transactions and entering them into FAMAS Accounting Package in the concerned books of account.
  • Collect and produce period reports from all support areas and timely submission of monthly report along with the fund request of all projects to Senior Management Team and concerned funding parters complying with prevailing rules and regulation of Government, policies of the organization as well as funding partners.
  • Verify and review of financial data, supporting documents, accounting and financial reports of the each projects and recommend and implement measure to ensure that financial reports are being generated accurately and timely for the purpose of reporting different stakeholders.
  • Coordinate with the organization’s internal auditor, statutory auditor and donor auditors to conduct organization audit and project audit.
  • Discuss of the findings of audit with Finance Head and Management Head in advance of finalizing audit report and incorporate audit comments.
  • Release monthly/quarterly budget to all districts as per approved DIP.
  • Analysis of expenses and payment to suppliers, Insurance Companies etc.
  • Timely deposit of TDS, PF and CIT.
  • Verify and review the transaction vouchers and supporting documents of support areas.
  • Preparation of Monthly Bank Reconciliation Statement.

Responsibility Area 2: Human Resource, Administration & Logistics (Supervisory Role)

  • Ensure that the office equipments and other institutional properties are well functioning and are safeguarded at all times.
  • Ensure the personal files are updated with all the required documents.
  • Ensure timely submission of the following reports to Senior Management Team, Funding Partners, and Support Areas
  • Attendance record of all the staffs along with the leave records and other substantiating documents.
  • Staff related document to update the personal files including the monthly time sheets.
  • Ensure that vehicles logbooks are kept accurately and up to date.
  • Ensure that the organizational properties are solely used for official purposes with proper documentation.

Responsibility Area 3: Procurement and Store Management

  • Assist Admin Officer in procurement process (procure required goods/materials as per organization and funding partner’s procurement policies, procedures and standard. of the organization ensuring their quality and cost effectiveness) and ensure the proper documentation of the procurement process.
  • Ensure safeguarding of assets and verify that assets are in existence and being used properly.
  • Ensure that logistic, procurement and store management has been done effectively following the organizational policy.

Responsibility Area 4: Program Implementation

  • Develop project budget in consultation with program team and management as per requirement.
  • Support in all support areas to ensure the project implementation based on the budget plan and update its expenses periodically to the Senior Management Team/Project Coordinators.
  • Ensure activities and expenditures claimed by field staffs are actual and eligible as per project documents.
  • Support program team for effective, efficiency and economically budget utilization to demonstrate the result of the concerned project.

Responsibility Area 5: Monitoring, documentation, and reporting

  • Regularly monitor and review the field activities in each support area to ensure that activities are in line with achieving expected outputs and booked expenses complying all requirements and policy.
  • Monitor ongoing levels of expenditure on individual project outputs as budgeted and provide timely advice of likely over and under spending budget.
  • Ensure systematic documentation to prepare and submit periodic (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual and annual) financial, management and progress reports to concerned line managers as per requirements.
  • Share promptly if found irregularity, laps, fraud, and deviation with evidence after analyzing the finance documents.

Responsibility Area 6: Other Tasks

  • Other responsibilities as assigned by Line Manager and Reporting Manager.

Qualifications and Key Competencies:

  • Bachelor’s Degree in Business Administration/Business Studies with at least 2 year experience in Finance and Administration in I/NGOs.
  • Good understanding of current accounting standards, control issues/procedures, government laws and regulations and financial system of INGO/NGO.
  • Good communication, problem solving and teambuilding skills
  • Knowledge of purchasing, store management, logistic and administrative works
  • Capable of handling all types of financial logistic and administrative works. .
  • Computer skills including use of spreadsheet and electronic mail.
  • Knowledge of FAMAS (Accounting Software) will be an advantage.
  • Willingness and commitment to stay and work in remote areas of the support areas.

Interested candidates are requested to submit their application along with expected salary to hr@digobikas.org with the Title “Admin and Finance Officer 2026” along with the following documents by 12th January 2026, before 5:00 PM NST.

DOCUMENTS TO BE SUBMITTED

  • Cover letter
  • CV

Only short-listed candidates will receive information for further selection process. An attempt to influence at any stage of the selection process will negate the cause of the candidate. DBI reserves the right to accept or reject all or any of the application.
